proposal.utterance: God is a being that is absolutely infinite, consisting of infinite attributes each expressing eternal infinite essence.

entities.label: God
entities.rationale: God is presented as a singular, proper-named being — hence an individual. The utterance does not clearly place God in the material realm (no mass or spatial extent asserted), nor in any dependent or occurrent category. 'Independent continuant' is the most defensible BFO anchor for a self-subsisting entity whose existence does not depend on or inhere in another. Assigning BFO_0000040 (Material entity) would over-commit; BFO_0000004 is the broadest independent continuant and leaves room for further refinement.

entities.label: DivinAttribute
entities.rationale: The utterance speaks of 'infinite attributes each expressing eternal infinite essence'. Attributes that characterise a bearer map most naturally to BFO Quality (a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in exactly one bearer and expresses a property of that bearer). Modelled as a class because the utterance speaks of multiple such attributes generically.

entities.label: AbsoluteInfinity
entities.rationale: The utterance singles out 'absolutely infinite' as a specific characterisation of God as a whole (distinct from the individual infinite attributes). This overall absolute infinity is modelled as a specific quality individual inhering in the individual God.

entities.label: EternalInfiniteEssence
entities.rationale: An 'essence' as expressed by attributes reads as an informational or structural pattern that can be multiply instantiated or expressed — fitting BFO Generically dependent continuant. Each attribute expresses (is a vehicle for) an instance of this essence-class.

relations.rationale: The quality AbsoluteInfinity inheres in the individual God, per BFO's inheres-in relation for specifically dependent continuants.

The utterance says God 'consists of infinite attributes', suggesting a has-part relation from God to instances of DivineAttribute. Using BFO has-part (BFO_0000051) with the class as a placeholder pending instantiation of specific attributes.
DivineAttribute is a subclass of BFO Quality, as established in the entity entry.
EternalInfiniteEssence is a subclass of BFO Generically dependent continuant.

open_questions: BFO_0000004 (Independent continuant) is used for God, but God is not explicitly material. Should God be typed as a Material entity (BFO_0000040) if the discourse commits to God having some form of physical existence, or left at the broader Independent continuant?

The utterance implies infinitely many attributes. Should each major attribute (e.g., Thought, Extension in Spinoza's system) be modelled as separate named individuals of class DivineAttribute, or is the generic class sufficient for now?

Is 'essence' here intended as a generically dependent continuant (a pattern that can be expressed in multiple bearers), or as a quality of God specifically? The answer affects whether EternalInfiniteEssence should be BFO_0000031 or BFO_0000019.

Does 'eternal' commit to a specific temporal modelling (e.g., God existing across all temporal regions, or outside time entirely)? BFO's temporal regions may need to be invoked or explicitly excluded.

Is this utterance intended as a theological axiom (treated as a commitment of the ontology) or as a reported definition (e.g., Spinoza's Ethics, Definition VI)? The epistemic status affects how assertions should be scoped.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance is a theological definition of God as an absolutely infinite being constituted by infinitely many attributes, each expressing an eternal infinite essence. Under BFO 2020, God is most conservatively typed as an individual independent continuant (BFO_0000004), since the text asserts self-subsistent existence without clear material or dependent character. The 'attributes' are modelled as a class of qualities (BFO_0000019) that inhere in God, with absolute infinity as a named quality individual. The 'eternal infinite essence' expressed by each attribute is modelled as a generically dependent continuant class (BFO_0000031), because essences function as patterns or informational structures that can be expressed or instantiated. Several open questions remain: the exact BFO typing of God, whether individual attributes should be named, whether essence is generic or specifically dependent, how eternity maps onto BFO temporal regions, and whether this is an asserted axiom or a cited definition.

proposal.utterance: Substance is that which is in itself and is conceived through itself, not requiring conception of another thing.

entities.label: Substance
entities.rationale: Spinoza's Substance is defined as that which exists in itself and is conceived through itself, with no dependence on any other thing for its existence or conception. This maps most naturally to BFO Independent Continuant: an entity that does not inhere in or depend on another entity. It is modeled as a class rather than an individual because the utterance is a definitional assertion about what Substance is as a kind, even though Spinoza ultimately holds there is only one substance (God/Nature). The individual God already exists in the ontology and may later be typed as an instance of this class.

entities.label: SelfConceivability
entities.rationale: The property of being conceivable through itself (not requiring conception of another thing) is an internally grounded capacity or disposition intrinsic to Substance. BFO Disposition is appropriate because it is grounded in the intrinsic nature of the bearer, not in external relations. This models the 'conceived through itself' clause of the definition.

relations.rationale: Substance is defined as existing in itself with no dependence on another, making it a subclass of BFO Independent Continuant.
SelfConceivability is an intrinsically grounded disposition of Substance, subclass of BFO Disposition.

Every instance of Substance bears an instance of SelfConceivability. This captures the definitional clause that Substance is conceived through itself. (OWL restriction: bearerOf some SelfConceivability — flagged as open question for reasoner encoding.)

open_questions: Should the individual 'God' be asserted as an instance (rdf:type) of working:Substance, given Spinoza's identification of God with the one infinite Substance?
Should working:Substance be constrained as a singleton class (exactly one instance) to reflect Spinoza's monism, or left open for now?

The relation 'bearer of SelfConceivability' ideally requires an OWL SubClassOf restriction (RO_0000053 some working:SelfConceivability). Shall we encode this as a formal OWL restriction or keep it as a named relation assertion pending reasoner support?

Should working:EternalInfiniteEssence (existing GDC) be related to Substance — e.g., Substance has part or is characterized by its EternalInfiniteEssence? Spinoza defines Substance partly through its infinite attributes.

Is 'conceived through itself' an epistemic/cognitive property or a metaphysical one? This affects whether SelfConceivability is better modeled as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) or a Quality (BFO_0000019).
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance is Spinoza's definition of Substance (Ethics, Part I, Definition 3). Ontologically, Substance is defined by two conjoint properties: existing in itself (in se esse) and being conceived through itself (per se concipi). The first property maps to BFO Independent Continuant — an entity whose existence does not depend on inhering in another. The second property — self-conceivability — is modeled as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) because it is intrinsically grounded in the nature of the bearer rather than externally assigned. Substance is minted as a class (subclass of BFO_0000004) since the utterance is definitional. The existing individual 'God' is a candidate instance of this class but that identification is left as an open question. The third relation involving an OWL existential restriction is flagged because anonymous blank nodes cannot be cleanly expressed in this triple-based format and will require explicit OWL encoding.

proposal.utterance: A mode is an affection of substance, or that which exists in something else and is conceived through that thing.

entities.label: Mode
entities.rationale: A mode, in Spinoza's sense, is an affection of substance — something that exists in something else (substance) and is conceived through it. This maps well to BFO's specifically dependent continuant, which inheres in exactly one bearer and cannot exist independently. The bearer here is an instance of Substance. Mode is a common noun denoting a kind, so it is a class.

entities.label: ModeInstance
entities.rationale: Placeholder subclass to allow future individuals instantiating Mode to be typed; not strictly required now but noted as optional. Omit if unnecessary.

relations.rationale: Mode is a kind of specifically dependent continuant because it inheres in and is conceived through substance, matching BFO's definition of SDC as something that depends on and inheres in a bearer.

Every mode inheres in some instance of Substance. This is expressed as an OWL restriction: Mode subClassOf (RO_0000052 some working:Substance). Captures the Spinozist definition that a mode exists in and is conceived through substance.

open_questions: Should Mode be typed as BFO Quality (BFO_0000019) rather than generically as SDC (BFO_0000020)? Spinoza treats modes as modifications/affections, which could be quality-like (e.g., a specific shape or motion), but some modes may be more process-like. Do you want Mode to be a subclass of Quality specifically, or remain the broader SDC?
The second entity 'ModeInstance' was included only as a placeholder and is not needed if you do not plan to assert mode individuals now — should it be dropped?
Spinoza distinguishes infinite modes (e.g., motion-and-rest) from finite modes (e.g., a particular body). Should we mint subclasses FiniteMode and InfiniteMode now, or defer?
proposal.rationale_summary: Spinoza's 'mode' is defined as an affection of substance — something that exists in another thing (substance) and is conceived through it. This is paradigmatically a specifically dependent continuant (BFO_0000020) in BFO terms, since SDCs inhere in exactly one bearer and cannot exist independently of that bearer. The bearer class is the already-minted working:Substance. A single new class, working:Mode, is proposed as a subclass of BFO_0000020, with an OWL restriction expressing that every mode inheres in (RO_0000052 some working:Substance). The second 'ModeInstance' entity is vestigial and should likely be dropped. Open questions flag whether a narrower BFO type (Quality) is more appropriate and whether Spinoza's infinite/finite mode distinction warrants further subclassing.

proposal.utterance: A thing is finite when it can be determined by another thing of the same nature.

entities.label: Finitude
entities.rationale: Finitude is a measurable, determinate property that inheres in a thing — a quality in BFO terms. It captures the Spinozistic sense that a thing is limited or bounded, which is a quality of that thing.

entities.label: FiniteThingRole
entities.rationale: The status of being 'finite' in Spinoza's sense is relationally grounded — it is determined by another thing of the same nature. This external grounding (dependence on another entity of the same kind for its limit) fits BFO's Role rather than a purely intrinsic Quality. However, since the utterance also supports a purely qualitative reading, Finitude as Quality is preferred; FiniteThingRole is offered as an alternative.

entities.label: DeterminingRelation
entities.rationale: The act by which one thing 'determines' (limits, bounds) another thing of the same nature is a process — a happening in which two participants of the same kind are involved.

entities.label: SameNatureConstraint
entities.rationale: The condition 'of the same nature' denotes an internally grounded capacity or constraint intrinsic to the kind of thing — that only things sharing the same nature can serve as determinants for each other. This fits BFO Disposition.

relations.rationale: Finitude is a subclass of BFO Quality, as it is a property inhering in an independent continuant (the finite thing).
FiniteThingRole is a subclass of BFO Role, capturing the relationally grounded status of being finite.
DeterminingRelation is a subclass of BFO Process, the happening in which one thing limits another of the same nature.
SameNatureConstraint is a subclass of BFO Disposition, encoding the requirement that only things of the same nature can determine each other.
As a Quality, Finitude is also a Specifically Dependent Continuant (BFO_0000020), inheriting that classification.

open_questions: Should 'Finitude' be modeled primarily as a Quality (intrinsic property of a bounded thing) or as a Role (relationally grounded status dependent on the existence of a determining thing of the same nature)? The utterance's relational definition ('determined by another thing of the same nature') hints at a role, but qualities can also be relationally defined.
What is the ontological type of the 'thing' that can be finite — should it be typed as working:Substance (already in ontology), or is finitude applicable to working:Mode instances as well?

Should 'DeterminingRelation' be modeled as a BFO Process or as an object property / relation between individuals? BFO prefers relations as processes only if they have temporal extent; otherwise a bare object property may suffice.
Does 'same nature' in Spinoza mean 'same Attribute' (e.g., both extended, or both thinking)? If so, should SameNatureConstraint be tied to working:DivineAttribute?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance introduces Spinoza's definition of finitude (Ethics, Part I, Definition 2): a thing is finite when it can be limited by another thing of the same nature. This commits us ontologically to (1) a property of being-finite (best typed as a BFO Quality, class Finitude), (2) a relational grounding condition — that the determiner must share the same nature — which fits a BFO Disposition (SameNatureConstraint) inhering in the finite thing's kind, (3) the act of determination as a BFO Process (DeterminingRelation), and optionally (4) a BFO Role (FiniteThingRole) for the relational reading of finitude. AbsoluteInfinity already in the ontology serves as the complementary individual for which finitude does not apply. The existing working:Substance class is the likely bearer class for Finitude instances, but Modes may also be finite, so that question is flagged. No existing individuals are directly typed as finite here; only classes and structural relations are asserted.

proposal.utterance: A cause of itself is something whose essence involves its existence or whose nature necessarily contains existence.

entities.label: CausaSui
entities.rationale: Causa sui (cause of itself) is the disposition or internally-grounded capacity of a thing whose essence necessarily involves its own existence. It is internally grounded in the bearer (not externally conferred), making Disposition the best BFO fit. It is a class because the utterance defines a kind, not a particular instance.

entities.label: ExistenceNecessitation
entities.rationale: The property of necessarily containing existence within one's nature is itself a disposition — an internally grounded capacity that, when realized, manifests as the entity's actual existence. This captures the 'nature necessarily contains existence' clause of the definition.

entities.label: EssentialExistenceQuality
entities.rationale: The fact that a thing's essence *involves* existence is a quality inhering in that thing — it is a measurable/characterisable property of its essence, distinct from the dispositional aspect captured by ExistenceNecessitation.

relations.rationale: CausaSui is a subclass of Disposition, as it is an internally grounded capacity whose realization is the entity's own existence.
ExistenceNecessitation is the specific dispositional ground — the 'nature necessarily contains existence' — that constitutes the causa sui disposition; it is a subtype of CausaSui.
The involvement of existence in an essence is a DivineAttribute (already in ontology as a Quality subclass), and EssentialExistenceQuality is a more specific such attribute.

God (existing individual of type BFO_0000004) is the paradigm bearer of the CausaSui disposition per Spinoza's definition; asserting this now instantiates an instance of CausaSui borne by God. Note: HermiT will need this typed as an instance-level triple — the individual God bears an instance of class CausaSui.

open_questions: Should CausaSui be modeled as a subclass of the existing SelfConceivability (Disposition) class, since self-conceivability and cause-of-itself are closely related in Spinoza's system (Ethics I, Def. 1 vs. Def. 3)?

Is ExistenceNecessitation intended as a strictly distinct disposition from CausaSui, or should it be collapsed into CausaSui as a single disposition with two equivalent characterizations (essence-involves-existence vs. nature-necessarily-contains-existence)?

Should EssentialExistenceQuality be typed under DivineAttribute only, or also under EternalInfiniteEssence (GDC), since Spinoza treats the essence-existence identity as part of the content of the infinite substance's essence?

Do you want to assert that the CausaSui disposition, when realized, produces a process (e.g., a SelfGroundingProcess : BFO_0000015) that is its realization, to capture the dynamic implication of necessary existence?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance is Spinoza's definition of 'causa sui' (Ethics Part I, Definition 1): a thing is a cause of itself if its essence involves its existence, equivalently if its nature necessarily contains existence. This is primarily ontological definitional content. I model CausaSui as a Disposition class (BFO_0000016) because the property is internally grounded in the bearer's own nature — not externally conferred — and because its 'realization' is just the entity's own continued existence. ExistenceNecessitation is modeled as a subclass of CausaSui capturing the modal-necessity reading, while EssentialExistenceQuality (Quality, BFO_0000019) captures the essence-characterization reading. EssentialExistenceQuality is placed under the existing DivineAttribute class. God is asserted as a bearer of CausaSui. The existing SelfConceivability class is related but distinct (Def. 3 vs. Def. 1 in Spinoza), so I leave a question about whether to merge or link them.

proposal.utterance: The intellect has the power to form clear and distinct ideas.

entities.label: Intellect
entities.rationale: The intellect, in Spinoza's framework, is a thing that persists and acts as a bearer of capacities. Modeled as a class of independent continuant since individual intellects are instances of it. In Spinoza, intellect (intellectus) can be finite (human) or infinite (divine); we mint the class and let individuals be typed under it.

entities.label: IdeaFormationCapacity
entities.rationale: The 'power to form clear and distinct ideas' is an internally grounded capacity (a disposition in BFO sense) inhering in the intellect. It is realized when the intellect actually forms such ideas. Disposition is the right BFO type rather than Role (which is externally grounded).

entities.label: ClearAndDistinctIdea
entities.rationale: A 'clear and distinct idea' is an informational/representational entity in Spinoza's epistemology. It can be instantiated in multiple intellects and is the product/output of the idea-forming process. Generically dependent continuant captures its pattern-like, multiply-instantiable nature.

entities.label: IdeaFormationProcess
entities.rationale: The activity of forming ideas is an occurrent process in which the intellect participates and through which the IdeaFormationCapacity is realized.

relations.rationale: IdeaFormationCapacity is a subclass of Disposition (BFO_0000016), the BFO type for internally grounded realizable entities.
Intellect is a kind of independent continuant.

The power (disposition) to form clear and distinct ideas inheres in the intellect as its bearer — expressed as a class-level axiom: every instance of IdeaFormationCapacity inheres in some instance of Intellect.
The disposition to form ideas is realized in the process of idea formation.
The intellect participates in (is the agent of) the idea-formation process.
The process of idea formation has ClearAndDistinctIdea instances as its output participants.

open_questions: Should 'Intellect' here be treated as a finite intellect (a mode of the attribute of Thought), or does the utterance intend to cover both finite and infinite intellects? This affects whether Intellect should be modeled as a subclass of working:Mode (a specifically dependent continuant / mode) rather than an independent continuant.

Is 'clear and distinct idea' being used in the Cartesian sense or specifically in Spinoza's sense (adequate idea)? If the latter, should we rename this class 'AdequateIdea' to align with Spinoza's technical vocabulary in TheEthics?
Should IdeaFormationCapacity be related to the existing working:SelfConceivability (also a Disposition), or is it a distinct disposition?

In BFO terms, the intellect is typed as an independent continuant class (though an open question is raised about whether it should be a mode/SDC in Spinoza's system, where intellect is a mode of the attribute of Thought). The power is a Disposition (BFO_0000016) inhering in the intellect and realized in an IdeaFormationProcess. The clear and distinct idea is a generically dependent continuant — an informational/representational pattern that can be concretely instantiated in a particular intellect but is not itself material. Relations capture inherence, realization, and participation. All four entities are newly minted since none exist in the current working ontology.

proposal.utterance: The intellect is distinct from the imagination.

entities.label: Imagination
entities.rationale: In Spinoza's system, the imagination is a faculty (a capacity-bearing entity) parallel to the intellect, which already exists in the ontology as an independent continuant class. Imagination is a kind of cognitive faculty, distinct from but parallel to Intellect.

entities.label: DistinctnessQuality
entities.rationale: The claim of distinctness between intellect and imagination is a quality that can be used to assert their non-identity and ontological separation. This is a quality inhering in the relationship or in the kinds themselves as a distinguishing marker.

relations.rationale: Reaffirming that Intellect is typed as independent continuant (already in ontology, confirming consistency).
Imagination is a cognitive faculty, an independent continuant parallel to Intellect, but a distinct class.

open_questions: In Spinoza's system, is the imagination best modeled as a faculty (independent continuant like Intellect), or as a mode or disposition of the mind? The Ethics treats both intellect and imagination as cognitive faculties but they may differ in their ontological grounding.
Should we assert a disjointness axiom (owl:disjointWith) between working:Intellect and working:Imagination to formally capture their distinction?
Is the distinction being asserted here a claim about individual tokens (this intellect vs. this imagination) or about the kinds/classes in general?
Should DistinctnessQuality be instantiated as an individual inhering in Intellect, or modeled purely as a class-level disjointness constraint?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts that the intellect and imagination are ontologically distinct faculties. The intellect already exists in the working ontology as a class under BFO independent continuant. I propose adding Imagination as a parallel class under BFO_0000004, since in Spinoza's system both are cognitive faculties of the mind. To capture the distinctness claim formally, I propose a DistinctnessQuality class under BFO_0000019 (Quality), though the most rigorous formal encoding would be an owl:disjointWith axiom between the two classes—flagged as an open question since the reasoner would need to handle it. The DistinctnessQuality entity provides a hook for future annotation. The key open question is whether the disjointness should be encoded as an OWL axiom rather than (or in addition to) an instantiated quality.

proposal.utterance: Things feared have no intrinsic good or bad nature.

entities.label: FearObject
entities.rationale: A class for things that are feared; modeled as independent continuants since feared objects are bearers of qualities (or lack thereof). Spinoza's claim is about the intrinsic nature of such things.

entities.label: IntrinsicMoralValence
entities.rationale: A quality class representing intrinsic goodness or badness as a property of a thing. The utterance asserts that feared objects lack this quality intrinsically.

entities.label: AbsenceOfIntrinsicMoralValence
entities.rationale: A quality (or its absence) capturing that feared objects have no intrinsic good or bad nature. In BFO, absence of a quality is best represented as a distinct quality class or annotation rather than a negative existential; we mint this as a sub-quality capturing the Spinozistic claim.

entities.label: FearResponse
entities.rationale: The process of fearing; fear is a psychological/affective process that a subject undergoes toward an object. Spinoza treats affects (including fear) as processes or modes of the mind.

entities.label: FearRole
entities.rationale: The role of being a feared object is externally grounded (it depends on the fearing subject's affect, not on any intrinsic property of the object). This directly supports the ontological claim that the feared-object role is extrinsic.

relations.rationale: FearRole is a subclass of BFO Role, confirming its externally-grounded, extrinsic character.
Feared objects are independent continuants bearing the FearRole extrinsically.
AbsenceOfIntrinsicMoralValence is typed as a subclass of IntrinsicMoralValence to represent the specific quality-state (zero/null valence) asserted of FearObjects.

open_questions: Is this utterance from Spinoza's Ethics specifically (e.g. E3 or E4 on affects and good/evil)? If so, should we link this claim to TheEthics individual as its source?
Should 'FearObject' be restricted to material entities, or can immaterial things (e.g. ideas) also be feared? This affects whether FearObject is a subclass of BFO_0000040 or remains at BFO_0000004.

The utterance asserts a universal negative about intrinsic moral valence. Should we model this as an OWL axiom (e.g. FearObject disjointWith bearer-of some IntrinsicMoralValence), or merely as an annotation on the class?
Is 'fear' here Spinoza's affect 'metus/timor'? If so, should FearResponse be linked to an existing or new Affect class distinct from other passions?
Do you want to model 'good' and 'bad' as sibling subclasses of IntrinsicMoralValence, with the claim being that FearObjects bear neither?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance expresses a Spinozistic metaethical claim: objects of fear have no intrinsic moral valence (goodness or badness). In BFO terms, this is best captured by: (1) a class FearObject (independent continuant) whose feared status is grounded in an extrinsic FearRole (BFO Role) inhering due to another subject's affective process (FearResponse, a BFO Process), not in any intrinsic quality of the object itself; and (2) a quality class IntrinsicMoralValence with a subclass AbsenceOfIntrinsicMoralValence to represent the claim that feared things lack such a quality by nature. The FearRole being externally grounded (a BFO_0000023 Role) ontologically encodes the claim that being feared is relational and observer-dependent, not intrinsic — directly supporting the philosophical assertion. No existing individuals in the ontology are implicated, though the claim likely derives from TheEthics and could be annotated accordingly.

proposal.utterance: Wealth, honor, and sensual pleasure distract the mind from other goods.

entities.label: Wealth
entities.rationale: Wealth as a general kind is a pattern of information/value that can be instantiated across bearers; alternatively could be a quality or role, but as a social-ontological category of goods it fits GDC. Open to revision.

entities.label: Honor
entities.rationale: Honor is an externally grounded social role/status that inheres in a person based on others' recognition; Role is the best BFO fit.

entities.label: SensualPleasure
entities.rationale: Sensual pleasure is an experiential process that unfolds in time and involves a participant (the experiencer); BFO Process is appropriate.

entities.label: DistractingFromHigherGoods
entities.rationale: The distraction is a causal process in which the mind's attention is diverted away from higher goods; BFO Process captures this dynamic occurrence.

entities.label: HigherGoods
entities.rationale: Higher goods (the goods contrasted with wealth, honor, pleasure) are value-bearing informational/normative entities; GDC is a reasonable fit for such abstract normative content.

entities.label: Mind
entities.rationale: In Spinoza's framework, the mind (mens) is a mode of thought but also individuated as a thing; given existing Intellect and Imagination classes typed as BFO_0000004, Mind as an independent continuant is consistent.

entities.label: AttentiveCapacity
entities.rationale: The mind's capacity to attend to goods is an internally grounded disposition; Disposition captures this well. Distraction reduces or redirects this disposition.

relations.rationale: The distracting process has the Mind as participant (the entity being distracted).
Wealth participates in the distracting process as a distracting agent/cause.
Honor participates in the distracting process as a distracting agent/cause.
Sensual pleasure participates in the distracting process as a distracting agent/cause.
The Mind bears the AttentiveCapacity that is redirected during distraction.

open_questions: Should 'Mind' (mens) be modeled as a subclass of 'Mode' (already in working ontology as a specifically dependent continuant) rather than as an independent continuant, given Spinoza's view that mind is a mode of the attribute of Thought?
Should 'Wealth' be typed as a Role (BFO_0000023) rather than a GDC, since Spinoza treats it as an externally assigned social status rather than an intrinsic property?
Is 'Honor' better modeled as a Quality (BFO_0000019) reflecting social esteem, rather than a Role?

Should 'HigherGoods' be further specified? Spinoza in the TreatiseOnEmendationOfIntellect identifies the highest good as knowledge of union with Nature — should this be linked to existing individuals?

Should the distracting relation be modeled using a disposition (e.g., 'DistractingDisposition') that inheres in Wealth/Honor/Pleasure and is realized in the DistractingFromHigherGoods process, to capture that these things have the power to distract rather than always doing so?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance is a claim from Spinoza's Treatise on the Emendation of the Intellect (TIE/TEI) asserting that wealth, honor, and sensual pleasure are distractors that draw the mind away from higher goods. Four new classes are needed: Wealth, Honor, SensualPleasure (the three distractors), and HigherGoods (what they distract from). A process class DistractingFromHigherGoods captures the causal event. Mind is introduced as a participant class consistent with the existing Intellect and Imagination classes. An AttentiveCapacity disposition inhering in the Mind captures the faculty that is redirected. Several open questions concern whether Mind should be a Mode (Spinoza's metaphysics), whether Wealth and Honor are better typed as Role or Quality, and whether distracting power should be modeled as a disposition realized in the process.

proposal.utterance: Things ordinarily pursued for their own sakes hinder the preservation of being and cause destruction.

entities.label: OrdinaryPursuit
entities.rationale: Things ordinarily pursued for their own sake (wealth, honor, sensual pleasure as noted in prior context) are best captured as a generically dependent continuant class — they are goods-as-conceived, informationally individuated patterns of valuation. This generalizes over the specific goods already in the ontology.

entities.label: PreservationOfBeing
entities.rationale: The preservation of being (conatus-like self-maintenance) is an internally grounded capacity of an entity — a disposition to persist and maintain existence. This is distinct from EssentialExistenceQuality (which marks necessary existence) and CausaSui (self-causation); it is the ongoing striving to continue.

entities.label: HinderingOfPreservation
entities.rationale: The hindering of preservation of being is an occurrent process — a happening in which the pursuit of ordinary goods interferes with the disposition to persist.

entities.label: DestructionProcess
entities.rationale: Destruction is the terminal process that results from the hindrance of preservation of being — an occurrent in which an entity's continuance is ended.

relations.rationale: Wealth (already in ontology) is one of the things ordinarily pursued for its own sake.
Honor (already in ontology) is one of the things ordinarily pursued for its own sake.
SensualPleasure (already in ontology) is one of the things ordinarily pursued for its own sake.
Instances of OrdinaryPursuit participate in HinderingOfPreservation processes as the causal input — the ordinary pursuits are participants in the hindering process.

DestructionProcess is represented as having HinderingOfPreservation as a part, or alternatively the hindering leads to destruction; modeled here as part-of relation (HinderingOfPreservation has part DestructionProcess, i.e., destruction is the culminating sub-process).

open_questions: Should 'PreservationOfBeing' be modeled as a Disposition (BFO_0000016, internally grounded striving) or as a Quality (BFO_0000019, a static property of persisting)? The conatus reading favors Disposition; a more static reading might favor Quality.
Is the causal relation between OrdinaryPursuit and HinderingOfPreservation better expressed as a custom 'causes' object property, or is participation (RO_0000057) sufficient?
Should HinderingOfPreservation and DestructionProcess be kept as distinct process classes or collapsed into one (e.g., DestructionProcess with hindrance as a sub-process)?

The statement reads as a general philosophical claim (universally quantified). Should this be encoded as a class-level axiom (all instances of OrdinaryPursuit participate in some HinderingOfPreservation) rather than individual assertions?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts that things ordinarily pursued for their own sake — wealth, honor, sensual pleasure, which are already in the ontology — hinder the preservation of being and cause destruction. I introduce OrdinaryPursuit as a generically dependent continuant class that subsumes these existing goods-classes, PreservationOfBeing as a disposition (internally grounded striving of an entity to maintain itself, the Spinozistic conatus), HinderingOfPreservation as a process in which ordinary pursuits interfere with that disposition, and DestructionProcess as the terminal process that results. The existing Wealth, Honor, and SensualPleasure classes are typed as subclasses of OrdinaryPursuit. The DistractingFromHigherGoods process already in the ontology is closely related but distinct (it concerns distraction from higher goods rather than active destruction). I flag several open questions about the best BFO typing of PreservationOfBeing and how to represent the causal-consequential structure.

proposal.utterance: All happiness or unhappiness depends on the quality of the object loved.

entities.label: Happiness
entities.rationale: Happiness is a quality inhering in a mind/person — a positive affective state that can be measured along a valence dimension. BFO Quality fits.

entities.label: Unhappiness
entities.rationale: Unhappiness is the negative pole of the same affective quality dimension; modeled symmetrically as a Quality subclass.

entities.label: AffectiveValenceQuality
entities.rationale: Superclass for Happiness and Unhappiness, capturing the general dimension of affective valence that the proposition asserts is determined by the loved object.

entities.label: LovingRelation
entities.rationale: Love in Spinoza is an active affective process/striving toward an object, not a static quality. Modeling it as a Process allows participation by both lover and loved object.

entities.label: LovedObject
entities.rationale: Being 'the loved object' is an externally grounded role that any independent continuant can bear by participating in a LovingRelation.

entities.label: LoverRole
entities.rationale: The agent bearing love toward the object plays the Lover role; this role is the bearer of the resulting affective valence quality.

entities.label: ObjectQualityDeterminesAffect
entities.rationale: The core claim of the utterance is that a quality of the loved object (its nature/worth) has the capacity to determine the happiness or unhappiness of the lover. This is internally grounded in the object and so is a Disposition.

relations.rationale: Happiness is a positive instance of affective valence quality.
Unhappiness is a negative instance of affective valence quality.
AffectiveValenceQuality is a BFO Quality.
The LovingRelation process has a participant bearing the LoverRole.
The LovingRelation process has a participant bearing the LovedObject role.
The disposition of the loved object's quality to determine affect is realized in the LovingRelation process.
The happiness/unhappiness quality inheres in the bearer of the LoverRole (the loving mind/person).

open_questions: In Spinoza's TEI, the 'quality of the object' refers to whether the object is eternal/infinite vs. perishable/finite. Should we link LovedObject's quality explicitly to the existing EternalInfiniteEssence and Finitude classes?
Should LovingRelation be further sub-typed (e.g., LoveOfPerishableObject vs. LoveOfEternalObject) to capture the two cases Spinoza contrasts?
Is the AffectiveValenceQuality bearer the Mind individual already in the ontology, or should we introduce a generic Person/Agent class as bearer?

proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts a dependency relation between affective states (happiness/unhappiness) and a property of an object of love. In BFO terms: happiness and unhappiness are Qualities inhering in the lover (a mind/person); they are unified under a new superclass AffectiveValenceQuality. Love is modeled as a Process (LovingRelation) with two participant roles: LoverRole (bearer of the affective quality) and LovedObject (a Role borne by whatever entity is loved). The core explanatory claim — that the object's quality determines the lover's happiness — is captured as a Disposition (ObjectQualityDeterminesAffect) inhering in the loved object and realized in the LovingRelation process. This connects naturally to existing ontology nodes: LovedObject's quality could be linked to existing Finitude and EternalInfiniteEssence classes, and the claim originates in TreatiseOnEmendationOfIntellect (TEI). Several open questions are raised for the user about those further connections.

entities.label: Happiness

entities.label: Unhappiness

entities.label: AffectiveValenceQuality

entities.label: LovingRelation

entities.label: LovedObject

entities.label: ObjectQualityDeterminesAffect

proposal.utterance: Love toward the eternal and infinite thing produces joy exempt from sadness.

entities.label: LoveTowardEternalInfiniteThing
entities.rationale: Love toward the eternal and infinite thing is a disposition of a mind/agent that is internally grounded in the nature of the bearer and directed toward the eternal-infinite; it is a kind of orientation or conative-affective capacity.

entities.label: Joy
entities.rationale: Joy (laetitia in Spinoza) is an occurrent transition to a state of greater perfection — a process of increase in the power of acting. Modeled as a Process subclass.

entities.label: Sadness
entities.rationale: Sadness (tristitia) is a process of decrease in the power of acting; modeled symmetrically with Joy as a Process subclass.

entities.label: SadnessExemptionQuality
entities.rationale: The property of being exempt from (unmixed with) sadness is a quality inhering in a particular instance of Joy; it distinguishes this love-produced joy from ordinary mixed pleasures.

entities.label: LoveProducesJoyProcess
entities.rationale: The causal/productive process by which love toward the eternal and infinite thing gives rise to joy; needed to ground the production relation between the disposition and the affect.

relations.rationale: The disposition (love toward the eternal) is realized in the process of producing joy — BFO 'realized in' links a realizable entity to the process in which it is manifested.
The love-produces-joy process has Joy as a participant (the affect produced).
The sadness-exemption quality inheres in Joy instances produced by this love — joy of this kind bears the quality of being unmixed with sadness.
Explicit subclass assertion ensuring LoveTowardEternalInfiniteThing is typed under BFO Disposition.
Joy is a subclass of BFO Process.
Sadness is a subclass of BFO Process.
LoveProducesJoyProcess is a subclass of BFO Process.

open_questions: Should Joy and Sadness be modeled as Processes (transitions/events) or as Qualities (states inhering in a mind at a time)? Spinoza's definitions suggest dynamic transitions, but they are often treated as enduring affective states. The choice affects which BFO type is most faithful.

Should LoveTowardEternalInfiniteThing be a Disposition (internally grounded) or a Role (externally grounded)? Given that for Spinoza this love arises from the intellect's own adequate understanding, a Disposition seems appropriate, but the user may prefer a Role.

Is 'the eternal and infinite thing' here identical to the existing individual working:God (Deus sive Natura), or is it a distinct class reference? If it is God, we should link LoveTowardEternalInfiniteThing's bearer-range to working:God.
Should we assert that LoveProducesJoyProcess is disjoint from (or excludes) instances of working:Sadness, to formally capture 'exempt from sadness'?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance is Spinoza's Ethics V proposition-level claim (cf. Ethics IV App. and Ethics V P20-36 context) that love directed toward the eternal and infinite thing (God/Nature) produces a joy that is not mixed with sadness, unlike love toward finite, perishable objects. Ontologically, the claim commits us to: (1) a class of disposition (LoveTowardEternalInfiniteThing) inhering in minds; (2) a productive process (LoveProducesJoyProcess) in which that disposition is realized; (3) a class of process (Joy) that is produced; (4) a quality (SadnessExemptionQuality) inhering in that joy distinguishing it from ordinary mixed affects; and (5) a parallel class (Sadness) for contrast. Joy and Sadness are provisionally typed as BFO Processes following Spinoza's definition of affects as transitions in the power of acting, but this is flagged as an open question. The existing individual working:God and class working:EternalInfiniteEssence are relevant context but are not directly modified here.

proposal.utterance: Money, sensual pleasure, and esteem are obstacles only when sought for their own sakes.

entities.label: SoughtForOwnSakeRole
entities.rationale: The key ontological commitment here is that money, pleasure, and esteem become obstacles specifically when they are pursued as ends in themselves — i.e., when they bear the role of being sought for their own sake. This role is externally grounded (it depends on the agent's orientation toward the object) and is a subclass of BFO Role.

entities.label: ObstacleRole
entities.rationale: Being an obstacle to higher goods is a role that certain objects bear under certain conditions (when sought for their own sake). This is externally grounded and context-dependent, fitting BFO Role.

entities.label: Money
entities.rationale: Money as a medium of exchange and store of value is best treated as a generically dependent continuant — an information-like or socially constituted pattern that can be instantiated across substrates. Wealth already exists in the ontology as BFO_0000031; Money is more specific (the medium) and warrants its own class. Note: could also be Material entity (coins, notes); open question raised.

entities.label: Esteem
entities.rationale: Esteem (social standing, honor) is already partially captured by the existing 'Honor' class typed as BFO_0000023 (Role). Esteem is closely related; however, Spinoza distinguishes 'gloria'/'fama' (esteem/honor) as a social role conferred on persons. A new class Esteem is warranted as a subclass of Role, related to but distinct from Honor.

entities.label: SeekingForOwnSakeProcess
entities.rationale: The act of seeking something for its own sake is a process in which an agent participates and in which the SoughtForOwnSakeRole is realized. This process is what triggers the ObstacleRole being realized.

relations.rationale: ObstacleRole is a kind of Role in BFO.
SoughtForOwnSakeRole is a kind of Role in BFO.
Esteem is a subtype of the already-existing Honor role class; both concern social recognition conferred externally.
Money is a specific form of Wealth already in the ontology.

The ObstacleRole (with respect to HigherGoods) is also realized in the SeekingForOwnSakeProcess — it is precisely during/through this process that the obstacle character manifests.
Seeking money, pleasure, or esteem for their own sake is a subtype of the already-existing DistractingFromHigherGoods process class.

open_questions: Should 'Money' be typed as BFO_0000031 (generically dependent continuant, as a social/informational pattern) or BFO_0000040 (material entity, as coins/notes)? Spinoza's context suggests the social/representational sense, but clarification helps.
Should 'Esteem' be modeled as a subclass of the existing 'Honor' class, or as a sibling? Spinoza sometimes treats gloria (esteem) and honor differently.

The utterance implies a conditional: these things are obstacles *only when* sought for their own sake — should we encode this conditionality as an OWL restriction (e.g., SensualPleasure bears ObstacleRole only if it also bears SoughtForOwnSakeRole), or is noting the role classes sufficient for now?
Is 'SensualPleasure' (already in the ontology as a Process subclass) the correct reuse for the pleasure mentioned here, or does Spinoza mean something broader by 'voluptas'?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance encodes a conditional ontological claim from Spinoza's Treatise on the Emendation of the Intellect: money, sensual pleasure, and esteem are not intrinsically bad but become obstacles to higher goods only when pursued as ends in themselves. The key ontological move is to introduce (a) a SoughtForOwnSakeRole that attaches to objects when an agent orients toward them as final ends, and (b) an ObstacleRole that is realized in the same seeking process. SensualPleasure already exists in the ontology as a Process; Wealth already exists as a GDC; both are reused. Money is added as a subclass of Wealth. Esteem is added as a subclass of the existing Honor role. The conditionality — obstacle-hood only when sought for own sake — is captured by tying both roles to the SeekingForOwnSakeProcess, which is itself modeled as a subclass of the existing DistractingFromHigherGoods process.

proposal.utterance: Good and bad are predicates that apply to things only in a certain respect.

entities.label: GoodBadPredicate
entities.rationale: Good and bad as predicates that apply to things are qualities — specifically dependent continuants that inhere in bearers. They are relational or respect-relative qualities rather than intrinsic ones, but they remain qualities in the BFO sense.

entities.label: RespectOrRelationOfApplicability
entities.rationale: The 'certain respect' under which good or bad applies is itself a quality or contextual parameter of the bearer that conditions the applicability of the GoodBadPredicate. Modeled as a quality to capture the relational aspect.

entities.label: RelativeOrRespectalGoodness
entities.rationale: The capacity of a thing to be good or bad only under certain respects can be modeled as a disposition — internally grounded but only manifested under specific conditions. This captures the conditionality of the predication.

relations.rationale: Good and bad as predicates are qualities inhering in bearers.
The conditionally-realized nature of goodness/badness is a disposition that is only realized under certain respects.

GoodBadPredicate is a more specific subclass of IntrinsicMoralValence — but note the utterance asserts these are NOT intrinsic but respect-relative, so this subclass relation may need to be inverted or re-examined. See open_questions.

open_questions: The utterance asserts good and bad apply only 'in a certain respect,' which strongly contrasts with existing class 'AbsenceOfIntrinsicMoralValence' (already in the ontology as a subclass of IntrinsicMoralValence). Should GoodBadPredicate be placed under AbsenceOfIntrinsicMoralValence rather than IntrinsicMoralValence, to mark that goodness/badness is never intrinsic?
Is this claim from Spinoza's Ethics specifically (e.g., Preface to Part IV), and should it be linked to TheEthics as its source?

Should 'RespectOrRelationOfApplicability' be modeled as a Role (BFO_0000023) rather than a Quality, since the 'respect' in which something is good or bad may be a relational/functional context rather than an intrinsic property of the bearer?

Does 'things' refer specifically to modes (finite things), or does it include Substance/God? If the latter cannot be called good or bad even in a respect, the scope of the bearer class needs constraining.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts that 'good' and 'bad' are not absolute or intrinsic properties of things but only apply relative to a certain respect or context. In BFO terms, good/bad are best modeled as a class of Quality (specifically dependent continuants inhering in bearers), but their conditional applicability suggests they are more properly disposition-like — only realized under certain conditions. I introduce GoodBadPredicate as a Quality class, RespectOrRelationOfApplicability as the contextual Quality that conditions applicability, and RelativeOrRespectalGoodness as a Disposition capturing the conditional nature of the predication. The existing AbsenceOfIntrinsicMoralValence class is highly relevant here and may be the right parent for GoodBadPredicate, but I flag this as an open question because placing it under IntrinsicMoralValence (even as a subclass) risks implying intrinsicness. The relation to TheEthics (Part IV) as the philosophical source is also flagged.

proposal.utterance: Perfect and imperfect are not intrinsic properties considered in a thing's own nature.

entities.label: PerfectionQuality
entities.rationale: Perfection as a quality that can be attributed to a thing; needed to represent the claim that it is not intrinsic.

entities.label: ImperfectionQuality
entities.rationale: Imperfection as a quality; paired with PerfectionQuality to represent the claim that neither is intrinsic to a thing's own nature.

entities.label: RelationalQuality
entities.rationale: A quality that is grounded in comparison to or relation with something external rather than in the intrinsic nature of the bearer alone. Perfection and imperfection are asserted to be relational qualities in Spinoza's sense.

relations.rationale: Perfection is a relational quality, not intrinsic to the thing's own nature, per the utterance.
Imperfection is likewise a relational quality, not intrinsic to the thing's own nature, per the utterance.
RelationalQuality is a subclass of BFO Quality; distinguishes qualities grounded in comparison from intrinsic qualities.

open_questions: Spinoza's claim in the Ethics is that 'perfect' and 'imperfect' are modes of thinking (ways we conceive things) rather than properties of things themselves. Should PerfectionQuality and ImperfectionQuality be modeled instead as generically dependent continuants (BFO_0000031, i.e., conceptual content) rather than as qualities inhering in bearers?
Should we introduce an explicit 'IntrinsicQuality' class to contrast with 'RelationalQuality', so we can assert a disjointness axiom between them?

The utterance does not specify the bearer of these qualities. Should perfection/imperfection be asserted to inhere in things relative to a comparison class or standard? If so, should we model the comparison standard as a separate entity?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts a Spinozistic thesis that 'perfect' and 'imperfect' are not intrinsic properties of a thing considered in its own nature but are instead relational or comparative notions. Ontologically this is captured by introducing PerfectionQuality and ImperfectionQuality as subclasses of a new RelationalQuality class (itself a subclass of BFO Quality, BFO_0000019), where RelationalQuality denotes qualities that are grounded in external comparison rather than in the intrinsic constitution of the bearer. This contrasts with qualities like Finitude or EssentialExistenceQuality already in the graph, which are treated as intrinsic. There is a genuine open question about whether, following Spinoza more closely, these 'qualities' should instead be modeled as generically dependent continuants (conceptual modes of thinking) rather than as inhering qualities, and the user should clarify this before committing.

proposal.utterance: Everything that happens occurs according to the eternal order and certain laws of nature.

entities.label: EternalOrder
entities.rationale: The eternal order of nature is an informational/structural pattern — a set of laws or principles that can be instantiated across events — best typed as a generically dependent continuant (like a law or rule whose content can be multiply instantiated).

entities.label: LawOfNature
entities.rationale: Laws of nature in Spinoza are necessary, deterministic regularities governing all occurrents. They are best typed as generically dependent continuants — pattern-like informational entities that are concretely manifested in the dispositions of things.

entities.label: NaturalDetermination
entities.rationale: The necessity by which everything follows from eternal laws is an internally grounded disposition — a capacity/tendency of nature's substance to produce determinate effects. This captures Spinoza's necessitarianism as a disposition inhering in substance.

entities.label: EventOccurrence
entities.rationale: Whatever happens is an occurrence, a process unfolding in time. This class collects all processes that are governed by the eternal order and laws of nature.

entities.label: EternalLawGovernanceRelation
entities.rationale: The governance of all events by eternal laws can be modeled as a process (or type of process) by which natural determination is realized in occurrences — i.e., the realization of NaturalDetermination in EventOccurrence instances.

relations.rationale: Laws of nature are the specific, certain rules that constitute the eternal order; each law of nature is part of the eternal order.
NaturalDetermination is a disposition inhering in substance by which all events are necessitated.
The disposition (NaturalDetermination) is realized in the governance process (EternalLawGovernanceRelation) whenever any event occurs according to eternal laws.
Inverse of BFO_0000054: the governance process realizes the disposition of natural determination.
All happenings are processes (occurrents unfolding in time).
The governance process has EventOccurrence instances as participants — each governed event participates in the law-governance relation.
The disposition of natural determination inheres in Substance (the single infinite substance in Spinoza's metaphysics whose nature necessitates all events).

open_questions: Should 'EternalOrder' be an individual (there is exactly one eternal order) rather than a class? If so, we could mint working:TheEternalOrder as an individual of type working:EternalOrder.

Should 'LawOfNature' be typed as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) rather than a GDC, given that laws may be better understood as internally grounded tendencies of nature rather than information artifacts? Spinoza's laws are arguably not separable content but necessary expressions of substance's nature.

Is 'NaturalDetermination' meant to be a single universal disposition of Substance (one individual) or a class of dispositions each corresponding to a specific law? The utterance suggests universality.
Does 'eternal' here imply that these laws/order are outside BFO temporal regions (i.e., they hold for all temporal regions)? This may require an annotation rather than a structural BFO assertion.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts Spinoza's thoroughgoing necessitarianism: every event (process/occurrence) is governed by the eternal order and certain laws of nature. I mint four new classes: EternalOrder (GDC — the overarching structural pattern of necessity), LawOfNature (GDC — the specific certain laws, subclass of EternalOrder), NaturalDetermination (Disposition — the internally grounded capacity of Substance by which all events are necessitated), and EventOccurrence (Process — the class of all happenings). I also mint EternalLawGovernanceRelation (Process) to represent the realization of NaturalDetermination in concrete occurrences. Key relations assert that NaturalDetermination inheres in working:Substance, is realized in EternalLawGovernanceRelation, which in turn has EventOccurrences as participants. Laws of nature are typed as subclass of EternalOrder. Several open questions remain about whether EternalOrder should be an individual and whether LawOfNature should be a Disposition rather than a GDC.

proposal.utterance: The true good consists of means to acquiring a human nature stronger and more enduring than one's current nature.

entities.label: TrueGood
entities.rationale: The true good is a normative/evaluative concept — a content or standard that can be instantiated and understood across minds; modeled as a generically dependent continuant (like other 'goods' and 'higher goods' in this ontology). It is distinct from working:HigherGoods which is already present but this is a specific Spinozistic technical notion warranting its own class.

entities.label: StrongerHumanNature
entities.rationale: A stronger and more enduring human nature is an internally grounded capacity or power of the human being — a disposition inhering in a person. It is the target state whose acquisition the true good enables. Modeled as a subclass of Disposition (BFO_0000016).

entities.label: AcquisitionOfStrongerNatureProcess
entities.rationale: The acquiring or attaining of a stronger human nature is a process — an unfolding event in which a person comes to instantiate StrongerHumanNature. The true good serves as means to this process.

entities.label: MeansToAcquisitionRole
entities.rationale: The true good is defined relationally as the means to the acquisition of a stronger nature. This relational, externally grounded function is best modeled as a Role that TrueGood instances bear with respect to AcquisitionOfStrongerNatureProcess.

relations.rationale: The true good is a species of higher goods already present in the ontology; it is that which directs toward a stronger, more enduring nature rather than distracting from it.
The MeansToAcquisitionRole is realized in the process of acquiring a stronger human nature — standard BFO pattern for roles realized in processes.
The disposition StrongerHumanNature is realized (expressed, actualized) through the acquisition process — the process is the unfolding of that capacity coming to be.
Explicit BFO typing for TrueGood as generically dependent continuant.

open_questions: Should 'TrueGood' be treated as a Spinozistic individual concept (a single normative standard) rather than a class, given that Spinoza seems to speak of it as a unique target? If so, it would be an individual of type BFO_0000031.

Is 'stronger and more enduring human nature' best captured as a Disposition (internally grounded capacity) or as a Quality (a measurable property of the human being)? The endurance aspect might favor Quality; the power/striving aspect favors Disposition.
Should this 'true good' be connected to working:PreservationOfBeing (conatus) as its metaphysical ground, since a stronger nature better preserves one's being?
proposal.rationale_summary: Spinoza's claim in the Treatise on the Emendation of the Intellect (and echoed in the Ethics) is that the true good is not wealth, honor, or sensual pleasure but rather that which enables one to acquire a stronger and more enduring human nature. I model TrueGood as a class under the existing working:HigherGoods (itself a BFO_0000031 generically dependent continuant), since it is a normative content-pattern. The target — a stronger human nature — is a Disposition (BFO_0000016) because it is an internally grounded power or capacity inhering in the person. The becoming or attainment of that nature is a Process (AcquisitionOfStrongerNatureProcess). The definitional relation 'means to' is captured as a Role (MeansToAcquisitionRole) that instances of TrueGood bear, realized in the acquisition process. Relations to existing nodes PreservationOfBeing and HigherGoods are proposed but left partly open for user confirmation.

proposal.utterance: The highest human perfection is knowledge of the union of the mind with the whole of nature.

entities.label: HighestHumanPerfection
entities.rationale: The highest human perfection is a quality or state that can be borne by a human being; it is a specifically dependent continuant (quality) inhering in the person who achieves it.

entities.label: KnowledgeOfUnionWithNature
entities.rationale: Knowledge of the union of mind with the whole of nature is an informational/representational content — a generically dependent continuant that can be instantiated in different minds. It is closely related to ClearAndDistinctIdea already in the ontology but is a distinct, named kind of knowledge content.

entities.label: WholeOfNature
entities.rationale: In Spinoza's system, the whole of nature (Natura naturata + Natura naturans, i.e. the totality of substance and its modes) is the single all-encompassing independent continuant. It is best represented as an individual because Spinoza treats it as a unique totality, akin to God/Substance.

entities.label: UnionOfMindWithNature
entities.rationale: The union of the mind with the whole of nature is a disposition or capacity grounded in the nature of mind — it is the basis for the highest perfection and is internally grounded in the bearer (the mind), making it a disposition rather than a role.

entities.label: AchievementOfHighestPerfection
entities.rationale: The realization of the highest human perfection through knowing the union of mind with nature is an occurrent process — the process by which this disposition is realized.

relations.rationale: Knowledge of the union of mind with nature is a higher good in Spinoza's hierarchy — it is the supreme instance of HigherGoods already in the ontology.
HighestHumanPerfection is a quality inhering in a person.
The disposition of union-of-mind-with-nature is realized in the process of achieving the highest perfection.
Inverse: the process realizes the disposition.
In Spinoza, knowledge of the union of mind with nature is a species of clear and distinct idea — the highest such idea.
Reaffirming existing typing; Mind as independent continuant can bear the disposition UnionOfMindWithNature.

open_questions: Should 'WholeOfNature' be identified with the individual 'God' already in the ontology, given Spinoza's equation Deus sive Natura? If so, we can add an owl:sameAs or a note rather than a new individual.

Should 'HighestHumanPerfection' be modeled as a quality (BFO_0000019) inhering in individual humans, or as a disposition (BFO_0000016) that humans bear and that is realized in the achievement process? The utterance could support either reading.

Is 'KnowledgeOfUnionWithNature' best treated as a generically dependent continuant (a content that can be in many minds) or as a process of knowing (BFO_0000015)? The noun phrase 'knowledge' is ambiguous between a state and an act.
proposal.rationale_summary: Spinoza's claim that the highest human perfection consists in knowing the union of mind with the whole of nature introduces several ontological commitments. First, 'highest human perfection' is a quality borne by a human (BFO_0000019). Second, the content of that perfection — 'knowledge of the union of the mind with the whole of nature' — is a generically dependent continuant (BFO_0000031), a species of ClearAndDistinctIdea already in the ontology, and also the supreme HigherGood. Third, the 'union of mind with nature' that is the object of this knowledge is a disposition (BFO_0000016) internally grounded in the mind. Fourth, achieving this perfection is a process (BFO_0000015) that realizes the disposition. Finally, 'the whole of nature' is the totality of what exists — in Spinoza likely identical to God/Substance, raising the question of whether to identify it with the existing individual 'God' via Deus sive Natura.

proposal.utterance: It is part of the author's happiness that others understand as he understands.

entities.label: AuthorHappiness
entities.rationale: Happiness in Spinoza's sense is an active disposition or capacity for flourishing (beatitudo), not merely a passing feeling. Modeled as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) inhering in an agent.

entities.label: MutualUnderstanding
entities.rationale: The state of others understanding as the author understands is an occurrent process of shared intellectual apprehension.

entities.label: AuthorRole
entities.rationale: Reusing existing AuthorRole class.

entities.label: HappinessRealizationProcess
entities.rationale: The process by which the author's happiness disposition is realized, specifically through MutualUnderstanding with others.

relations.rationale: AuthorHappiness is a subclass of Disposition.
MutualUnderstanding is a subclass of Process.
HappinessRealizationProcess is a subclass of Process.
The realization of author happiness is part of (or constituted by) the process of mutual understanding.
AuthorHappiness (a Disposition) is realized in a HappinessRealizationProcess, per BFO realized-in relation.

Spinozistic happiness (beatitudo) is a higher good; AuthorHappiness is a subtype of the HigherGoods class already in the ontology — though HigherGoods is typed BFO_0000031 (GDC), this relation is flagged as an open question.

open_questions: Is 'the author' here specifically Spinoza (the individual already in the ontology), or is 'AuthorRole' being treated as a general class applicable to any author? If Spinoza-specific, we should instantiate an individual SpinozaHappiness inhering in Spinoza.

HigherGoods is currently typed as BFO_0000031 (Generically Dependent Continuant — informational content), but AuthorHappiness is typed as BFO_0000016 (Disposition). These are disjoint in BFO, so the subClassOf relation from AuthorHappiness to HigherGoods may be inconsistent. Should HigherGoods be retyped, or should we use a different relation (e.g., a custom 'constitutes' or 'isPartOf' relation at the class level)?

Does 'understanding as he understands' refer specifically to understanding via clear and distinct ideas (ClearAndDistinctIdea already in the ontology), or a broader shared comprehension? If the former, we should link MutualUnderstanding to ClearAndDistinctIdea.
Should this claim be annotated as a proposition from TheEthics or the TreatiseOnEmendationOfIntellect (both individuals already in the ontology)?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts that the author's happiness is (at least partly) constituted by others coming to understand what the author understands — a Spinozistic claim about beatitudo as inherently communicable or interpersonal. I model AuthorHappiness as a Disposition (BFO_0000016), since Spinozistic happiness is an enduring capacity/state of flourishing, not a momentary feeling. The sharing of understanding is modeled as a Process class (MutualUnderstanding), and the realization of the happiness disposition is tied to that process via BFO_0000054 (realized in). A HappinessRealizationProcess subclass is introduced to represent the specific processual realization. I flag the HigherGoods typing mismatch as an open question because it is currently GDC (BFO_0000031), which is disjoint from Disposition (BFO_0000016), making a direct subClassOf relation between AuthorHappiness and HigherGoods potentially inconsistent with BFO.

proposal.utterance: The soul is united to the body.

entities.label: Soul
entities.rationale: In Spinoza's framework (Ethics Part II), the soul (mind) is the idea of the body — a mode of thought. As a persistent entity that could bear qualities and roles, an Independent continuant is the safest top-level BFO type, though see open_questions for the tension.

entities.label: Body
entities.rationale: A body is a spatially extended, material thing — paradigmatically a Material entity in BFO.

entities.label: SoulBodyUnion
entities.rationale: The union of soul and body is best captured as a disposition (an intrinsically grounded realizable that explains how the soul and body function together). It inheres in the body (or the soul-body composite) and can be realized in various mental-physical processes.

relations.rationale: In Spinoza's system, the soul (anima/mens) is treated as equivalent to, or a subtype of, Mind (already in the ontology as working:Mind). Typing Soul as a subclass of Mind preserves the existing modeling.
The disposition of union inheres in the body (as the material bearer of the soul-body composite), per BFO's inheres-in relation.

open_questions: In Spinoza's Ethics, the soul (mens/anima) is identified with the idea of the body — a mode of thought, not an independent continuant. Should 'Soul' be modeled as a subclass of working:Mode (a specifically dependent continuant) rather than an independent continuant? This would be more Spinozistically faithful but creates a soul that depends on a body for its existence.
Should 'Soul' simply be treated as an alias for the existing working:Mind individual/class, rather than minting a new entity?
Is this utterance from a specific Spinozistic text (e.g., Ethics Part II Prop. 13)? If so, should a textual provenance relation be added?

Should 'SoulBodyUnion' be modeled as a quality (a stable property of the composite) rather than a disposition? This depends on whether 'union' is treated as a static relational fact or as a capacity grounding certain behaviors.
Does 'Body' here refer to a human body specifically, or any extended thing? Should it subclass working:Substance or BFO_0000040 directly?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance 'The soul is united to the body' introduces three new commitments: (1) there exists a kind called Soul, (2) there exists a kind called Body, and (3) there is a relation of union between them. Soul is provisionally typed as an Independent continuant subclassing the existing working:Mind class, since in Spinoza the mens/anima is a persistent thinking entity; however, the strictly Spinozistic reading would make it a mode (specifically dependent continuant) inhering in Substance, and this is flagged as an open question. Body is straightforwardly a Material entity. The union itself is modeled as a Disposition (SoulBodyUnion) inhering in the body, capturing the internally grounded capacity that explains how soul and body function as one — consistent with Spinoza's IIP13 claim that the human mind is the idea of an actually existing body. The existing working:Mind class is reused as the parent of Soul to avoid duplication.

proposal.utterance: The existence of any singular thing is not known unless its essence is known.

entities.label: SingularThing
entities.rationale: A singular thing (res singularis in Spinoza's terminology) is an individual existing entity — an independent continuant. We model it as a class since it is a kind.

entities.label: Essence
entities.rationale: In Spinoza, the essence of a thing is its defining intelligible content — what a thing is. Modeled as a generically dependent continuant (information-like content that can be instantiated in or abstracted from things), analogous to how the EternalInfiniteEssence individual is already typed as BFO_0000031.

entities.label: EssentialKnowledge
entities.rationale: Knowledge of an essence is modeled as a disposition (capacity/state) of a knower's intellect — it is internally grounded in the bearer (the intellect) and enables knowledge of existence. This captures the epistemic-prerequisite character of the claim.

entities.label: ExistenceKnowledge
entities.rationale: Knowledge that a singular thing exists is likewise a cognitive disposition of the knower's intellect. The proposition asserts this cannot obtain without EssentialKnowledge.

entities.label: EssencePrecedesExistenceKnowledgeConstraint
entities.rationale: The epistemic constraint that knowledge of essence is a necessary precondition for knowledge of existence. Modeled as a disposition class because it is an internally-grounded enabling condition. Could alternatively be a Quality, flagged in open_questions.

relations.rationale: EssentialKnowledge is a species of the intellect's idea-formation capacity already in the ontology (IdeaFormationCapacity : BFO_0000016).
ExistenceKnowledge is also a species of IdeaFormationCapacity — knowing that a thing exists is a cognitive disposition of the intellect.

SameNatureConstraint (BFO_0000016) is already in the ontology as a constraint disposition. The essence-before-existence-knowledge constraint is a species of such normative constraint on what is required for knowledge.

Essence in general is a subclass of EternalInfiniteEssence only if we restrict to God — but for singular finite things, Essence should NOT be a subclass of EternalInfiniteEssence. Flagged in open_questions; this relation is omitted pending clarification.

proposal.utterance: True ideas exist.

entities.label: TrueIdea
entities.rationale: A true idea in Spinoza is a specific kind of idea — one that corresponds adequately to its object. It is representational content that can be instantiated in different intellects, making it a generically dependent continuant. It is a subclass of ClearAndDistinctIdea already in the ontology, since for Spinoza true ideas are clear and distinct.

entities.label: TrueIdeaExistence
entities.rationale: The claim 'true ideas exist' asserts an existential quality — the property of existing — borne by true ideas. In BFO, existence as a quality can be modeled as a Quality inhering in the bearer. This captures Spinoza's assertion that true ideas are not merely logical constructs but actually obtain in reality.

relations.rationale: For Spinoza, true ideas are a species of clear and distinct ideas — they are the paradigm case. TrueIdea is thus a subclass of the already-committed ClearAndDistinctIdea class.
TrueIdeaExistence is a quality, a subclass of BFO Quality.
The existential quality inheres in instances of TrueIdea, capturing the assertion that true ideas exist — i.e., that this quality of actually obtaining belongs to them.

proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance 'True ideas exist' asserts both (a) a kind — TrueIdea, a species of ClearAndDistinctIdea (generically dependent continuant, representational content that can be instantiated in different intellects) — and (b) an existential claim that instances of this kind actually obtain, modeled as a quality TrueIdeaExistence inhering in TrueIdea instances. In Spinoza's framework (Ethics Part II, Axiom 6 and surrounding propositions), true ideas are distinguished by adequacy and correspondence to their objects; they are not merely possible but actually present in God's infinite intellect and derivatively in finite intellects. I have kept the modeling conservative, flagging the stronger modal reading (necessary existence of true ideas) as an open question rather than asserting it without user confirmation.

entities.label: IdeaOfIdea
entities.rationale: An idea-of-an-idea is a subtype of Idea (already a GDC class) whose intentional object is itself another idea. This captures Spinoza's claim that ideas can be objects of further ideas (reflexive ideation).

relations.rationale: An idea-of-an-idea is a specialised kind of Idea.
IdeaObjectRole is a Role (BFO_0000023) that inheres in an Idea when that Idea is taken as the object of another Idea.

In BFO terms, an Idea is already modeled as a Generically Dependent Continuant (BFO_0000031).
