entities.rationale: The utterance asserts that the origin of Nature is unique — uniqueness is a quality (measurable, intrinsic property) of the entity. This is a new class not yet in the ontology.

entities.label: NoBeyondConstraint
entities.rationale: The claim 'beyond which there is no being' is a propositional/informational content — a constraint on the totality of being. It is best modeled as a generically dependent continuant (a propositional content or constraint), parallel to existing constraint individuals like NecessaryClarityAndDistinctnessConstraint.

relations.rationale: The role 'OriginOfNature' inheres in God (the unique infinite being identified in this Spinozistic context as the origin of Nature).

OriginOfNature is typed as a Role individual; FiniteThingRole is the closest existing role class, though this is marked as an open question since the origin of Nature is explicitly infinite, not finite — the mapping may need refinement.
Reusing the existing AbsoluteInfinity quality individual already borne by God, reinforcing that the origin of Nature is infinite.
This propositional constraint is part of the content of TheEthics (Spinoza's system), paralleling other constraint individuals already part of that work.

Is 'WholeOfNature' the same individual as 'God' in this context (deus sive natura), or should they be modeled as distinct individuals linked by an identity or equivalence relation?

proposal.utterance: There is no doubt in the soul through the thing itself concerning which one doubts.

entities.label: Soul
entities.rationale: In Spinoza's framework (and broader scholastic usage invoked here), the soul (anima/mens) is an independent continuant — a mind-like entity that bears mental states. It is a kind, not an individual.

entities.label: Doubt
entities.rationale: Doubt is an internally grounded mental disposition of the soul toward a proposition or object; it inheres in the soul and is realized in acts of doubting. Modeling as a disposition (BFO_0000016) is appropriate.

entities.label: ObjectOfDoubt
entities.rationale: The 'thing itself concerning which one doubts' plays a contextually assigned role relative to the doubting soul. This is externally grounded (the thing is singled out by the doubt relation), so a role class is appropriate.

entities.label: DoubtGroundedInObjectConstraint
entities.rationale: This is a propositional/normative constraint (an informational content) asserting that doubt in the soul is grounded in the object doubted, not in the soul itself. It parallels other constraint individuals already in the ontology (e.g. IncompatibilityOfClearDistinctPerceptionWithFeigning).

relations.rationale: Doubt as a disposition inheres in the soul (its bearer).
The constraint is an informational content (generically dependent continuant) capturing the propositional claim that doubt is grounded in the object, not the soul.
ObjectOfDoubt is a subclass of Role (externally grounded, conferred by the doubt relation).
Soul is an independent continuant class.
Doubt is a disposition class.

open_questions: Should 'Soul' be identified with the existing 'Mind' class (working:Mind, BFO_0000004) already in the ontology, or does Spinoza's text here use 'soul' (anima) to denote a distinct concept from 'mind' (mens)?

Is 'Doubt' here specifically an epistemic disposition about a proposition, or more broadly a psychological state? This affects whether it is better typed as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) or a Quality (BFO_0000019).
Should 'ObjectOfDoubt' be restricted to material entities, or can it range over any continuant or even propositions (generically dependent continuants)?
Should DoubtGroundedInObjectConstraint be linked to existing works like TreatiseOnEmendationOfIntellect or TheEthics as its informational source?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance (from Spinoza's Treatise on the Emendation of the Intellect, §55 context) asserts a normative-epistemic constraint: doubt residing in the soul is not produced by the soul independently but is determined by (grounded in) the object about which one doubts. Ontologically this introduces three new kinds — Soul (an independent continuant class, possibly coextensive with the existing Mind class, hence flagged as an open question), Doubt (a disposition inhering in the soul), and ObjectOfDoubt (a role borne by the thing that grounds the doubt) — plus one new individual constraint (DoubtGroundedInObjectConstraint) parallel to the family of epistemic-constraint GDC individuals already in the working ontology. The key relation is that Doubt inheres in the Soul (RO_0000052) but its causal/grounding source is the object bearing the ObjectOfDoubt role, a claim captured declaratively in the constraint individual. No existing individuals or classes are directly reused, but Soul/Mind overlap is flagged for human review.

proposal.utterance: A single idea in the soul, whether true or false, produces neither doubt nor certainty but only a sensation.

entities.label: Certainty
entities.rationale: Certainty is the positive epistemic state grounded in the bearer; also requires more than one idea per this claim. Modeled as a disposition.

entities.label: Sensation
entities.rationale: A sensation is a happening or episode in the soul, temporally bounded; modeled as a process. Spinoza here says a single idea produces only a sensation, distinguishing it from cognitive attitudes like doubt or certainty.

entities.label: SingleIdeaInSoulConstraint

proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance encodes a doctrinal claim from Spinoza (likely from the Treatise on the Emendation of the Intellect or Ethics) that a single idea — regardless of truth value — is insufficient to generate either doubt or certainty, producing only a sensation. proposal.utterance: Doubt arises through another idea that is not clear and distinct.

entities.label: Doubt
entities.rationale: Doubt in Spinoza's epistemology is an internally grounded cognitive state — a disposition of the mind to suspend or withhold assent — arising when the idea in view lacks clarity and distinctness. entities.label: NonClearAndDistinctIdea
entities.rationale: A subclass of Idea (already in the ontology) that lacks the quality of clarity and distinctness. This is the proximate cause of doubt per the utterance.

entities.label: DoubtArisingFromNonClearIdea
entities.rationale: A propositional / theoretical commitment (GDC, encoded as a Spinozistic constraint-content) that doubt arises through another idea that is not clear and distinct. Parallel to existing constraint individuals like IncompatibilityOfClearDistinctPerceptionWithFeigning.

relations.rationale: A non-clear-and-distinct idea is a species of Idea, contrasting with ClearAndDistinctIdea already in the ontology.
Doubt is a disposition (internally grounded realizable entity) of the mind.
Doubt as a disposition inheres in the Mind (Mind already in the ontology as an individual/class).
The constraint-individual is a generically dependent continuant encoding the propositional content that doubt arises from a non-clear-and-distinct idea.

Spinoza's TEI suggests a second idea (about the first) generates doubt — should we model a 'DoubtGeneratingIdea' role distinct from the doubted idea?

Should DoubtArisingFromNonClearIdea be typed as an individual constraint-content (like IncompatibilityOfClearDistinctPerceptionWithFeigning) or should it be left as a class-level subClassOf axiom between Doubt and NonClearAndDistinctIdea via some causation relation?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts a Spinozistic epistemic principle: doubt is not a primitive state but arises causally from the presence of an idea that lacks clarity and distinctness. proposal.utterance: Memory is something different from the intellect.

entities.label: Memory
entities.rationale: In Spinoza's TEI, memory is treated as a faculty or capacity of the mind distinct from intellect. Existing classes Intellect and Imagination are already typed as BFO_0000004 (independent continuant), so Memory is typed consistently as an independent continuant class representing a mental faculty. It is distinct from Intellect, which is already in the ontology.

relations.rationale: Memory is an independent continuant (a faculty), consistent with how Intellect and Imagination are typed.

open_questions: Should Memory be modeled as a subclass of a shared 'MentalFaculty' class alongside Intellect and Imagination, or remain a direct subclass of BFO_0000004?

Is the claim purely a distinction assertion (Memory ≠ Intellect), or does the context also specify what memory is positively (e.g., a disposition, a process, or a faculty-continuant)? The text of TEI §83 associates memory with association of ideas rather than with intellect's clear-and-distinct perception, which may suggest a Disposition (BFO_0000016) rather than an independent continuant.
Should we assert an OWL disjointness axiom between Memory and Intellect to formally encode their distinctness?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts that memory and intellect are distinct entities. The ontology already contains working:Intellect typed as BFO_0000004 (independent continuant). By analogy with Intellect and Imagination (both BFO_0000004), we mint working:Memory as a new class under BFO_0000004. The key ontological commitment is the distinctness of memory from intellect; this can be represented by giving them separate class IRIs with no subsumption relation between them. An open question remains whether Memory is better typed as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) since in Spinoza memory is more of a capacity linked to bodily traces and association of corporeal images, but conservative reuse of the pattern established for Intellect and Imagination favors BFO_0000004 for now, leaving the question open for user resolution.

proposal.utterance: Memory is nothing but a sensation of impressions on the brain together with the thought of a determinate duration.

entities.label: Memory
entities.rationale: Memory in Spinoza's account is a capacity or disposition of the mind/brain — an internally grounded tendency to re-present sensations together with temporal indexing. Disposition (BFO_0000016) fits best as it is a realizable that is internally grounded in its bearer.

entities.label: SensationOfBrainImpression
entities.rationale: The sensation of impressions on the brain is an occurrent process — a happening involving the brain as material participant. It is the phenomenal/causal side of memory.

entities.label: BrainImpression
entities.rationale: An impression on the brain is a specifically dependent quality inhering in the brain (a material entity). It is a measurable, intrinsic property of the brain's state.

entities.label: DeterminateDuration
entities.rationale: A determinate duration is a quality (or measure) that inheres in a process or temporal region — the specific, bounded length of time associated with a recalled experience. Typed as Quality because it is a specifically dependent property of the thing remembered.

entities.label: ThoughtOfDuration
entities.rationale: The 'thought of a determinate duration' is an informational/representational content — the mental representation of a bounded time span. As a representational content that can be multiply realised, it fits GDC (BFO_0000031), consistent with the existing Idea and ClearAndDistinctIdea classes.

relations.rationale: Memory is a subclass of Disposition, directly under BFO Disposition.
Sensation of brain impression is a process subclass.
Memory (disposition) is realized in a SensationOfBrainImpression process — the sensation is the realization of the memory disposition.
A thought of a determinate duration is a species of Idea (already in the ontology as a GDC subclass), being a representational content about temporal extent.
The sensation process has BrainImpression as a quality-bearing part of its substrate; the process unfolds with the brain impression as the material grounding quality.

open_questions: Should 'Memory' be typed as a Disposition (internally grounded capacity of the mind/brain) or as a Process (the actual act of remembering)? Spinoza's definition suggests it is constituted by two co-occurring components (sensation + thought), which could also point to a Process type.
Is 'Brain' already in the ontology as an individual or class of material entity? If not, should it be added as a material entity that bears BrainImpression qualities?

Should ThoughtOfDuration be a subclass of the existing 'Idea' class or of 'ClearAndDistinctIdea'? Spinoza's account of memory often associates it with imagination rather than intellect, suggesting it may not be a clear and distinct idea.

The definition treats Memory as a compound of sensation and thought — should we represent Memory as a complex process having both SensationOfBrainImpression and ThoughtOfDuration as parts (using BFO_0000051), rather than as a disposition?
proposal.rationale_summary: Spinoza's definition of memory (TEI §83) identifies it as constituted by two jointly necessary components: (1) a sensation of impressions on the brain, and (2) a thought of a determinate duration. I have modeled Memory as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) because it is an internally-grounded, realizable capacity of the mind-body complex; its realization is SensationOfBrainImpression (a Process, BFO_0000015). BrainImpression is typed as a Quality (BFO_0000019) inhering in the brain as material entity, while DeterminateDuration is also a Quality capturing the bounded temporal extent. ThoughtOfDuration is typed as a Generically Dependent Continuant (BFO_0000031) and placed as a subclass of the existing Idea class, reflecting its representational nature. The main open question is whether Memory should instead be modeled as a compound Process rather than a Disposition, given that Spinoza's phrasing is more constitutive than dispositional.

proposal.utterance: The imagination is affected only by singular things and by bodies.

entities.label: SingularThing
entities.rationale: A singular thing in Spinoza is a particular individual existent — a concrete, independently existing entity. Modeled as a class under independent continuant.

entities.label: Body
entities.rationale: A body in Spinoza is a material, extended thing — paradigmatically a material entity in BFO.

entities.label: AffectionByImagination
entities.rationale: The being-affected of the imagination is an occurrent process involving the imagination and its object. Modeled as a subclass of BFO Process.

entities.label: ImaginationAffectedBySingularsConstraint
entities.rationale: The propositional content asserting that imagination is affected only by singular things and bodies is an information-bearing, generically dependent continuant — a theoretical constraint or principle encoded in Spinoza's system.

relations.rationale: Bodies are a species of singular thing in Spinoza — the claim specifies 'singular things and bodies', where bodies are the extended subset of singular things the imagination is particularly responsive to. Alternatively bodies may be listed as a coordinate kind; this is open for user review.
The process of affection has the imagination as a participant (the entity being affected).
Singular things (and bodies as a subclass) are the participants that affect the imagination in this process.
This constraint is part of the theoretical content of the Treatise on Emendation of Intellect, where Spinoza discusses modes of perception and imagination.

open_questions: Should 'Body' be modeled as a subclass of 'SingularThing', or as a coordinate class (both being species of singular things that affect imagination)? Spinoza's phrasing 'singular things and bodies' may be treating bodies as a subset or as a parallel category.

Is 'Imagination' here the same individual already in the ontology (working:Imagination typed as BFO_0000004), or should it be a class? Currently it is a class under independent continuant — should the affection constraint inhere in or be associated with that class?

Should working:SingularThing be typed under BFO_0000040 (material entity) rather than BFO_0000004 (independent continuant), since Spinoza's singular things are typically extended or thinking things? Or should it remain at the more general level?
Does this utterance come from the Treatise on Emendation of Intellect specifically, or from another Spinoza text? This affects which work individual the constraint should be part-of.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts a Spinozistic constraint on the Imagination: it is only affected (passively acted upon) by singular things and by bodies. This introduces three new items: the class SingularThing (a particular, concrete individual existent, typed as independent continuant), the class Body (a material extended thing, typed as material entity, likely a subclass of SingularThing), and the process class AffectionByImagination (the occurring of the imagination being affected). A propositional-content individual ImaginationAffectedBySingularsConstraint is minted to encode the theoretical claim itself as a generically dependent continuant. The existing working:Imagination class (BFO_0000004) and working:TreatiseOnEmendationOfIntellect individual are reused. Key open questions concern whether Body is a subclass or coordinate class of SingularThing, and which text this claim belongs to.

proposal.utterance: Fictitious, false, and other ideas have their origin in the imagination.

entities.label: FictitiousIdea
entities.rationale: A fictitious idea is a type of Idea (already a class in the ontology, typed as GDC/BFO_0000031). Fictitious ideas are a kind of information content that can be tokened in different minds, hence generically dependent continuant.

entities.label: FalseIdea
entities.rationale: A false idea is another subtype of Idea, distinct from fictitious ideas as captured by the already-existing FalseVsFictitiousDistinction individual. Typed as GDC.

entities.label: IdeaOriginationProcess
entities.rationale: The process by which ideas originate or are produced. This captures the causal/generative relation asserted in the utterance.

entities.label: Imagination
entities.rationale: Imagination already exists in the ontology as a class typed BFO_0000004. Reusing it.

relations.rationale: Fictitious ideas are a subtype of Idea.
False ideas are a subtype of Idea.
The IdeaOriginationProcess has participant Imagination as its source/origin — Imagination is the continuant that participates in the origination process as the generative faculty.
Fictitious ideas are outputs of the IdeaOriginationProcess — the process has these ideas as participants (products).
False ideas are outputs of the IdeaOriginationProcess originating in imagination.
The utterance says 'other ideas' also originate in imagination, so Idea in general participates in the origination process from imagination.

open_questions: Spinoza distinguishes fictitious ideas, false ideas, and doubtful ideas as three non-adequate idea types. Should we also add a DoubtfulIdea class as a third subtype here?

Should IdeaOriginationProcess be further constrained so that adequate (clear and distinct) ideas are NOT produced by imagination — i.e., should we assert a disjointness between IdeaOriginationProcess-from-imagination and the process producing ClearAndDistinctIdea instances?

Is Imagination here conceived as a faculty (a disposition or capacity of the mind) rather than an independent continuant? It is currently typed BFO_0000004; should it be retyped as BFO_0000016 (Disposition) inhering in Mind?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts that fictitious ideas, false ideas, and other (non-adequate) ideas have their causal origin in the imagination. I model FictitiousIdea and FalseIdea as new subclasses of the existing Idea class (both GDCs), and introduce IdeaOriginationProcess (a Process) to represent the generative/causal relationship. Imagination already exists in the ontology as BFO_0000004 and is reused. The IdeaOriginationProcess is linked via RO_0000057 (has participant) to both Imagination as the originating faculty and to the idea-types as products. This is a class-level assertion (all-instances reading), consistent with Spinoza's general claim in the TEI. I raise open questions about whether a DoubtfulIdea class is needed, whether we should assert disjointness with clear-and-distinct idea formation, and whether Imagination's BFO typing should be reconsidered.

proposal.utterance: False ideas do not arise from the very power of the mind but from external causes.

entities.label: FalseIdea
entities.rationale: A false idea is a subtype of Idea (already in the ontology as BFO_0000031). It is a generically dependent continuant (an informational/cognitive content) that can be instantiated in different minds.

entities.label: ExternalCause
entities.rationale: An external cause is an independent continuant outside the mind that is the origin of false ideas. Typed as independent continuant because external causes are things that exist independently and act on the mind.

entities.label: FictitiousIdea

entities.label: FalseIdea

entities.label: ImaginationOriginationProcess

proposal.utterance: Imagination is something different from intellect, and the soul has the nature of something acted upon in imagination.

entities.label: Soul
entities.rationale: The soul (anima) in Spinoza's framework is treated as an independent continuant — a thing that persists through time and has properties. It is distinct from Mind as used elsewhere (though related), so a new class is warranted unless the user wants to equate them.

entities.label: PassiveQuality
entities.rationale: The soul is described as 'acted upon' (passive) in imagination — this is a quality of being in a passive mode, inhering in the soul when it imagines. Modeling as a Quality subtype captures the Spinozistic notion that imagination involves passivity (being determined from without).

entities.label: ImaginingProcess
entities.rationale: Imagination as an activity (the soul being acted upon) is a process — an occurrent in which the soul participates passively. The existing working:Imagination is typed as BFO_0000004 (an independent continuant, the faculty), so we need a separate class for the act/process of imagining.

entities.label: ImaginingVsIntellectDistinction
entities.rationale: The assertion that imagination is different from intellect is a propositional/doctrinal content — an information artifact (generically dependent continuant) captured in the philosophical work. This mirrors how other doctrinal claims are modeled in the ontology.

proposal.utterance: A true idea is simple or composed of simple ideas and shows how and why something is or has been done.

entities.label: TrueIdea
entities.rationale: A true idea is a subtype of Idea (already in the ontology as a generically dependent continuant — an information-bearing content). It is a class because 'true idea' is a kind, not a particular instance.

entities.label: SimpleIdea
entities.rationale: A simple idea is a kind of idea that is not composed of further ideas. It is a generically dependent continuant (information content) and a subtype of the existing Idea class.

entities.label: ComposedIdea
entities.rationale: A composed idea is built from simple ideas. It is a generically dependent continuant subtype of Idea, distinct from SimpleIdea.

entities.label: SimplicityQuality
entities.rationale: Simplicity (being simple, undecomposable) is a quality that inheres in an idea. It is a BFO Quality — a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in its bearer.

entities.label: CausalExplanatoryContent
entities.rationale: The 'showing how and why something is or has been done' is an explanatory/causal content that a true idea carries. This is best modeled as a kind of generically dependent continuant (information content) distinct from the idea itself but carried by it.

relations.rationale: A true idea is a species of Idea.
Spinoza asserts a true idea is either simple or composed of simples; a simple idea is thus a subtype of true idea.
A composed-of-simples idea is also a subtype of true idea, per the assertion.
A composed idea has simple ideas as parts (BFO has-part relation between generically dependent continuants).
SimplicityQuality is a BFO Quality.
The quality of simplicity inheres in simple ideas.
A true idea has as part (carries) causal-explanatory content — it shows how and why something is or has been done.

open_questions: Should 'showing how and why something is or has been done' be modeled as a disposition (capacity to explain) on the idea rather than a content part? BFO Disposition might better capture this normative/functional character.
Should SimpleIdea and ComposedIdea be disjoint classes (a true idea is either simple OR composed, not both)?
Is CausalExplanatoryContent a property of ALL true ideas (both simple and composed), or only of composed ones? Spinoza's text may imply the causal-genetic account applies to both.
Should 'TrueIdea' also be related to the existing ClearAndDistinctIdea class — are they coextensive in Spinoza's system, or is there a further distinction to draw?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance defines a true idea structurally (simple, or composed of simple ideas) and functionally (shows how and why something is or has been done). I model TrueIdea as a subclass of the existing Idea class (BFO_0000031, generically dependent continuant). Two further subclasses capture the structural disjunction: SimpleIdea (atomic, bears a SimplicityQuality) and ComposedIdea (has SimpleIdea instances as parts via BFO has-part). The causal-explanatory function — showing how and why — is modeled as a CausalExplanatoryContent, a generically dependent continuant that true ideas have as part. An alternative disposition-based modeling is flagged as an open question, as is the relationship between TrueIdea and the already-committed ClearAndDistinctIdea individual/class.

proposal.utterance: The soul acts according to certain laws, like a spiritual automaton.

entities.label: Soul
entities.rationale: In Spinoza's framework the soul (mind) is a finite mode of thought, but as a bearer of dispositions and qualities it is modeled as an independent continuant. A new class is warranted because 'Soul' is conceptually distinct from the existing 'Mind' class, though the two may later be related. Alternatively it could be equated with Mind; flagged as open question.

entities.label: SpiritualAutomatonDisposition
entities.rationale: The claim that the soul acts 'like a spiritual automaton' asserts an internally-grounded, law-governed causal disposition inhering in the soul. A Disposition is the correct BFO type for an intrinsic capacity that is realized in processes when triggered.

entities.label: LawGovernedActingProcess
entities.rationale: The soul acting according to certain laws is a process — a happening in time realizing the spiritual-automaton disposition. Modeling this as a Process class captures the occurrent nature of the soul's law-governed operation.

entities.label: DeterminingLaw
entities.rationale: The 'certain laws' according to which the soul acts are informational/normative patterns — generically dependent continuants that can be instantiated across bearers and are not tied to a single material substrate.

relations.rationale: SpiritualAutomatonDisposition is a subclass of BFO Disposition.
Soul is a subclass of Independent continuant.
LawGovernedActingProcess is a subclass of Process.
DeterminingLaw is a subclass of Generically dependent continuant.
Every soul bears a SpiritualAutomatonDisposition (OWL restriction: bearer_of some SpiritualAutomatonDisposition); captures the universal claim in the utterance.
The SpiritualAutomatonDisposition is realized in LawGovernedActingProcess — the disposition, when triggered, is realized as the soul acting according to laws.
The LawGovernedActingProcess has participant the Soul.

open_questions: Should 'Soul' be equated with the existing 'Mind' class, or is Spinoza's use of 'soul' (anima) here distinct from 'mind' (mens) as already modeled?

Is 'spiritual automaton' being asserted as a universal claim about all souls, or only as an analogy for the ideal intellect's operation (as in the Treatise on the Emendation of the Intellect context)?
Should 'DeterminingLaw' be linked to existing 'DeterminingRelation' or kept separate, given that laws here are informational patterns rather than causal processes?

Does 'acting according to certain laws' imply that the laws are causes of the soul's acts (efficient causation), or normative constraints on them — affecting whether DeterminingLaw should be a GDC or modeled differently?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts that the soul operates deterministically according to fixed laws, a claim associated with Spinoza's 'spiritual automaton' metaphor in the Treatise on the Emendation of the Intellect. Ontologically, this commits to: (1) a kind of entity — Soul — as an independent continuant bearing a disposition; (2) a disposition class — SpiritualAutomatonDisposition — inhering in souls and encoding their internally-grounded, law-governed operation; (3) a process class — LawGovernedActingProcess — as the realization of that disposition; and (4) a class of informational patterns — DeterminingLaw — that govern those processes, modeled as generically dependent continuants. The existing 'Mind' class may overlap with 'Soul'; this is flagged as an open question. No individuals are asserted by the utterance, only universal structural claims about the soul's nature.

entities.label: LawsOfIntellect

entities.label: ImaginingProcess

proposal.utterance: Words are part of the imagination.

entities.label: Words
entities.rationale: Words, in Spinoza's framework, are linguistic signs whose meaning depends on their use in minds and imagination; they are patterns that can be instantiated in different bearers, fitting GDC. They are not material entities per se but information-content objects.

relations.rationale: The utterance asserts that words are part of the imagination. BFO 'part of' (BFO_0000050) encodes this mereological claim. Note: Imagination is currently typed as BFO_0000004 (independent continuant / material entity), while Words is typed as BFO_0000031 (GDC). This cross-category part-of relation is ontologically awkward and flagged as an open question.

open_questions: Spinoza's claim that 'words are part of the imagination' is a theoretical/philosophical claim about the ontological status of language, not a simple mereological containment. Should this be modeled as (a) a part-of relation between Words (GDC) and Imagination (BFO_0000004), (b) a disposition or capacity of Imagination that realizes words, or (c) as an annotation/constraint on the Imagination class rather than a direct BFO part-of relation?

Imagination is currently typed as BFO_0000004 (independent continuant). Should it instead be a BFO_0000016 (disposition) or BFO_0000004 subtype such as a cognitive faculty? BFO part-of relations between GDCs and independent continuants are not standard in BFO 2020 and may cause reasoning errors.

Should 'Words' be a class of GDCs (linguistic sign-tokens as generically dependent continuants) or should word-tokens be material entities (inscriptions, sounds) and word-types be GDCs? Spinoza likely means word-meanings/signs, favoring GDC for the type.

Words are best typed as a class of generically dependent continuants (BFO_0000031) because they are information-content patterns that can be multiply instantiated. proposal.utterance: Words can be a cause of many and great errors.

entities.label: Words
entities.rationale: Words are linguistic/symbolic patterns that can be instantiated in multiple bearers (spoken, written, etc.); they are generically dependent continuants — information-bearing entities.

entities.label: Error
entities.rationale: An error in this Spinozistic context is a false or confused idea — a cognitive content item, best typed as a generically dependent continuant (a representational content that can be multiply instantiated in minds).

entities.label: WordCausedErrorProcess
entities.rationale: The causal production of errors by words is an occurrent process — the happening in which words bring about confused or false ideas in a mind.

entities.label: WordsAsErrorCauseConstraint
entities.rationale: The specific Spinozistic doctrinal claim that words can be a cause of many and great errors is itself an information-content item (a propositional claim in the text), best treated as an individual generically dependent continuant, analogous to other constraint/principle individuals already in the ontology.

relations.rationale: This propositional claim is part of the content of the Treatise on the Emendation of the Intellect, where Spinoza discusses the hazards of words for clear thinking.
Instances of the WordCausedErrorProcess have Words as participants (as the causal agent in the process).
Instances of the WordCausedErrorProcess have Error (confused/false ideas) as participants (as the output/effect in the process).
An error in Spinoza's epistemology is a species of Idea — specifically a false or confused idea — so Error is a subclass of the existing Idea class.

open_questions: Is this utterance a direct quotation from the Treatise on the Emendation of the Intellect (TEI), or from another Spinozistic text? This affects which PhilosophicalWork individual the WordsAsErrorCauseConstraint should be part of.
Should 'Error' be modeled more specifically as a subclass of 'ClearAndDistinctIdea's negation — i.e., a confused or inadequate idea — or is a simple subclass of Idea sufficient at this stage?
Should 'Words' be further distinguished from 'Idea' or 'Imagination'? In Spinoza, words are associated with the first kind of knowledge (imagination); do you want to assert that relation now?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts a Spinozistic doctrinal claim: words (linguistic signs) can causally produce errors (false or confused ideas). I model 'Words' as a new class of generically dependent continuant (linguistic patterns), 'Error' as a subclass of the existing Idea class (a confused/false idea, itself a generically dependent continuant), and 'WordCausedErrorProcess' as a process class linking the two as participants. The doctrinal claim itself is reified as an individual 'WordsAsErrorCauseConstraint' — a propositional content item of the type already used throughout this ontology for Spinozistic principles — and asserted to be part of the TreatiseOnEmendationOfIntellect, which is the most plausible source. No BFO violations are introduced: all types are consistent with existing class hierarchies.

entities.label: Word
entities.rationale: A word is a linguistic sign — a pattern of meaning that can be instantiated in multiple tokens (spoken, written). BFO_0000031 (generically dependent continuant) covers information artifacts and patterns that can be copied and tokened.

entities.rationale: The standing of a word as a sign for something is a relational/functional process of signification — a role-like process binding word to object. entities.label: ImaginativeRepresentation
entities.rationale: Things as they appear in the imagination — imaginative content — are information-like patterns carried by the imagination faculty. BFO_0000031 fits since they are representational contents that could in principle be tokened or copied.

entities.label: IntellectualRepresentation
entities.rationale: Things as they are in the intellect — adequate ideas — are a subtype of ClearAndDistinctIdea (already in the ontology). This class captures the content held by the intellect as distinct from imaginative representation.

entities.label: NegativeCharacterTendency

relations.rationale: NegativeNameQuality inheres in NameInIntellect instances — it is a specifically dependent continuant whose bearer is a name of this kind.

Names given 'only in the intellect' are part of (or dependent on) the Intellect individual/class already in the ontology; this part-of relation captures the 'only in the intellect' qualifier.

entities.label: InItselfCondition

entities.label: UnderstandableThroughItselfConstraint
entities.rationale: This is a specific propositional/conceptual content — the constraint that whatever is in itself or cause of itself is understood through its essence alone. It is an information artifact (GDC) that can be articulated and instantiated in multiple texts.

entities.label: EssenceAloneUnderstandingDisposition
entities.rationale: The disposition of being understandable through essence alone — an internally grounded feature of substances/causa sui entities that grounds their epistemic self-sufficiency.

relations.rationale: In Spinoza, being 'in itself' and being 'cause of itself' are co-defined (Ethics Def 1 and 3); InItselfCondition is closely related to CausaSui — modeling as subclass since 'in itself' is the ontological side and CausaSui the causal side of the same Substance concept.
The constraint is propositional content — a generically dependent continuant.
This disposition is internally grounded in the bearer's essence, qualifying it as a BFO Disposition.
This constraint is expressed as part of the content of The Ethics (cf. Ethics Part I, Definition 3 and Axiom 4).

entities.label: CausalDependence

entities.label: PerfectDefinition

entities.label: InnermostEssenceExplanation
entities.rationale: The content that explains the inmost essence of a thing is a generically dependent continuant — it is an informational pattern or propositional content that a perfect definition must carry. It is the core constitutive requirement of a perfect definition.

entities.label: Proprium
entities.rationale: A proprium (propria plural) in the scholastic/Spinozistic sense is a property that necessarily belongs to a thing but is not part of its essence — best modeled as a Quality (specifically dependent continuant) that inheres in a thing but does not constitute its inmost essence. relations.rationale: A perfect definition has as part the content that explains the inmost essence of the thing defined — the inmost-essence explanation is a constitutive part of the perfect definition.

proposal.utterance: Created things have proximate causes.

entities.label: CreatedThing
entities.rationale: A 'created thing' in Spinoza's framework (Ethics 1p28) is a finite mode or dependent entity that has a cause external to itself. It is an independent continuant (material or immaterial entity) that exists in virtue of a proximate cause. Modeling as a subclass of independent continuant is the closest BFO fit, though Spinoza's modes are specifically dependent; this is flagged as an open question.

entities.label: ProximateCause
entities.rationale: A proximate cause is a relational, externally grounded function that a thing plays with respect to another thing it produces. Modeling it as a Role (BFO_0000023) captures its relational, context-dependent character: an entity bears the proximate-cause role relative to the thing it causes.

entities.label: ProximateCausationProcess
entities.rationale: The causal production of a created thing by its proximate cause is an occurrent process. This parallels the existing DeterminingRelation class (also a process) but specifically captures the proximate, finite causal nexus asserted in this proposition.

entities.label: HasProximiteCauseConstraint
entities.rationale: The propositional content asserting that every created thing has a proximate cause is an information artifact (generically dependent continuant), analogous to other constraint/principle individuals already in the ontology (e.g., IncompatibilityOfSimplicityWithFeigning).

relations.rationale: The constraint has as part (or has as its content) the notion of a proximate cause role. Using has-part loosely to associate the propositional content with the role concept it invokes.
Created things are independent continuants (finite modes of substance) in Spinoza's metaphysics.
Proximate cause is a role borne by whatever entity immediately produces the created thing.
The proximate causation process realizes the proximate cause role of the causing entity.
The created thing participates in the proximate causation process as its effect/output.

open_questions: In Spinoza's system, 'created things' are finite modes, which are specifically dependent continuants (modes of substance). Should CreatedThing be a subclass of working:Mode (BFO_0000020) rather than BFO_0000004? The current typing as independent continuant may conflict with Spinoza's monism.
Should 'proximate cause' also cover infinite modes (which also have proximate causes, namely other infinite modes), or is this class restricted to finite/created things only?

Should the HasProximiteCauseConstraint individual be linked to TheEthics (Ethics 1p28) via a part-of or source relation?

proposal.utterance: All properties of a thing can be deduced from its definition.

entities.label: DefinitionalDeducibility
entities.rationale: A disposition class representing the capacity or tendency of a defined thing to have all its properties derivable from its definition. This is internally grounded in the nature of the defined entity, making Disposition the best BFO fit.

entities.label: Definition
entities.rationale: A definition is an information artifact — a generically dependent continuant that can be instantiated in multiple physical or mental bearers. It encodes the essential nature of a thing.

entities.label: DeductionOfProperties
entities.rationale: The act of deducing properties from a definition is a cognitive/logical process — an occurrent unfolding in time. This is a subclass of Process.

relations.rationale: The principle 'all properties of a thing can be deduced from its definition' is an information entity — a generically dependent continuant.
DefinitionalDeducibility is a disposition class, internally grounded in the nature of defined things.

Deducing properties is a process unfolding in time.
The disposition DefinitionalDeducibility is realized in the process DeductionOfProperties, following BFO's realized-in relation.

proposal.utterance: Uncreated things require nothing except their own being for explanation.

entities.label: UncreatedThing
entities.rationale: An uncreated thing is a kind of independent continuant — it subsists on its own and is not brought into being by another. It does not depend on another for its existence in the way dependent continuants do.

entities.label: SelfExplanatoryExistence
entities.rationale: The property of requiring nothing except one's own being for explanation is an internally grounded capacity/disposition — a self-grounding explanatory sufficiency. This is closely related to CausaSui already in the ontology, but distinct in being about explanatory rather than causal self-sufficiency. It is typed as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) because it is a real, intrinsic feature of the bearer.

entities.label: UncreatedThingExplanatoryPrinciple
entities.rationale: The principle itself — 'uncreated things require nothing except their own being for explanation' — is an informational/propositional content that can be encoded and is part of Spinoza's philosophical framework (related to TheEthics and the Spinozistic texts). It is a generically dependent continuant as a propositional content.

relations.rationale: SelfExplanatoryExistence is a refinement of CausaSui — being self-explanatory is closely related to being self-caused; both are forms of ontological self-sufficiency. Subclassing captures the relationship while preserving the distinction between explanatory and causal self-grounding.
In Spinoza's system, the uncreated things are Substances — entities conceived through themselves. UncreatedThing is a natural subclass of Substance already in the ontology.
The principle is a generically dependent continuant — propositional content that can be instantiated in multiple texts.
This principle is part of the content of TheEthics as a philosophical work.

open_questions: Should UncreatedThing be equated with Substance exactly (making it an equivalent class), or is 'uncreated' a distinct attribute that happens to co-extensionally apply to substances in Spinoza's system?

Is SelfExplanatoryExistence intended to be strictly identical to CausaSui (in which case we should reuse that class), or is the explanatory self-sufficiency distinct from causal self-sufficiency in this context?
Should UncreatedThingExplanatoryPrinciple also be linked to working:ExistenceNecessitation, since self-explanatory existence and necessary existence are closely related in Spinoza?

I propose three new items: (1) UncreatedThing as a class of independent continuants (subclassing the existing Substance class, since in Spinoza uncreated things are substances conceived through themselves); (2) SelfExplanatoryExistence as a disposition (BFO_0000016) capturing the intrinsic self-grounding explanatory capacity, subclassed under the existing CausaSui disposition since explanatory self-sufficiency is a species of causal/ontic self-sufficiency; and (3) an individual UncreatedThingExplanatoryPrinciple representing the propositional content of this claim as a generically dependent continuant, linked as a part of TheEthics. The core ontological commitment is that uncreated things bear a disposition of SelfExplanatoryExistence, which is internally grounded in their nature — consistent with BFO's treatment of dispositions as intrinsic.

proposal.utterance: Singular, changeable things depend essentially on fixed and eternal things.

entities.label: SingularChangeableThing
entities.rationale: Singular, changeable things are individual existing entities with temporal variability — best modeled as a subclass of Independent Continuant (BFO_0000004), which covers persisting things that exist independently.

entities.label: FixedEternalThing
entities.rationale: Fixed and eternal things are persisting entities that do not change — modeled as a subclass of Independent Continuant (BFO_0000004). They persist eternally and are the ground for singular things. Spinoza's fixed and eternal things include God/Substance and infinite modes.

entities.label: EssentialDependence
entities.rationale: The essential dependence of singular changeable things on fixed eternal things is an internally grounded, necessary relational feature — best modeled as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) inhering in singular changeable things. relations.rationale: Singular changeable things are independent continuants — they persist and exist in their own right even as they change.

Essential dependence is a disposition — an internally grounded capacity inhering in singular changeable things whereby their existence and nature necessarily derive from fixed eternal things.
The disposition of essential dependence inheres in singular changeable things — they are the bearers of this dependency disposition.

proposal.utterance: Fixed and eternal things are the proximate causes of all things.

entities.label: FixedAndEternalThing
entities.rationale: In Spinoza's TEI, 'fixed and eternal things' are a class of entities distinguished from finite/mutable modes. They persist with necessary existence and are not mere mental constructs. Independent continuant is the most defensible BFO parent because they are self-standing, non-inhering entities. They overlap conceptually with Substance/God but are also said to include their universal essences; modeling as a class under BFO_0000004 is the conservative choice.

entities.label: ProximateCausation
entities.rationale: The causal relationship between fixed/eternal things and all particular things is a process (or process class) in BFO terms — an occurrent unfolding by which particulars are brought about or determined. Proximate causation is a sub-type of causal process distinct from the already-modeled DeterminingRelation (which models the modal determination between modes). A separate class is warranted to capture the specific proximate causal direction asserted here.

entities.label: ProximalCauseRole
entities.rationale: The assertion that fixed and eternal things are the proximate causes of all things assigns them a relational, externally-grounded functional role — exactly what BFO Role captures. The role inheres in bearers of class FixedAndEternalThing and is realized in instances of ProximateCausation.

relations.rationale: ProximalCauseRole is a subclass of BFO Role.
FixedAndEternalThing is a subclass of independent continuant.
ProximateCausation is a subclass of process.
The ProximalCauseRole is realized in instances of ProximateCausation — the causal activity that brings particulars about.
Instances of FixedAndEternalThing bear the ProximalCauseRole; expressed as a subclass axiom: FixedAndEternalThing rdfs:subClassOf (bearer_of some ProximalCauseRole).

open_questions: Should FixedAndEternalThing be modeled as a subclass of the existing working:Substance class, given that in Spinoza fixed and eternal things are sometimes read as infinite modes or as God/Substance itself, or should they remain a sibling class under BFO_0000004?

Are 'fixed and eternal things' meant here to include only God/Substance, or also the infinite modes (such as motion-and-rest, infinite intellect)? This would affect whether God (the existing individual) is typed as a FixedAndEternalThing.

proposal.utterance: The essence of singular things is determined by fixed and eternal things and their laws.

entities.label: SingularThing
entities.rationale: Singular things (res singulares) in Spinoza are finite, individually existing entities — paradigmatically independent continuants with determinate essence.

entities.label: FixedAndEternalThing
entities.rationale: The 'fixed and eternal things' (res fixae et aeternae) of the TEI are universal, eternal causal-structural entities — modeled as a subclass of independent continuant distinct from singular finite things.

entities.label: EternalLaw
entities.rationale: The 'laws' of fixed and eternal things are universal, abstract informational patterns — correctly typed as generically dependent continuants (information content / normative structures).

entities.label: EssenceDetermination
entities.rationale: The determination of essence is a causal/structural process — subclassing the existing DeterminingRelation process class, which was already introduced for similar ontological determination.

entities.label: SingularEssence
entities.rationale: The essence of a singular thing, as what is determined by fixed and eternal things, is a specifically dependent quality inhering in the singular thing.

relations.rationale: The singular essence inheres in a singular thing (specifically dependent on it as bearer).
The essence-determination process has the singular thing as participant (its essence is what is being determined).
Fixed and eternal things participate as the determiners in the essence-determination process.
The laws are part of (or expressed by) the fixed and eternal things — they are the normative-informational aspect of those structural entities.
Eternal laws co-participate in the essence-determination process alongside the fixed and eternal things themselves.
Singular things are independent continuants.
Fixed and eternal things are independent continuants of a universal, eternal structural kind.

open_questions: Should 'FixedAndEternalThing' be related to the existing 'working:Substance' class (as infinite modes or attributes of God/Substance), or kept as a distinct category?

Should 'SingularEssence' be related to the existing 'working:EssentialExistenceQuality'? Spinoza sometimes links essence to necessary existence, but here 'singular' things are finite — clarification of scope would help.

Are the 'laws' (EternalLaw) best modeled as part of FixedAndEternalThing (BFO_0000050), or as a separate generically dependent continuant that is 'about' those things? The relationship is metaphysically close but ontologically distinct.

Should 'EssenceDetermination' be understood as a synchronic structural dependency (disposition/disposition-realization) rather than a temporal causal process? If so, it might be better typed as BFO_0000016 (Disposition) or a constraint.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance (from Spinoza's Treatise on the Emendation of the Intellect, §101) asserts that the essence of singular (finite, particular) things is determined by fixed and eternal universal things and their laws. This introduces four new ontological commitments: (1) a class of SingularThings as independent continuants; (2) a class of FixedAndEternalThings as a distinct kind of independent continuant; (3) EternalLaws as generically dependent continuants that are the normative-structural expressions of those eternal things; and (4) EssenceDetermination as a determining process (subclassing existing DeterminingRelation) in which fixed and eternal things and their laws causally/structurally fix what the essence of singular things is. The SingularEssence quality inheres in singular things and is what gets determined. Relations connect these via BFO participation and inherence predicates. Several open questions are flagged regarding the placement of FixedAndEternalThing relative to existing Substance/God individuals and whether determination here is better modeled processually or dispositionally.

proposal.utterance: False thoughts will be uncovered by the mind's attempt to deduce consequences from them.

entities.label: FalseThought
entities.rationale: A false thought is a kind of idea (generically dependent continuant, a pattern of content that can be entertained by a mind), specifically one whose content does not accurately represent its object. It is a subclass of the existing working:Idea class.

entities.label: ConsequenceDeductionProcess
entities.rationale: The mind's act of attempting to deduce consequences from a thought is a process (an occurrent unfolding in time). This captures the epistemic activity described in the utterance.

entities.label: FalsehoodRevealedByDeduction
entities.rationale: This is a specific propositional/epistemic constraint asserted by the utterance: that the falseness of a thought is revealed (uncovered) when the mind attempts to deduce consequences from it. Modeled as a generically dependent continuant (a content-bearing constraint or principle), parallel to existing individuals like IncompatibilityOfClearDistinctPerceptionWithFeigning.

relations.rationale: A false thought is a species of idea, inheriting its GDC typing.
Deduction of consequences is a process (occurrent).
The principle that falseness is revealed through deduction is a generically dependent continuant (a representational/epistemic content item).
This principle is part of the broader false-vs-fictitious distinction already in the ontology; the utterance elaborates a criterion by which falseness (as opposed to fiction) is detectable.

open_questions: Should 'ConsequenceDeductionProcess' have the Intellect or a mind-bearer as its required participant? We could assert that instances of ConsequenceDeductionProcess must have a participant of type working:Intellect.

Is the 'uncovering' here meant as a logical/necessary result (i.e., a disposition of FalseThought to be revealed when consequences are drawn), or merely a contingent epistemic heuristic? If necessary, we should model it as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) on FalseThought.

Should FalseThought be distinguished from fictitious thought (which is already partially addressed by FalseVsFictitiousDistinction)? The utterance seems to apply specifically to false thoughts, not fictitious ones.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts an epistemic principle from Spinoza's theory of mind: false thoughts are distinguishable from fictitious or true ones because attempting to derive consequences from them reveals their falseness. Three new entities are proposed: (1) FalseThought as a subclass of working:Idea (a GDC), since false thoughts are a kind of idea with incorrect representational content; (2) ConsequenceDeductionProcess as a BFO Process, capturing the act of deriving consequences from a thought; and (3) FalsehoodRevealedByDeduction as an individual propositional/epistemic constraint (GDC), parallel to the many existing constraint-individuals in the ontology. The new individual is linked via BFO_0000050 (part of) to the existing FalseVsFictitiousDistinction individual, since this principle elaborates how false thoughts are identified and thus forms part of the broader distinction between false and fictitious content.

proposal.utterance: True thoughts generate continuous deduction of further true thoughts.

entities.label: TrueThought
entities.rationale: A true thought in Spinoza's sense is an idea that adequately represents its object; it is an information-bearing pattern (GDC) and a species of ClearAndDistinctIdea already in the ontology.

entities.label: DeductiveInferenceProcess
entities.rationale: The continuous derivation of further true thoughts from an initial true thought is a temporally extended happening — a deductive inference process.

entities.label: DeductiveProductivity
entities.rationale: The capacity of a true thought to generate further true thoughts is an internally grounded, realizable property — a disposition inhering in the true thought.

entities.label: TrueThoughtGenerationConstraint
entities.rationale: The propositional content that 'true thoughts continuously generate further true thoughts' is an information entity (GDC) — a Spinozistic epistemic principle comparable to other constraint-individuals already in the ontology.

relations.rationale: A true thought is a species of clear and distinct idea, already modelled as a GDC class.
DeductiveProductivity is a disposition (internally grounded realizable entity).
The disposition DeductiveProductivity is realized in a DeductiveInferenceProcess.
True thoughts participate in (are outputs of) the deductive inference process.
The constraint is an information-bearing GDC individual parallel to other epistemic-constraint individuals in the ontology.

open_questions: Should 'true thought' be modelled as a subclass of ClearAndDistinctIdea specifically, or directly under Idea? Spinoza does treat adequate ideas and true ideas as closely related but not always identical.

Is the 'continuous' character of the deduction intended to encode an infinite regress/chain, or simply that the process is iterative? This may affect whether we need a part-of chain of DeductiveInferenceProcess instances.
Should DeductiveProductivity be constrained to inhere only in TrueThought individuals, or in any Idea? (Spinoza argues only adequate/true ideas are genuinely productive.)
Is the utterance quoting or summarising a specific proposition in the Ethics or TreatiseOnEmendationOfIntellect? Linking to that source individual would strengthen provenance.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance encodes a Spinozistic epistemic principle: true (adequate) thoughts possess a generative power that produces further true thoughts via continuous deduction. Ontologically this involves three new classes — TrueThought (a GDC subclass of ClearAndDistinctIdea, the information-bearing pattern), DeductiveProductivity (a Disposition inhering in true thoughts, realizable in the inference process), and DeductiveInferenceProcess (the BFO Process in which that disposition is realized and whose outputs are further TrueThought instances) — plus one new individual (TrueThoughtGenerationConstraint) encoding the propositional principle itself, following the pattern already established for epistemic-constraint GDC individuals in the ontology. Key BFO relations used are rdfs:subClassOf, BFO_0000054 (realized in), and RO_0000057 (has participant).

proposal.utterance: Method is reflexive knowledge itself.

entities.label: Method
entities.rationale: In Spinoza's TEI, 'method' is the reflexive capacity of the intellect to know itself and its own power of forming clear ideas. This is best typed as a Disposition (BFO_0000016): an internally-grounded capacity that inheres in the intellect and is realized in the process of self-knowing. It is a class because it designates a kind of capacity.

entities.label: ReflexiveKnowledge
entities.rationale: Reflexive knowledge (the intellect's knowledge of itself and its own activity) is a generically dependent continuant — a cognitive content that can be instantiated and transmitted. It is a subtype of ClearAndDistinctIdea (already in the ontology), since Spinoza treats reflexive self-knowledge as the paradigm case of clear and distinct cognition.

entities.label: ReflexiveKnowledgeProcess
entities.rationale: The realization of method as reflexive knowledge requires a process — the intellect's act of turning on itself. This process class captures the unfolding of that self-directed cognition.

entities.label: MethodIsReflexiveKnowledgeConstraint
entities.rationale: The propositional content of Spinoza's claim that 'method is reflexive knowledge itself' is an information artifact — a generically dependent continuant expressing an identity constraint between Method and ReflexiveKnowledge, analogous to other constraint individuals already in the ontology (e.g. IncompatibilityOfSimplicityWithFeigning).

relations.rationale: Method is a disposition — an internally-grounded capacity of the intellect.
Reflexive self-knowledge is the paradigm of clear and distinct ideas for Spinoza.
Method (as disposition) is realized in the process of reflexive self-knowing.
The reflexive knowledge process realizes the disposition called Method.

proposal.utterance: The intellect perceives things under a species of eternity and infinite number, not under duration.

entities.label: SpeciesOfEternity
entities.rationale: The 'species of eternity' (sub specie aeternitatis) is a mode of perception or framing under which the intellect grasps things — it is an internally grounded capacity/disposition of the intellect, not a quality of the thing perceived. Typed as Disposition (BFO_0000016).

entities.label: SpeciesOfInfiniteNumber
entities.rationale: Parallel to SpeciesOfEternity, perceiving under 'infinite number' is another framing disposition of the intellect — an internally grounded capacity for how it apprehends things.

entities.label: Duration
entities.rationale: Duration in Spinoza is a measurable, temporally bounded quality of finite things — their persistence through time as opposed to eternity. Best typed as Quality (BFO_0000019) since it is a property that inheres in finite continuants.

entities.label: IntellectualPerceptionUnderEternity
entities.rationale: The act of the intellect perceiving things sub specie aeternitatis is an occurrent — a process in which the intellect participates. Typed as Process (BFO_0000015).

entities.label: DurationBasedPerception
entities.rationale: Perception under duration is the contrasting mode of apprehension (associated with imagination/finite knowledge), also a process, distinct from intellectual perception under eternity.

entities.label: IntellectPerceivesUnderEternityConstraint
entities.rationale: The propositional content asserting that the intellect perceives things under a species of eternity and infinite number, not under duration, is an information artifact — a generically dependent continuant (a claim/constraint in the philosophical work).

relations.rationale: Sub specie aeternitatis is a mode/method of intellectual perception — a species of the Method class already in the ontology, which is itself a Disposition.
Perceiving under infinite number is likewise a methodological/dispositional framing of the intellect, subclassing Method.
The process of perceiving under eternity has the Intellect as participant.

I introduce SpeciesOfEternity and SpeciesOfInfiniteNumber as Disposition subclasses of the existing Method class (both are internally grounded perceptual framings of the intellect), Duration as a Quality (a property of finite modes that the intellect does not use as its framing), and two process classes for the contrasting modes of apprehension. The propositional content of the claim is captured as a generically dependent continuant individual (IntellectPerceivesUnderEternityConstraint), consistent with how similar doctrinal items are typed in the existing ontology. The existing Intellect, Finitude, and Method individuals/classes are reused to anchor new entities.

proposal.utterance: Clear and distinct ideas depend on our power alone; confused ideas are often formed against our will.

entities.label: DependenceOnOwnPower
entities.rationale: The claim that clear and distinct ideas depend on our power alone describes an intrinsic dispositional feature of the cognitive agent — the capacity/disposition to produce such ideas autonomously. This is internally grounded and thus a Disposition.

entities.label: VoluntaryIdeaFormationDisposition
entities.rationale: A subtype of IdeaFormationCapacity capturing the specifically voluntary, agent-controlled production of clear and distinct ideas. Disposition because it is internally grounded in the intellect's power.

entities.label: InvoluntaryIdeaFormationDisposition
entities.rationale: A subtype of IdeaFormationCapacity capturing the involuntary, will-independent formation of confused ideas. The fact that confused ideas are often formed against our will marks a distinct dispositional profile.

entities.label: ConfusedIdea
entities.rationale: Contrasted explicitly with ClearAndDistinctIdea in the utterance. A confused idea is an informational/representational content — a generically dependent continuant — that lacks the clarity and distinctness property.

entities.label: ClearAndDistinctIdea
entities.rationale: Already exists in the ontology; reused here as the subject of the dependence-on-power claim.

entities.label: AgentCognitivePower
entities.rationale: The utterance refers to 'our power' as the sole determinant of clear and distinct ideas. This is an intrinsic dispositional capacity of a cognitive agent — its power of intellect — best typed as Disposition.

entities.label: AgentWill
entities.rationale: 'Our will' is referenced as the faculty that confused ideas can be formed against. Typed as Disposition (internally grounded volitional capacity of a cognitive agent).

entities.label: ClearIdeasDependOnPowerConstraint
entities.rationale: The propositional content asserting that clear and distinct ideas depend on the agent's power alone — an information artifact / theoretical constraint parallel to other constraint individuals already in the ontology (e.g., NecessaryClarityAndDistinctnessConstraint).

entities.label: ConfusedIdeasFormedAgainstWillConstraint
entities.rationale: The propositional content asserting that confused ideas are often formed against the agent's will — a theoretical constraint analogous to existing constraint individuals.

Involuntary formation is a species of IdeaFormationCapacity.

ClearAndDistinctIdea is also a subkind of Idea — making the contrast explicit in the taxonomy.

The utterance says confused ideas are formed 'often' (not always) against the will — should InvoluntaryIdeaFormationDisposition carry a frequency/probabilistic quality, or is a simpler subclass relation sufficient?
Is 'power' (potentia) here the same construct as InnateCapacity, or should it be a distinct class to capture Spinoza's technical sense of potentia versus potestas?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts two correlated claims from Spinoza's epistemology: (1) clear and distinct ideas are produced through the agent's own power alone — marking their voluntary, self-determined character — and (2) confused ideas are often formed against the agent's will — marking their involuntary, externally-conditioned character. I model these as: two new constraint-content individuals (parallel to existing constraint individuals in the ontology); new classes ConfusedIdea (subclass of existing Idea) and ClearAndDistinctIdea (already present, now explicitly subclassed under Idea); new disposition classes VoluntaryIdeaFormationDisposition and InvoluntaryIdeaFormationDisposition as subtypes of the existing IdeaFormationCapacity; and new disposition classes AgentCognitivePower and AgentWill as subtypes of existing InnateCapacity. The dependence relation is captured via DependenceOnOwnPower as a disposition subclass. All typings respect BFO 2020 by placing informational/propositional contents under BFO_0000031 and cognitive faculties/powers under BFO_0000016.

proposal.utterance: The mind can determine ideas in multiple ways.

entities.label: MindEntity
entities.rationale: The mind is a substantive entity (independent continuant) whose instances bear capacities and ideas; it is distinct from but related to Intellect and Imagination already in the ontology.

entities.label: IdeaDeterminationCapacity
entities.rationale: The capacity of the mind to determine ideas in multiple ways is an internally grounded disposition inhering in the mind. This is distinct from IdeaFormationCapacity (which concerns forming ideas) and covers the directional/modal determination aspect.

entities.label: IdeaDeterminationProcess
entities.rationale: The actual determining of ideas by the mind is a process (occurrent) in which the mind participates; the utterance implies multiple such processes are possible.

relations.rationale: Determining ideas is a more specific kind of idea-related capacity already in the ontology; subclassing IdeaFormationCapacity maintains hierarchy without redundancy.
Determination of ideas is a subtype of the idea formation process already present in the ontology.
The capacity is realized in the determination process, per BFO realizable-in-process relation.
Mind is an independent continuant (bearer of dispositions and ideas).
BFO typing: this capacity is a disposition (internally grounded realizable entity).

open_questions: Is 'mind' here Spinoza's attribute of Thought (which would make it closer to an attribute/mode of the one Substance), or a generic cognitive entity? This affects whether MindEntity should be a kind of Mode or an independent continuant.

What are the 'multiple ways' referred to? If these correspond to specific existing modes of perception (e.g., FourthModeOfPerception) or to AbsoluteIdeaFormation vs. DeterminateIdeaFormation, we could assert specific subclasses of IdeaDeterminationProcess rather than leaving the multiplicity implicit.
Should IdeaDeterminationCapacity be a subclass of IdeaFormationCapacity, or is it better treated as a sibling (both under BFO_0000016)? The semantic overlap is significant.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts that the mind (a substantive cognitive entity) possesses the capacity to determine ideas in multiple ways. This introduces three new ontological commitments: (1) MindEntity as a class of independent continuants bearing cognitive capacities, (2) IdeaDeterminationCapacity as the disposition through which this multi-way determination is possible—subclassed under the existing IdeaFormationCapacity—and (3) IdeaDeterminationProcess as the occurrent in which that capacity is realized, subclassed under the existing IdeaFormationProcess. The existing DeterminationByOtherIdeas individual and the AbsoluteIdeaFormation/DeterminateIdeaFormation classes are related but model specific sub-types; the new classes provide the general framework for the mind's plural determination of ideas. Open questions concern whether 'mind' here is a Spinozistic mode of Thought (which would affect its BFO typing) and whether the multiple ways map to already-existing individuals or require further enumeration.

proposal.utterance: More perfect ideas express greater perfection of their objects.

entities.label: IdeaPerfection
entities.rationale: The degree of perfection of an idea is a measurable quality inhering in that idea (a generically dependent continuant). Perfection-as-degree is a Quality in BFO.

entities.label: ObjectPerfection
entities.rationale: The degree of perfection of the object expressed by an idea is likewise a Quality, inhering in the object entity. Spinoza treats perfection as a graded property of things.

entities.label: ExpressingRelation
entities.rationale: The 'expressing' of an object's perfection by an idea is a representational/semantic process connecting the idea (GDC) to its object. Modelled as a subclass of Process to capture the dynamic, relational expressing act.

entities.label: IdeaPerfectionObjectPerfectionProportionalityConstraint
entities.rationale: The claim 'more perfect ideas express greater perfection of their objects' is a propositional/informational content — a constraint or principle that can be copied and instantiated in multiple material substrates. It is a generically dependent continuant (an informational content entity / proposition).

relations.rationale: The constraint individual is typed as a generically dependent continuant (informational content).
IdeaPerfection is a Quality subclass.
ObjectPerfection is a Quality subclass.
Idea-perfection inheres in an Idea (already an existing class in the ontology).
ExpressingRelation is typed as a Process.
An expressing process has the Idea as participant (the thing doing the expressing).

open_questions: Should 'object' here be restricted to a particular BFO type? In Spinoza the 'object of an idea' (ideatum) can be a material entity, another idea, or a mode — should we mint an 'Ideatum' class or use an existing one?

Is 'perfection' in the Spinozistic sense a univocal Quality, or should it be modelled as a Disposition (the capacity to express more reality)? Spinoza sometimes treats perfection/reality as near-synonyms.
Should IdeaPerfectionObjectPerfectionProportionalityConstraint be linked to a specific text location (e.g., within TheEthics or TreatiseOnEmendationOfIntellect) via a part-of or citation relation?

Is ExpressingRelation the right model for 'express'? Alternatively, expressing could be treated as a formal-ontological relation (like 'represents') rather than a process — should we use a custom object property instead?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance encodes a Spinozistic proportionality principle: the perfection-quality of an idea covaries with the perfection-quality of its object. I mint two Quality subclasses (IdeaPerfection, ObjectPerfection) to capture the graded perfection properties on each side; an ExpressingRelation Process to model the idea-to-object expressing relation (since 'expressing' in Spinoza is a dynamic, representational-causal link, best treated as a process rather than a static quality); and an individual IdeaPerfectionObjectPerfectionProportionalityConstraint as a generically dependent continuant (informational content entity) encoding the proportionality claim itself. IdeaPerfection is anchored via RO_0000052 to the existing Idea class. Several modelling choices — the BFO type of the ideatum, whether perfection is a Quality or Disposition, and whether 'expressing' warrants a process or a pure relation — are flagged as open questions.

proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance encodes a Spinozistic proportionality principle: the perfection-quality of an idea covaries with the perfection-quality of its object. proposal.utterance: False and fictitious ideas have no positive content; they are only defects of knowledge.

entities.label: FalseIdea
entities.rationale: A false idea is a kind of Idea (generically dependent continuant) whose defining characteristic is absence of positive content — it is a defect in the informational structure of knowledge.

entities.label: FictitiousIdea
entities.rationale: A fictitious idea is a kind of Idea (generically dependent continuant) that similarly lacks positive content and constitutes a defect of knowledge. Already distinguished from false ideas via FalseVsFictitiousDistinction individual.

entities.label: AbsenceOfPositiveContent
entities.rationale: The claim that false/fictitious ideas have 'no positive content' is best captured as a quality (a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in an idea) whose value is absence/zero positive informational content.

entities.label: KnowledgeDefect
entities.rationale: The utterance characterizes false and fictitious ideas as 'defects of knowledge' — a quality (privation) that inheres in those ideas, capturing the epistemological privation claim.

entities.label: AbsenceOfPositiveContentConstraint
entities.rationale: The propositional content 'false and fictitious ideas have no positive content; they are only defects of knowledge' is a specific constraint/principle in Spinoza's epistemology, modeled as a generically dependent continuant (an information artifact/principle) parallel to other constraint individuals in the ontology.
