proposal.utterance: Substance is a principle of all its modes.

entities.label: SubstancePrincipalCausation
entities.rationale: The claim that Substance is a principle of all its modes expresses an internally-grounded causal-explanatory capacity of Substance with respect to its modes. This is best modeled as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) — a power inhering in Substance by virtue of which modes are produced/grounded. It is not a mere role (externally grounded) but an intrinsic ground, hence Disposition over Role.

entities.label: ModePrincipleRelation
entities.rationale: The actualization of Substance being a principle of its modes — i.e., the causal/grounding process by which modes are produced from Substance — is an occurrent, a Process in BFO. This complements the Disposition (SubstancePrincipalCausation) as the process in which that disposition is realized.

relations.rationale: SubstancePrincipalCausation is a more specific form of SubstanceProductionConstraint — both are dispositions capturing how Substance grounds/produces its modes, but SubstancePrincipalCausation specifically captures the principial (archê) relationship.
This disposition inheres in Substance as its bearer — it is Substance that bears the capacity to be the principle of its modes.
The ModePrincipleRelation process realizes the SubstancePrincipalCausation disposition — when Substance acts as principle of its modes, that disposition is being realized in that process.
Substance participates (as the principial cause) in the ModePrincipleRelation process.
Modes (as a class) participate in the ModePrincipleRelation process as the entities grounded/produced by Substance.

open_questions: Should 'principle' here be understood in a strictly efficient-causal sense (Substance produces modes), or also in an immanent/formal sense (modes exist in Substance as their ontological ground)? This affects whether ModePrincipleRelation should be a subclass of DeterminingRelation or GodCausesAllThingsProcess, or kept separate.

Is this claim meant to apply specifically to God/the one Substance (the individual 'God'), or is it a general schema for any Substance? If the former, we should add an assertion that God bears SubstancePrincipalCausation.

In Spinoza's framework, modes inhere in Substance (like SDCs in a bearer). Should we also assert that Mode rdfs:subClassOf BFO_0000020 with inheres-in pointing to Substance as bearer, to capture the ontological dependency structurally?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance 'Substance is a principle of all its modes' encodes a fundamental Spinozistic metaphysical claim: Substance is the causal and ontological ground from which all modes derive. In BFO terms, this is best modeled as (1) a Disposition (SubstancePrincipalCausation) inhering in Substance — capturing its intrinsic causal-principial power over modes — and (2) a Process (ModePrincipleRelation) in which that disposition is realized, taking both Substance and Mode as participants. SubstancePrincipalCausation is typed as a subclass of the existing SubstanceProductionConstraint, since principial causation is a specific form of Substance's productive capacity. The relations wire the disposition to its bearer (Substance), the process to its realizable, and both Substance and Mode as participants in the process. Three open questions are flagged: the precise sense of 'principle', whether to scope this to the God individual, and whether Mode's inherence in Substance should be made explicit structurally.

proposal.utterance: God exists outside nothing; nothing exists outside God.

entities.label: OmnipresenceOfGod
entities.rationale: God's omnipresence (nothing exists outside God) is a quality inhering in God as an independent continuant; it is a positive attribute of God's substance.

entities.label: GodExistsOutsideNothingQuality
entities.rationale: The claim that God exists outside nothing is a quality of God expressing His absolute, unconditioned, non-limited existence — complementary to omnipresence but capturing the asymmetry that God is not bounded or contained by anything external.

entities.label: GodContainsAllThingsQuality
entities.rationale: The positive side of 'nothing exists outside God' can also be represented as a quality expressing that all existence is contained within or is part of God (immanence / pantheist containment).

relations.rationale: Omnipresence inheres in God as its sole bearer.
The quality of existing outside nothing inheres in God.
The quality that all things are contained within God inheres in God.
God is the bearer of His omnipresence.
God is the bearer of the quality of existing outside nothing.
God is the bearer of the quality of containing all things.

The quality that nothing exists outside God is closely related to (part of the complex of) God's disposition to cause all things; this links the containment claim to the existing GodCausesAllThings disposition.

open_questions: Should 'GodExistsOutsideNothingQuality' and 'GodContainsAllThingsQuality' be merged into a single 'OmnipresenceOfGod' quality, given that in Spinoza's monism 'nothing outside God' and 'God is everywhere' are two sides of the same proposition?

Is the intended scope Spinozist (God = Natura, pantheist containment) or classical theist (God transcends creation)? The ontological modelling differs: Spinoza's God contains all modes as parts, while classical theism would resist the BFO part-of relation between God and world.
Should we assert that working:WholeOfNature and working:God share the same individual (sameAs) to capture the Spinozist identity, or keep them distinct individuals related by a role?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance makes two reciprocal claims: (1) God is not contained by or limited to any external nothing — He exists entirely outside any nullity or vacuum; (2) everything that exists is within or part of God — no being stands outside Him. Both claims are ontological qualities of God as an independent continuant individual. I model them as three quality individuals inhering in working:God via RO_0000052/RO_0000053: OmnipresenceOfGod (the positive spatial/existential pervasiveness), GodExistsOutsideNothingQuality (the negative — no external limit or void constrains God), and GodContainsAllThingsQuality (the positive containment of all existents within God). All three are typed as BFO_0000019 Quality and subsumed under the existing working:DivineAttribute class. A weak part-of link connects GodContainsAllThingsQuality to the existing GodCausesAllThings disposition to maintain coherence with prior assertions. Open questions flag the Spinoza vs. classical theism interpretation and potential individual merging.

proposal.utterance: God is an immanent cause, not a transitive cause, of his effects.

entities.label: TransitiveCauseRole
entities.rationale: A transitive cause is an externally-grounded functional role that a thing can bear; Spinoza contrasts it with immanent causation. Modeling as a Role class allows the ontology to assert that God does NOT bear this role.

entities.label: GodImmanentCauseRoleRealization
entities.rationale: The immanent causation of God's effects is a process (an occurrent unfolding) in which the GodImmanentCauseRole is realized. This individual represents that happening.

relations.rationale: God (the individual) bears the existing GodImmanentCauseRole individual, asserting his immanent-cause status.
The immanent cause role is realized in the process of God causing all things immanently.
God participates in the immanent causation process as its agent/bearer.
TransitiveCauseRole is a subclass of BFO Role; Spinoza explicitly denies God bears this kind of role.

open_questions: Should we assert an explicit OWL disjointness or negation axiom to encode that God does NOT bear any instance of TransitiveCauseRole? OWL 2 can express this with a class complement restriction, but it goes beyond BFO relation triples.

Is 'transitive cause' here Spinoza's own term (causa transiens) contrasted with causa immanens? If so, should we add a skos:note linking to Ethics IP18?
proposal.rationale_summary: Ethics IP18 states 'God is the immanent, not the transient, cause of all things.' The ontology already has GodImmanentCauseRole and GodCausesAllThingsProcess. The main new commitment is (1) introducing TransitiveCauseRole as a class so we can formally contrast it with the immanent cause role, and (2) minting a process individual for the realization of immanent causation. The existing GodImmanentCauseRole individual is linked to God via RO_0000053 (bearer of) and to the new realization process via BFO_0000054 (realized in). Asserting that God does NOT bear TransitiveCauseRole requires a negation axiom that goes beyond simple BFO triples, so this is flagged as an open question for the human to decide whether to add an OWL complement restriction.

proposal.utterance: An immanent cause's effects remain united with the cause and form a whole with it.

entities.label: ImmanentCausalUnity
entities.rationale: The state of effects remaining united with their immanent cause is a quality (a property that inheres in the whole formed by cause and effects). It is a measurable/discernible property of that whole, grounding it as a Quality subclass.

entities.label: CauseEffectWhole
entities.rationale: The 'whole' formed by an immanent cause together with its effects is an independent continuant — a composite entity with parts (the cause and the effects). It has material/substantial existence in Spinoza's framework.

entities.label: ImmanentCausalUnification
entities.rationale: The process by which an immanent cause produces effects that remain united with it, forming a whole — this is an occurrent, a happening in time (even if atemporal for God in Spinoza). It is modeled as a subclass of Process.

relations.rationale: Immanent causal unification is a species of determining relation — the cause determines the effects while remaining united with them. DeterminingRelation already exists as a Process subclass.

In Spinoza's framework God/Substance as immanent cause has parts that include the effects (modes), so CauseEffectWhole has Substance as a part. Using hasPart (BFO_0000051) relationally at the class level captures that the whole includes the cause (Substance).
Remaining united with effects is a quality of the immanent cause (God/Substance), making it a species of DivineAttribute — a quality inhering in the divine substance.
The existing GodImmanentCauseRole individual (a Role) is realized in processes of ImmanentCausalUnification — the role is manifested when God produces effects that remain united with it.

open_questions: Should CauseEffectWhole be treated as an individual (e.g. WholeOfNature, which already exists) rather than a class, since in Spinoza there is only one such whole?

Is ImmanentCausalUnity better typed as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) — the tendency of the cause to retain effects within itself — rather than a Quality? The distinction matters for whether it is intrinsic structure vs. measurable property.
Should ImmanentCausalUnification be made a subclass of GodCausesAllThings (the existing disposition) or kept as a separate Process subtype of DeterminingRelation?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts a structural claim about immanent causation: effects do not separate from their cause but instead form a whole with it. This introduces three new ontological items. First, a quality class ImmanentCausalUnity capturing the property of cause-effect unity that inheres in the whole. Second, a class CauseEffectWhole — the composite independent continuant formed by cause plus its retained effects (closely related to, and possibly identical with, the existing WholeOfNature individual). Third, a process class ImmanentCausalUnification for the happening in which the cause produces and retains its effects. The existing individual GodImmanentCauseRole is linked via 'realized in' to this process class, and ImmanentCausalUnity is typed as a subclass of DivineAttribute since it characterizes God/Substance as immanent cause. Key open questions concern whether CauseEffectWhole collapses into the existing WholeOfNature individual and whether the unity quality is better a Disposition.

proposal.utterance: The essence of a thing does not increase through its union with another thing to form a whole.

entities.label: EssencePreservationUnderUnion
entities.rationale: The claim that the essence of a thing does not increase through union with another thing is best modeled as a disposition or constraint: each thing has an internal disposition such that its essence is invariant under composition with other things. This is a generically grounded, internally rooted tendency (hence Disposition) of any finite thing's essence to remain unchanged by part-whole relations.

entities.label: EssenceInvariance
entities.rationale: The invariance of essence under union is a quality that inheres in a thing: at any time, the essence of a thing has a fixed character that does not increase when the thing is joined to another to form a whole.

entities.label: WholeFormationProcess
entities.rationale: The union of two things to form a whole is an occurrent process. The axiom says that during/after this process, the essence of a participating thing does not increase.

relations.rationale: EssencePreservationUnderUnion is a subclass of Disposition (BFO_0000016), as it is internally grounded in each thing's essence.
EssenceInvariance is a subclass of Quality (BFO_0000019), inhering in a thing and expressing the fixed, non-increasing character of its essence.
WholeFormationProcess is a subclass of Process (BFO_0000015), representing the occurrent event of two things joining to form a whole.

The disposition EssencePreservationUnderUnion is realized in (or contra-realized in) a WholeFormationProcess, meaning that during such a process the essence of a participant does not increase — the disposition manifests (or is tested) in this process type.
Instances of FiniteSingularThing bear the quality EssenceInvariance, since the axiom applies to finite things whose essence does not grow under composition.

open_questions: Is this axiom intended to apply universally to all things (including God/Substance) or only to finite singular things (modes)? In Spinoza, Substance has a different relationship to essence than finite modes do.

Should EssenceInvariance be treated as a constraint on part-whole relations (BFO_0000050/BFO_0000051), or is it better framed as a quality that inheres in each finite thing independently of its mereological context?
Is 'essence' here to be mapped to EternalInfiniteEssence (already in the ontology) or to a distinct class representing the essence of finite things?
Should WholeFormationProcess be linked to an existing composition or aggregation concept, or is a new class sufficient?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance expresses a metaphysical axiom from Spinoza (Ethics I, Axiom 5 or related propositions): the essence of a thing is not augmented by its joining with another thing into a whole. This commits the ontology to three new constructs: (1) EssenceInvariance, a quality inhering in things that tracks their fixed essence under mereological operations; (2) EssencePreservationUnderUnion, a disposition capturing the internal groundedness of this invariance; and (3) WholeFormationProcess, a process class representing the event of two things composing into a whole. The disposition is realized in (or tested by) whole-formation processes. FiniteSingularThing individuals are the primary bearers of EssenceInvariance, since the claim most directly targets finite modes in Spinoza's system, though an open question remains about whether it also applies to Substance/God. No existing individuals or classes are reused, as no prior class adequately captures essence-invariance-under-composition.

proposal.utterance: All attributes depending on no other cause and requiring no genus to define them belong to God's essence.

entities.label: CausalIndependenceQuality
entities.rationale: A quality of an attribute: that it depends on no external cause. This is a measurable/ascribable property inhering in an attribute. Subclass of DivineAttribute since it characterizes divine attributes specifically.

entities.label: GenusIndependenceQuality
entities.rationale: A quality of an attribute: that it requires no genus (superordinate kind) for its definition — i.e., it is self-defining. Inheres in attributes constitutive of God's essence.

entities.label: AttributeBelongingToGodEssence
entities.rationale: The disposition of an attribute to constitute or belong to God's essence, grounded internally in the attribute's causal independence and genus-independence. Realized when God's essence is formally expressed.

entities.label: GodEssenceConstitutionProcess
entities.rationale: The process by which attributes, meeting the criteria of causal and genus independence, are realized as constitutive of God's essence. Realizes the AttributeBelongingToGodEssence disposition.

relations.rationale: Causal independence is a specific sub-type of the divine attribute quality.
Genus-independence is a specific sub-type of the divine attribute quality.
The disposition of an attribute to belong to God's essence is realized in the process of God's essence constitution.
God participates as the bearer-entity in the process by which divine essence is constituted through causally and genus-independent attributes.

Belonging to God's essence is closely related to the EssentialExistenceQuality already in the ontology — however, since it is a disposition here (internally grounded in the attribute's independence), we note a conceptual relationship rather than direct subclassing. Modeled as a subclass of Disposition, not Quality; but linking via annotation that it implies EssentialExistenceQuality in God.

open_questions: Spinoza's 'attributes' here are infinite attributes like Thought and Extension — should CausalIndependenceQuality and GenusIndependenceQuality inhere in attribute-individuals (like the existing working:Thought and working:Extension) or in a generic class of divine attributes?

Should 'requiring no genus to define them' be modeled as a disposition (self-defining capacity, akin to SelfConceivability) rather than a quality, given that it describes a definitional capacity rather than a static property?

The last relation (AttributeBelongingToGodEssence subClassOf EssentialExistenceQuality) mixes Disposition and Quality hierarchies — should we instead mint a separate bridge relation or annotation property to express that bearing this disposition entails the EssentialExistenceQuality in God?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance (Spinoza's Ethics, Part I, related to Def. 4 and Prop. 10) asserts a criterion for which attributes belong to God's essence: (1) depending on no other cause, and (2) requiring no genus for their definition. I mint two new Quality subclasses under DivineAttribute to capture these two criteria as inhering properties of attributes. I also mint a Disposition class (AttributeBelongingToGodEssence) to capture the internally-grounded tendency of qualifying attributes to constitute God's essence, and a corresponding Process class for the realization event. Relations tie the disposition to its realization process and to God as participant. The existing individuals working:Thought and working:Extension are the paradigm bearers, though no new individual assertions are made until the user confirms whether those individuals should explicitly bear the new qualities.

proposal.utterance: A whole is a being of reason, differing from a universal in structure of parts.

entities.label: Whole
entities.rationale: A 'whole' in this Spinozistic/rationalist context is a being of reason — a conceptual construct whose identity depends on how parts are grouped by the intellect, not a mind-independent material thing. It is an information-like entity (a way of conceiving things together) that can be instantiated in multiple bearers, fitting BFO's generically dependent continuant. It is a class because 'whole' is a common noun denoting a kind.

entities.label: Universal
entities.rationale: A 'universal' here is likewise a being of reason — an abstract conceptual pattern (e.g. genus, species) formed by the intellect through abstraction. Like a whole, it is a generically dependent continuant: a content-pattern that can be multiply instantiated. It is a class because 'universal' is a common noun denoting a kind.

entities.label: BeingOfReason
entities.rationale: A 'being of reason' (ens rationis) is a concept or construct that exists only in and through an intellect's activity. It is a generically dependent continuant — a representational content that depends generically on some intellect for its existence and can be copied or re-instantiated. Both Whole and Universal are asserted to be subtypes of this class.

entities.label: PartStructureQuality
entities.rationale: The utterance asserts that a Whole and a Universal differ in their 'structure of parts' — i.e., in a measurable, inhering property concerning how parts are organized. This is a quality (specifically-dependent continuant) that inheres in each being-of-reason and whose determinates differ between Whole and Universal.

relations.rationale: The utterance states that a whole is a being of reason.
The utterance contrasts whole with universal, implying universal is likewise a being of reason (standard rationalist doctrine; Spinoza treats both as entia rationis).
Beings of reason are conceptual/representational contents — generically dependent continuants in BFO terms.
Whole is a subclass of BeingOfReason which is a subclass of BFO_0000031; asserting directly for reasoner clarity.
Universal is a subclass of BeingOfReason which is a subclass of BFO_0000031; asserting directly for reasoner clarity.
Part-structure is a quality inhering in a being of reason; it differentiates Whole from Universal.

open_questions: Should Whole and Universal be disjoint classes (they differ in structure of parts, but the utterance does not make exhaustive partition claims — should we assert owl:disjointWith)?

Is 'being of reason' here specifically Spinoza's ens rationis (suggesting we link BeingOfReason to Intellect or TrueIntellect via a dependence relation), or is it used in a more general scholastic sense?
Should PartStructureQuality be further subdivided into WholePartStructureQuality and UniversalPartStructureQuality as two determinate qualities that differentiate the two kinds?

Does 'structure of parts' in this context refer to BFO mereological part-of relations (BFO_0000050), or is it a purely conceptual/logical structure internal to the being of reason? This affects whether we should add mereological axioms.
Should BeingOfReason be linked to the existing Intellect or TrueIntellect individuals via a generic dependence relation (since beings of reason depend on intellects for existence)?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts two ontological claims: (1) a whole is a being of reason (ens rationis), and (2) it differs from a universal in its structure of parts. Both 'whole' and 'universal' are common nouns denoting kinds, so they are classes. In the rationalist tradition Spinoza inherits, beings of reason are conceptual constructs that exist only through intellectual activity — they are not mind-independent material things. BFO's generically dependent continuant (BFO_0000031) is the best fit: these are information-like patterns that depend generically on some bearer (an intellect) and can in principle be multiply instantiated. I mint BeingOfReason as a parent class for both Whole and Universal under BFO_0000031. The difference between them is captured as a PartStructureQuality (BFO Quality), which inheres in each being of reason and whose determinate character differs between the two kinds. Several open questions remain about disjointness, the precise nature of part-structure, and whether to link BeingOfReason to the existing Intellect/TrueIntellect individuals already in the ontology.

proposal.utterance: The effect of an immanent cause cannot perish as long as its cause endures.

entities.label: ImmanentCausePersistenceConstraint
entities.rationale: This disposition inheres in an immanent cause and grounds the necessary persistence of its effects for as long as the cause itself endures. It is internally grounded in the nature of immanent causation (Spinoza Ethics I, P24 Cor. context), making Disposition the appropriate BFO type rather than Role or Quality.

entities.label: EffectPersistenceWhileCauseEndures
entities.rationale: This is a quality of an effect (a finite thing or mode) that it endures contingently on its immanent cause enduring. It is a measurable, bearer-specific property that the effect possesses as long as its cause persists.

entities.label: ImmanentCauseEffectRelation
entities.rationale: The causal nexus between an immanent cause and its effect is best represented as a subclass of DeterminingRelation (already a Process subclass). This class covers the ongoing process by which the immanent cause sustains its effect.

relations.rationale: Immanent cause-effect relations are a species of determining relation already present in the ontology.
The persistence constraint is a disposition inhering in the immanent cause (here God/NaturaNaturans).
This disposition inheres in the bearer that plays the immanent cause role; GodImmanentCauseRole is the existing individual representing God's immanent cause role.
The disposition is realized in processes of immanent cause-effect determination.
Quality borne by modes/effects asserting their persistence conditional on their cause.

open_questions: Should ImmanentCausePersistenceConstraint be modeled as inhering directly in God (the individual) rather than in GodImmanentCauseRole, since strictly speaking dispositions inhere in their bearer, not in roles?
Should EffectPersistenceWhileCauseEndures be a class rather than an individual, since it can be borne by any finite mode/effect, not just one specific entity?

Is the intended scope of this proposition universal (all immanent causes in nature) or specifically about God as sole immanent cause in Spinoza's system? This affects whether the disposition should inhere in God or in a general ImmanentCause class.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts a metaphysical-causal principle: the effect of an immanent cause cannot perish while its cause endures. This introduces three ontological commitments: (1) a disposition (ImmanentCausePersistenceConstraint) grounding the causal necessitation of effect-persistence, inhering in the immanent cause (linked to the existing GodImmanentCauseRole individual); (2) a quality (EffectPersistenceWhileCauseEndures) borne by effects, characterizing their conditional persistence; and (3) a process class (ImmanentCauseEffectRelation) as a subclass of the existing DeterminingRelation, representing the ongoing sustaining causal process. Reuse is maximized via GodImmanentCauseRole and DeterminingRelation. Several open questions remain about scoping and bearer assignment.

proposal.utterance: All other things cannot exist or be understood without God or outside him.

entities.label: OntologicalDependenceOnGod
entities.rationale: The claim that all other things cannot exist without God is best captured as a disposition inhering in finite things (or modes) — a structural dependence on God for both existence and conceivability. Typed as Disposition (BFO_0000016) because it is internally grounded in the nature of the dependent entities.

entities.label: ConceptualDependenceOnGod
entities.rationale: The claim that all other things cannot be understood without God captures an epistemic/conceptual dependence — a disposition of finite things to require God as the conceptual ground for their intelligibility.

entities.label: OntologicalDependenceOnGodClass

entities.label: ConceptualDependenceOnGodClass
entities.rationale: A class-level representation of the disposition of all non-God entities to require God for their intelligibility/conceivability, as a subclass of Disposition.

Should 'cannot exist outside God' be modeled as a constraint (SubstanceProductionConstraint) or as a quality (e.g., InternalityToGodQuality), rather than a disposition?

proposal.rationale_summary: Spinoza's claim (Ethics I, Prop. 15 or related) that all things exist in and are conceived through God alone expresses two linked dependence relations: an existential/ontological one (things cannot exist outside God) and a conceptual one (things cannot be understood without God). I model these as two Disposition individuals inhering in WholeOfNature (the stand-in for all finite/dependent things), under two new Disposition subclasses. This connects naturally to existing individuals GodContainsAllThingsQuality and GodImmanentCauseRole. The class-level entries allow future instances (e.g., specific modes) to bear these dispositions. Open questions flag key ambiguities about bearer identity, the nature of conceptual dependence, and whether a constraint-type model would be more apt.

proposal.utterance: God is an emanative or productive cause of his actions.

entities.label: EmanativeCauseRole
entities.rationale: Spinoza's 'emanative cause' (also called 'productive cause') is an externally-grounded role that God bears in relation to things produced from his nature. Roles in BFO are specifically dependent continuants that are externally grounded, making BFO_0000023 the correct parent. A new class is needed since no existing class captures this distinct causal role.

entities.label: GodEmanativeCauseRole
entities.rationale: The specific instance of EmanativeCauseRole inhering in the individual God. Modelled as an individual role instance that inheres in God, parallel to existing GodFirstCauseRole and GodImmanentCauseRole individuals.

entities.label: EmanativeCausationProcess
entities.rationale: The productive/emanative causal activity of God — the unfolding process by which things flow from God's nature — is an occurrent process. A new class is warranted because existing process classes (DeterminingRelation, GodCausesAllThingsProcess) do not specifically name the emanative/productive character of divine causation.

entities.label: EmanativeCausationDisposition
entities.rationale: The capacity (internally grounded in God's nature) to be an emanative/productive cause is a disposition. This is distinct from the role (externally grounded) and captures the intrinsic basis for emanative causation.

entities.label: GodEmanativeCausationDisposition
entities.rationale: The specific disposition instance inhering in God that grounds his being an emanative/productive cause. Parallel to existing GodCausesAllThings, GodFirstEfficientCauseDisposition, etc.

relations.rationale: GodEmanativeCauseRole is an instance of the class EmanativeCauseRole.
The emanative cause role inheres in God as its bearer (RO_0000052 inheres_in).
God is the bearer of the emanative cause role (RO_0000053 bearer_of).
GodEmanativeCausationDisposition is an instance of the EmanativeCausationDisposition class.

open_questions: In Spinoza, 'emanative cause' and 'productive cause' are sometimes used interchangeably but can be distinguished: should we treat them as a single class or mint separate subclasses (EmanativeCauseRole vs. ProductiveCauseRole)?

Should EmanativeCausationProcess be modelled as a subclass of GodCausesAllThingsProcess (since both describe God's causal activity), or kept separate to preserve the specific emanative/productive character?
Is this claim drawn from the Ethics or from an earlier work (e.g., Short Treatise), which might require a different provenance relation to the source PhilosophicalWork?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts that God stands in the relation of emanative (productive) cause to his actions/effects. In BFO terms, this requires: (1) a Role class (EmanativeCauseRole, BFO_0000023) for the externally-grounded causal role God bears; (2) an individual role instance (GodEmanativeCauseRole) inhering in God; (3) a Disposition class (EmanativeCausationDisposition, BFO_0000016) for the intrinsic, internally-grounded capacity that constitutes the basis for this causal activity; (4) an individual disposition instance (GodEmanativeCausationDisposition) inhering in God; and (5) a Process class (EmanativeCausationProcess, BFO_0000015) as the occurrent in which the disposition is realised. The role/disposition distinction is important: the disposition is internally grounded in God's infinite nature, while the role is constituted by the relational context of God producing effects. Existing individuals (God, GodCausesAllThings, GodFirstEfficientCauseDisposition) are reused as bearers and relata; no existing class precisely captures the emanative/productive causal character, so new classes are minted.

proposal.utterance: God is an immanent cause, not a transitive cause.

entities.label: TransitiveCauseRole
entities.rationale: A transitive cause is an external causal role (agent acts outside itself); modeled as a Role class for contrast with the immanent cause role already in the ontology.

entities.label: GodTransitiveCauseRoleDenial
entities.rationale: The assertion that God is NOT a transitive cause is a quality/property of God — a negative predication about God's causal nature that inheres in God as an individual.

proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts two things: (1) positively, that God is an immanent cause — already captured by the existing GodImmanentCauseRole individual, so we simply assert the bearer-of relation from God to that individual; and (2) negatively, that God is NOT a transitive cause. The negative claim is represented by minting a new Quality individual (GodTransitiveCauseRoleDenial) that inheres in God, and a new class TransitiveCauseRole (subclass of BFO Role) to give the denial its semantic target. An alternative and arguably cleaner approach would be an OWL disjointness axiom between ImmanentCauseRole and TransitiveCauseRole, but that requires the user to confirm the modeling strategy. The open questions raise this option.

proposal.utterance: God is a free cause, not a natural cause.

entities.label: FreeCauseRole
entities.rationale: Spinoza's 'free cause' is a causally external role God bears — God acts solely from the necessity of its own nature with no external compulsion. Modeled as a Role (BFO_0000023) because it is externally grounded relative to other things.

entities.label: GodFreeCauseRole
entities.rationale: The specific role-instance borne by the individual God, asserting that God is a free cause.

entities.label: NaturalCauseRole
entities.rationale: A 'natural cause' (causa naturalis in Spinoza) is a role borne by things that are compelled to act by external causes. Needed to contrast with FreeCauseRole for the assertion that God does NOT bear this role.

entities.label: FreedomFromExternalDetermination
entities.rationale: Spinoza's notion of free cause entails acting solely from the necessity of one's own nature — an internally grounded capacity/disposition, fitting BFO_0000016 (Disposition).

entities.label: GodFreedomFromExternalDetermination
entities.rationale: The specific disposition-instance inhering in God by which God acts solely from its own nature.

proposal.rationale_summary: Spinoza's claim (Ethics I, Prop. 17) that God is a 'free cause' (causa libera) and not a 'natural cause' (causa naturalis) introduces two contrasting role classes. A free cause acts solely from the necessity of its own nature with no external compulsion; a natural cause is compelled or determined by something external. In BFO terms, both are Roles (BFO_0000023) because they describe how God or finite things relate causally to other entities. The freedom itself — acting from one's own nature alone — is additionally modeled as a Disposition (BFO_0000016, FreedomFromExternalDetermination), which is internally grounded in God. Individual instances of the role and disposition are created and linked to the existing God individual via RO_0000052/RO_0000053. The NaturalCauseRole class is minted to make the negation articulable; open questions flag whether to assert disjointness and whether to connect the FreeCauseRole to the already-committed CausaSui disposition.

A new individual DivineNecessitationOfAction is minted as an instance of Disposition, linked to God via RO_0000052/RO_0000053, and linked to the already-existing GodCausesAllThingsProcess via BFO_0000054 (realized in), since that process is the arena in which this disposition manifests. No new class is needed; the existing Disposition BFO type suffices, and the individual slots alongside NecessaryExistenceOfGod and GodCausesAllThings already in the graph.

proposal.utterance: God makes things as perfectly as they are conceived in his Idea.

entities.label: GodConceptualPerfectionQuality
entities.rationale: The perfection of things as they are conceived in God's Idea is a quality inhering in God (or in things as produced by God). Modeled as a Quality individual under DivineAttribute.

entities.label: DivineIdea
entities.rationale: God's Idea (the divine intellect's conception of things) is an informational/intentional content — a generically dependent continuant, subclass of ClearAndDistinctIdea already in the ontology.

entities.label: GodDivineIdea
entities.rationale: The specific individual instance of God's Idea referenced in the proposition — the total divine conception from which all things are produced.

entities.label: ProductionByDivineIdea
entities.rationale: The disposition of God to produce things in exact conformity with (and to the degree of perfection of) his Idea — an internally-grounded capacity of God as Substance.

entities.label: GodProductionByDivineIdeaDisposition
entities.rationale: The individual disposition inhering in God by which he produces all things exactly as perfectly as they are conceived in his Idea.

entities.label: PerfectProductionProcess
entities.rationale: The class of processes in which God produces things with perfection commensurate to their conception in the divine Idea.

relations.rationale: The disposition of producing things as perfectly as conceived inheres in God as its bearer.
God bears the disposition to produce things in perfect conformity with his Idea.
The disposition is realized in processes of perfect production.
The quality of producing with perfection equal to divine conception inheres in God.

Should GodConceptualPerfectionQuality be treated as identical to or a subtype of OmnipotenceOfGod already in the ontology?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts that God produces all things with exactly the degree of perfection corresponding to how they are conceived in his Idea. Ontologically this commits us to: (1) a DivineIdea class and individual (GodDivineIdea) as generically dependent continuant encoding divine conception — subclassed under the existing ClearAndDistinctIdea; (2) a disposition (GodProductionByDivineIdeaDisposition) inhering in God that governs the mode of production; (3) a quality (GodConceptualPerfectionQuality) inhering in God capturing that his productions are perfect to the degree of his conception; and (4) a PerfectProductionProcess class as the realization of that disposition. Key relations link the disposition to God via RO_0000052/53, the disposition to processes via BFO_0000054, and GodDivineIdea to TrueIntellect via BFO_0000050. Several open questions remain about the scope of 'things', the identity of God's Idea with his Intellect, and overlap with existing individuals like OmnipotenceOfGod.

proposal.utterance: It would be an imperfection in God to be able to omit what he does.

entities.label: DivineOmissionImperfectionQuality
entities.rationale: Spinoza's claim that the ability to omit would constitute an imperfection in God is best captured as a quality (a specifically dependent continuant inhering in God). It represents a hypothetical imperfection quality — the quality of being able to omit — which Spinoza denies God has. We represent it as an individual quality of the DivineAttribute type to record the ontological commitment that such omission-capacity would be an imperfection.

entities.label: DivineOmissionCapacity
entities.rationale: The 'ability to omit what he does' is a disposition (an internally grounded realizable entity). Spinoza asserts God lacks this disposition; its presence would constitute imperfection. Modeling it as a disposition individual allows the relation to God and to the imperfection quality to be expressed.

relations.rationale: The imperfection quality, if it obtained, would inhere in God — Spinoza is asserting its negation, but the ontological commitment is that such a quality would inhere in God as its bearer.
The disposition to omit would, if present, inhere in God as its bearer. Spinoza denies it is realized, but the assertion concerns God as the potential bearer.
This quality is a divine attribute (in the sense of a quality attributed to God in the argument), so it is typed under DivineAttribute.

open_questions: Spinoza's claim is a counterfactual negation: God does NOT have this disposition. Should we add an explicit negation axiom (e.g., owl:complementOf or a 'lacks' annotation) to record that working:God is explicitly asserted NOT to bear working:DivineOmissionCapacity?

Should working:DivineOmissionImperfectionQuality be related to the existing working:ImpassibilityOfGod or working:OmnipotenceOfGod individuals, since the argument grounds this denial in God's perfection and necessary activity?
Is this utterance from the Ethics (Part I) or from another Spinoza text? This would affect whether to link it to working:TheEthics.
proposal.rationale_summary: Spinoza's statement asserts that if God possessed the ability to omit any of his actions, that ability would constitute an imperfection in him. This introduces two ontological commitments: (1) a disposition — the capacity to omit divine acts — which Spinoza denies God bears, and (2) a quality of imperfection that would inhere in God were that disposition present. Both are modeled as individuals inhering in God (RO_0000052), consistent with BFO's treatment of specifically dependent continuants. The disposition is typed BFO_0000016 (Disposition) because it is internally grounded in the bearer's nature; the imperfection is typed BFO_0000019 (Quality) as a qualitative property. The statement is ultimately a negation, so the graph records what would be the case if the disposition obtained, with open questions flagging whether explicit negation axioms should be added.

proposal.utterance: Everything that happens is done by God and must be predetermined by him.

entities.label: DivinePredetermination
entities.rationale: Divine predetermination is an internally grounded capacity/disposition of God by which all events are fixed in advance; it inheres in God as an individual disposition instance.

entities.label: AllEventsProcess
entities.rationale: The aggregate of everything that happens — all occurrences — is represented as a process individual (the totality of processes in the world). This is the object of God's causal and predetermining activity.

entities.label: DivinePredeterminationClass
entities.rationale: A class for all dispositions of the type 'divine predetermination', paralleling other disposition classes already in the ontology.

relations.rationale: The individual DivinePredetermination is an instance of the class DivinePredeterminationDisposition.
The disposition of predetermination inheres in God as its bearer.
God is the bearer of the DivinePredetermination disposition (inverse of inheres-in).
The predetermination disposition is realized in the totality of all events/processes that occur.
God's causal process is part of (or co-extensive with) the totality of all events, since everything that happens is caused by God.
DivinePredeterminationDisposition is a subclass of BFO Disposition.

open_questions: Is 'predetermination' here meant in the strict logical/necessitarian sense (Spinoza: all things follow necessarily from God's nature) or in the theological voluntarist sense (God freely decrees each event)? This affects whether DivinePredetermination should be modeled primarily as a Disposition (necessary internal ground) or also as a Role (externally grounded decree).
Should AllEventsProcess be identified with or related to the existing WholeOfNature individual, since in Spinoza Natura Naturata = all events/modes following from God?
Is the predetermination universal and exceptionless (no contingency), or are there exceptions? This would affect whether we need a modal quality (e.g., NecessitationQuality) added to the class.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts two interrelated claims: (1) God is the efficient cause of everything that happens, and (2) everything that happens is predetermined by God. Claim (1) is already partially covered by existing individuals (GodCausesAllThingsProcess, GodCausesAllThings disposition, GodFirstCauseRole, etc.), so no new causal entities are strictly needed beyond linking them to a new AllEventsProcess individual representing the totality of occurrences. Claim (2) adds the specific idea of predetermination — a disposition inhering in God by which all events are fixed before (or as a consequence of) their occurrence. I model this as a new individual DivinePredetermination of type DivinePredeterminationDisposition (a new BFO Disposition subclass), inhering in God and realized in AllEventsProcess. The AllEventsProcess individual represents the totality of what happens in the world, and may be relatable to the existing WholeOfNature individual (flagged as an open question). Existing causal process individuals are linked to AllEventsProcess via part-of.

proposal.utterance: God's predetermination of all things is from eternity.

entities.label: DivinePredetermination
entities.rationale: God's predetermination of all things is an internally grounded causal power/disposition inhering in God — it is the eternal capacity by which God fixes or necessitates all things from eternity. Disposition (BFO_0000016) is appropriate because it is an intrinsic, internally grounded realizable that need not be currently manifest.

entities.label: DivinePreterminationFromEternityQuality
entities.rationale: The 'from eternity' qualification is a temporal quality inhering in the predetermination — it characterizes the eternal (atemporal / omni-temporal) character of that disposition. Modeled as a Quality (BFO_0000019) inhering in the DivinePredetermination disposition.

entities.label: DivinePreterminationProcess
entities.rationale: The actual determining/fixing of all things is a process (BFO_0000015) in which God participates, realized by the DivinePredetermination disposition. This captures the dynamic, occurrent aspect of the predetermination claim.

entities.label: Eternity
entities.rationale: Eternity, understood as the temporal/atemporal horizon within which the predetermination holds, is best approximated as a Temporal region (BFO_0000008) — the maximal temporal region coinciding with God's existence. This is a Spinozistic technical term meaning existence outside of time, approximated here.

proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts that God's predetermination of all things is eternal. BFO analysis: (1) The predetermination is an internally grounded causal power inhering in God, best typed as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) — individual DivinePredetermination inhering in the existing individual God. (2) The 'from eternity' character is a Quality (BFO_0000019) inhering in that disposition, capturing the atemporal/eternal nature of the predetermination. (3) The actual determining process is a Process (BFO_0000015) — DivinePreterminationProcess — realized by the disposition and in which God participates. (4) Eternity is provisionally typed as a Temporal region (BFO_0000008), though this is noted as an open question because Spinoza treats aeternitas as strictly non-temporal; an alternative would be to treat it as a Quality or as the maximal extent of God's necessary existence. Existing individuals (God, GodCausesAllThings, GodFirstCauseRole, GodCausesAllThingsProcess) are reused where relevant rather than duplicated.

proposal.utterance: In a created thing, existence and being produced by God is a perfection.

entities.label: CreatedThing
entities.rationale: A created thing is an independent continuant that has been produced by God; it is a kind of finite singular thing but warrants its own class to carry the specific qualities predicated of it in this proposition.

entities.label: ExistenceOfCreatedThing
entities.rationale: The existence of a created thing is a quality (a positive property that inheres in it), distinct from the mere fact of being produced.

entities.label: BeingProducedByGod
entities.rationale: Being produced by God is an externally grounded relational property of a created thing — paradigmatically a role, since it is conferred by God's causal activity rather than intrinsic constitution.

entities.label: PerfectionOfCreatedThing
entities.rationale: Perfection here is a positive quality inhering in a created thing, asserting its positive ontological status. This parallels DivineGoodnessQuality and DivineFullnessQuality already in the ontology but applied to created (finite) things.

entities.label: ProductionByGodProcess
entities.rationale: The production of a created thing by God is an occurrent — a process in which God participates as cause and the created thing as product/participant.

relations.rationale: Created things are finite singular things — they are produced and therefore not self-subsistent substances in the Spinozistic sense.
The proposition asserts that existence in a created thing IS a perfection; modeled as ExistenceOfCreatedThing being a subclass of PerfectionOfCreatedThing.
The proposition equally asserts that being produced by God IS a perfection in the created thing; BeingProducedByGod (as a role-type quality) is a subtype of PerfectionOfCreatedThing.
Confirms BFO typing: existence-as-quality inheres in the created thing as an independent continuant.
The role BeingProducedByGod is realized in a ProductionByGodProcess — the actual causal production event.
ProductionByGodProcess is a subtype of the already-existing GodCausesAllThingsProcess individual's type; reusing the process lineage.
God participates in every ProductionByGodProcess as the efficient cause.

open_questions: Is 'perfection' here meant in a Spinozistic sense (positive reality/being) rather than a normative sense? If so, PerfectionOfCreatedThing as a Quality (positive ontological content) seems correct, but should it be further tied to EternalInfiniteEssence or remain only a finite-thing quality?

Should CreatedThing be an individual (a universal covering all finite modes) rather than a class, given that in Spinoza all finite things collectively constitute Natura Naturata? Or is a class more appropriate to capture the general claim?

Does 'existence' here refer to formal existence (the actual being of the thing) or objective existence (representation in intellect)? This would affect whether ExistenceOfCreatedThing should have a sub-relation to any intellectual representation entity.
Should BeingProducedByGod be modeled as a Role (externally conferred) or as a Quality (intrinsic mark of creaturely finitude)? The choice affects the BFO_0000023 vs BFO_0000019 typing.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance (from Spinoza's Short Treatise or Ethics context) asserts that in a created (finite) thing, both its existence and the fact of being produced by God are perfections. Ontologically this introduces: (1) CreatedThing as a class of FiniteSingularThing — finite independent continuants; (2) ExistenceOfCreatedThing as a Quality inhering in such things; (3) BeingProducedByGod as a Role (externally grounded by God's causal activity) that also inheres in them; (4) PerfectionOfCreatedThing as a Quality superclass that both existence and being-produced instantiate, capturing the propositional claim that these are perfections; and (5) ProductionByGodProcess as the Process in which the role is realized. The key philosophical move — that existence and divine production are perfections — is modeled by making ExistenceOfCreatedThing and BeingProducedByGod subclasses of PerfectionOfCreatedThing, so any instance bearing either quality thereby bears a perfection. Several open questions remain about whether the existential register is formal or objective and whether BeingProducedByGod is better a Role or a Quality.

proposal.utterance: God cannot omit doing what he does.

entities.rationale: The claim that God cannot omit doing what he does expresses that God has a disposition (internally grounded in his nature) such that every action he performs is necessitated — he lacks the capacity to refrain. relations.rationale: DivineNecessitationOfAction is an individual disposition — a specifically dependent continuant inhering in God.
This disposition inheres in God as its bearer; it is the disposition by which God's acts are necessitated and cannot be omitted.

I mint 'DivineNecessitationOfAction' as a new individual disposition, relate it to God via RO_0000052 (inheres in), and note its part-of relationship to the existing GodCausesAllThings disposition. proposal.utterance: True freedom is being the first cause, unconstrained by anything else.

entities.label: TrueFreedom
entities.rationale: True freedom, in Spinoza's sense (Ethics 1D7), is the property of existing from necessity of one's own nature alone and being determined to act by oneself alone — this is an internally grounded capacity/disposition, not a mere quality or role. It maps to Disposition (BFO_0000016) as a real, intrinsic potency grounded in the bearer's nature.

entities.label: UnconstrainedFirstCausality
entities.rationale: Being 'unconstrained by anything else' is a quality of the bearer — a measurable, attributable property that distinguishes the first cause from all derivative causes. It is the absence of external determination, which is a quality of the entity's causal standing.

relations.rationale: True freedom, defined as being one's own first cause unconstrained by anything external, is a species of CausaSui (the disposition to be self-caused). CausaSui is already in the ontology as a Disposition.

The utterance characterizes true freedom as a property of the first cause; God (the unique Substance, individual already in ontology) is the bearer of TrueFreedom as a disposition.

proposal.utterance: No contingent things exist in Nature.

entities.label: ContingentThing
entities.rationale: A contingent thing is a kind of independent continuant whose existence is not necessitated by its own nature — it could exist or not exist. This is the Spinozist foil to Substance/God whose existence is necessary.

entities.label: ContingencyQuality
entities.rationale: The quality of being contingent — having existence that is not self-necessitated. This quality would inhere in bearers whose existence depends on external causes rather than their own essence.

entities.label: AbsenceOfContingencyInNatureQuality
entities.rationale: The specific ontological commitment being asserted: that the whole of Nature bears the quality of containing no contingent things. This is a quality of WholeOfNature.

relations.rationale: The whole of Nature is the bearer of the quality that no contingent things exist within it, encoding Spinoza's claim that everything in Nature exists necessarily.
The absence-of-contingency quality inheres in WholeOfNature as its bearer.

ContingencyQuality is a subclass of Quality in BFO.

Should ContingentThing be treated as an empty class in this ontology (i.e., declared to have no instances, since Spinoza denies their existence), or kept as a class for contrast/reference purposes?

Is the claim specifically about finite things (FiniteSingularThing) — i.e., that even finite things exist necessarily given prior causes — or is it a broader claim excluding any genuinely contingent entities from Nature altogether?
proposal.rationale_summary: Spinoza's claim 'No contingent things exist in Nature' is a strong modal claim: everything that exists, exists necessarily (either through its own essence, as with God/Substance, or through a determinate chain of prior causes). To represent this, I introduce a class ContingentThing (subclass of BFO independent continuant) as a reference class for things whose existence is not necessitated, and a ContingencyQuality. The core assertion is encoded as a quality (AbsenceOfContingencyInNatureQuality) inhering in the existing individual WholeOfNature, signaling that Nature as a whole lacks contingent members. The existing individuals NecessaryExistenceOfGod, GodNecessaryExistenceDisposition, and the Substance class already establish the necessity side; this addition creates the complementary negative claim. Disjointness axioms and possible declaration of ContingentThing as owl:Nothing in this ontology are raised as open questions for the user.

proposal.utterance: Everything depends on one single cause.

entities.label: SingleCauseQuality
entities.rationale: The claim that there is one single cause characterizes a quality of the causal structure — the uniqueness or singleness of the ultimate cause. This is a quality class inhering in the substance/God that is that cause.

entities.label: UniversalDependenceDisposition
entities.rationale: The disposition of everything (all finite things, all modes) to depend on the single cause. This is internally grounded in the dependent entities.

proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance 'Everything depends on one single cause' makes two claims: (1) there exists a single ultimate cause, and (2) all other things are dependent on it. In Spinozistic context this maps onto God/Substance as the unique cause. I propose a new quality class SingleCauseQuality (subclass of DivineAttribute, itself a Quality) to represent the singleness of that cause as a property of God, and a new disposition class UniversalDependenceDisposition to represent the internally grounded tendency of dependent things to depend on the single cause. I also assert the existing God individual bears the existing GodEmanativeCauseRole, which already captures this causal function. No new individuals are created, and existing classes (DivineAttribute, SubstanceProductionConstraint, GodEmanativeCausationDisposition) are reused where appropriate.

proposal.utterance: Without God, no thing can be or be understood.

entities.label: OntologicalDependenceOnGod
entities.rationale: The claim that no thing can BE without God captures an ontological dependence: finite things have a disposition (or rather: a grounded necessary condition) for their existence only insofar as God sustains them. Modeled as a disposition inhering in finite things, realizable only through God's causal activity.

entities.label: EpistemicDependenceOnGod
entities.rationale: The claim that no thing can BE UNDERSTOOD without God captures an epistemic dependence: concepts/ideas of finite things can only be formed (their intelligibility realized) through their relation to God as first cause. Modeled as a disposition inhering in the Intellect, realized through idea-formation processes that must pass through God.

entities.label: OntologicalDependenceOnGodClass
entities.rationale: Class generalizing the disposition of ontological dependence on God borne by all finite/non-substance things.

entities.label: EpistemicDependenceOnGodClass
entities.rationale: Class generalizing the disposition of epistemic dependence on God: things can only be conceived through their causal connection to God.

entities.label: ConceivingThroughGodProcess
entities.rationale: A subtype of IdeaFormationProcess in which any idea of a finite thing is formed by conceiving through God as its cause; this is the realization condition for EpistemicDependenceOnGod.

relations.rationale: The individual instance is typed under its class.

proposal.utterance: The will's existence does not belong to its essence.

entities.label: Will
entities.rationale: In Spinoza's context (Ethics II P49 and related), 'Will' (voluntas) is treated as a kind of thing whose existence and essence are separable. As a faculty or entity whose existence is distinct from its essence, it is typed as an independent continuant class (analogous to Intellect already in the ontology).

entities.label: WillEssence
entities.rationale: The essence of Will is modeled as a generically dependent continuant (an information-like content pattern), following the pattern used for EternalInfiniteEssence. This represents what it is to be a Will, abstractly.

entities.label: WillExistenceNotInEssenceQuality
entities.rationale: The claim that the Will's existence does not belong to its essence is a quality (a specifically dependent continuant) of the Will as an entity. This quality captures the ontological separation between existence and essence for the Will, contrasting with God's EssentialExistenceQuality.

relations.rationale: The quality of having existence not belong to its essence inheres in the Will as its bearer.
The Will, whose existence does not follow from its essence, is a finite singular thing in Spinoza's ontology — existence-contingent entities fall under FiniteSingularThing.

open_questions: Is 'Will' here intended as a universal class (all wills) or as a particular individual will (e.g., a specific human will)? Spinoza's Ethics II P49 treats it as a general claim about will-as-faculty, suggesting a class.

Should WillEssence be related to EternalInfiniteEssence via a negation or contrast axiom (i.e., asserting that WillEssence is NOT an instance of EternalInfiniteEssence, to capture the contrast with God's essence)?
Is this utterance from a specific proposition in the Ethics (e.g., II P49 or I P24)? Knowing the source would help tighten the typing and connect it to TheEthics individual.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance expresses a core Spinozist claim: the Will is a finite mode whose existence is not contained in its essence (unlike God/Substance, whose essence necessitates existence). I introduce a Will class as an independent continuant (parallel to the existing Intellect individual), a WillEssence individual as a generically dependent continuant encoding what-it-is-to-be-a-Will, and a WillExistenceNotInEssenceQuality individual as a quality inhering in Will to represent the ontological gap between its essence and existence. Will is typed as a subclass of FiniteSingularThing, since any entity whose existence does not follow from its essence is contingent and finite in Spinoza's system. This contrasts with GodNecessaryExistenceQuality and EssentialExistenceQuality already in the ontology. The WillEssence individual is left as a bare GDC for now, pending clarification on whether a negation axiom relating it to EternalInfiniteEssence is desired.

proposal.utterance: Only particulars have causes; universals are nothing.

entities.label: Particular
entities.rationale: A 'particular' in this Spinozistic/scholastic context is an individual existing thing — a finite singular thing or mode — best typed as a subclass of Independent Continuant (or at minimum a continuant). BFO's independent continuant is the natural home for concretely existing particulars.

entities.label: Universal
entities.rationale: Universals as abstract, shareable conceptual patterns are most naturally typed as generically dependent continuants in BFO — they are informational/pattern entities that can be 'copied' or multiply instantiated. However, Spinoza's claim is that they have no ontological standing of their own (they are 'nothing'), which is flagged as an open question.

entities.label: CausalReceptivityDisposition
entities.rationale: The claim that 'only particulars have causes' implies particulars bear a disposition to be causally affected and causally efficacious. This is an internally-grounded disposition inhering in particulars.

entities.label: UniversalNullityQuality
entities.rationale: Spinoza's assertion that universals are 'nothing' (entia rationis with no real ontological status) can be captured as a quality — specifically a nullity or ontological-vacuity quality — that would inhere in any posited universal, marking it as lacking genuine existence.

relations.rationale: Particulars are concretely existing independent continuants in BFO terms.
Universals, to the extent they are anything at all, function as generically dependent (abstract, copyable) patterns — though Spinoza denies them real existence.
FiniteSingularThing (already in ontology) is a paradigm case of a particular in Spinoza's system.
CausalReceptivityDisposition is a disposition subclass.
Restricting causal receptivity to particulars — encoded as a subClassOf axiom pairing Particular with bearing CausalReceptivityDisposition.
UniversalNullityQuality is a quality class marking the ontological vacuity Spinoza ascribes to universals.

open_questions: Spinoza says universals are 'nothing' (entia rationis) — should working:Universal be modeled as a class at all, or should it be captured purely as a negative claim (an annotation that no instances of Universal exist in the ontology)? Modeling it as a BFO_0000031 subclass implies it has some ontological standing, which contradicts the assertion.

Is 'Particular' here intended to cover all modes (finite and infinite) or only finite singular things? Infinite modes in Spinoza also have causes, so the scope of 'Particular' may need to be broader than working:FiniteSingularThing.
Should working:CausalReceptivityDisposition be restricted to Particulars via an OWL restriction (e.g., only Particulars can bear this disposition), or is a comment/annotation sufficient?

Is this utterance intended as a Spinozistic thesis (from his own texts) or as a general scholastic principle Spinoza is endorsing/rejecting? This affects which PhilosophicalWork or context individual should be linked to these classes.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance encodes two tightly coupled Spinozistic theses: (1) causal relations attach only to particulars (individual existing things), and (2) universals lack genuine ontological standing ('are nothing'). I model Particular as a new class under BFO Independent Continuant, linking the existing FiniteSingularThing as a subclass. I model CausalReceptivityDisposition as a new Disposition class restricted to Particulars, reflecting that only particulars enter causal relations. For universals I propose a class under Generically Dependent Continuant (the closest BFO home for abstract shareable patterns), while acknowledging the deep tension: Spinoza denies universals any real being, so the class may ultimately need to be declared empty or represented only as a negative annotation. UniversalNullityQuality is proposed to encode the 'nothing' claim as a quality that would attach to any posited universal. Several open questions are raised about scope, ontological commitment, and textual provenance.

proposal.utterance: God is a cause of and provider for only particular things.

entities.label: GodParticularsOnlyCauseQuality
entities.rationale: The claim that God causes and provides for only particular things (rather than universals or abstract entities) is a quality inhering in God as the bearer. It characterizes the scope of God's causal activity as restricted to particular, individual things.

entities.label: GodCausesParticularsDisposition
entities.rationale: The dispositional capacity of God to cause and provide for particular things — an internally grounded tendency toward particular causal action. This is distinct from the quality (which characterizes the scope) and the process (which is the actual causation).

entities.label: GodCausesParticularsProcess
entities.rationale: The actual process by which God causes and provides for particular things. This is the realization of the disposition in a temporal unfolding.

entities.label: ParticularsProvisionRole
entities.rationale: God bears the externally-grounded role of provider for particular things. The 'provider' aspect is relationally grounded in particular things that receive provision, making it a role rather than a disposition.

God bears this quality characterizing the scope of its causation.
The disposition to cause particular things inheres in God.
God bears the disposition toward causation of particulars.

The process of causing particulars realizes the disposition.
God participates in the process of causing particular things.

Does 'provider' (in addition to 'cause') introduce a distinct concept such as sustaining or maintaining particular things in existence, or is it synonymous with 'cause' here?
Is this claim meant to restrict the scope of an existing causal role (e.g., GodProximateCauseRole, GodEmanativeCauseRole) or to assert a wholly new causal modality?

proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance claims that God's causal and providential activity is restricted to particular (individual, token-level) things only. This introduces three new individuals: a Quality inhering in God characterizing the scope restriction of its causation (GodParticularsOnlyCauseQuality, subtype of DivineAttribute/Quality), a Disposition grounding that causal tendency (GodCausesParticularsDisposition), and a Process realizing it (GodCausesParticularsProcess). Additionally, a Role (ParticularsProvisionRole) captures the 'provider' aspect, which is relationally grounded in particular things receiving provision. Key open questions concern whether this claim conflicts with existing assertions (e.g., God as cause of all things via GodCausesAllThingsProcess), and what precisely 'particular' means in this context.

proposal.utterance: Good and evil are modes of thinking, not things or entities with existence.

entities.label: GoodAndEvilAsModeOfThinking
entities.rationale: Spinoza's claim that good and evil are 'modes of thinking' is itself a propositional content — a philosophical thesis expressed in The Ethics. It is best typed as a generically dependent continuant (an informational content item / propositional content), not as the modes themselves.

entities.label: Good
entities.rationale: Spinoza explicitly states that 'good' is a mode of thinking (modus cogitandi), not an independently existing thing. Typed as an instance of working:Mode (which is a subclass of BFO_0000020 Specifically Dependent Continuant), inhering in a thinking subject.

entities.label: Evil
entities.rationale: Spinoza explicitly states that 'evil' is a mode of thinking (modus cogitandi), not an independently existing thing. Typed as an instance of working:Mode (which is a subclass of BFO_0000020 Specifically Dependent Continuant), inhering in a thinking subject.

entities.label: ModeOfThinking
entities.rationale: A subclass of Mode restricted to those modes that inhere in a thinking substance (i.e., modes of the attribute Thought). Good and Evil are instances of this class per Spinoza's claim.

entities.label: GoodEvilNotIndependentlyExistentQuality
entities.rationale: The denial of independent existence to good and evil is a quality of the thesis — it qualifies the ontological status of Good and Evil as non-self-subsisting, dependent on a thinking mind. This parallels existing DenialOfPassion and similar quality individuals in the ontology.

relations.rationale: Good is an instance of ModeOfThinking per Spinoza's claim.
Evil is an instance of ModeOfThinking per Spinoza's claim.
ModeOfThinking is a specialization of Mode restricted to those inhering in or arising within a thinking substance.

proposal.rationale_summary: Spinoza's claim that good and evil are modes of thinking (modi cogitandi) and not independently existing things or entities is a central thesis of the Ethics (particularly the Preface to Part IV). This is best captured as a Disposition (internally grounded realizable entity). It is distinct from CausaSui (which applies to Substance/God) but structurally analogous.

entities.label: AttributeSelfSubsistenceQuality
entities.rationale: The fact of existing through itself is also a quality that can be predicated of each attribute — its mode of being. As a Quality it captures the static, measurable status of self-subsistence, complementing the dispositional aspect.

relations.rationale: SelfSubsistenceDisposition is a subclass of BFO Disposition.
Self-subsistence quality is a kind of AttributeOfSubstance quality, since the utterance specifically concerns attributes qua beings-through-themselves.
The self-subsistence disposition inheres in attributes, which are modeled under AttributeOfSubstance.

open_questions: Is 'existing through themselves' meant here in the strict Spinozistic sense (equivalent to CausaSui — the concept of a thing whose essence involves existence), or is it a weaker sense of ontological independence? If the former, SelfSubsistenceDisposition should be typed as a subclass of CausaSui rather than a fresh class.

Should we also assert that specific existing attribute individuals (e.g., working:Extension, working:Thought) bear instances of SelfSubsistenceDisposition and AttributeSelfSubsistenceQuality, or is this a class-level claim only?

Do attributes 'exist through themselves' derivatively (because they are attributes of the self-subsistent Substance/God) or absolutely (same ground as God)? The answer affects whether AttributeSelfSubsistenceQuality is a subclass of EssentialExistenceQuality.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance 'Attributes are beings existing through themselves' introduces a metaphysical predicate: attributes are self-subsistent. In BFO terms, self-subsistence has two facets — a dispositional one (the internal grounding for self-existence, BFO Disposition) and a quality facet (the actual measurable status of being self-subsistent, BFO Quality). I introduce SelfSubsistenceDisposition as a new Disposition class and AttributeSelfSubsistenceQuality as a new Quality class, both situated under the existing AttributeOfSubstance hierarchy. I avoid reusing CausaSui (already committed to Substance/God) because the utterance is specifically about attributes, though an open question asks whether the two should be unified. No individuals are asserted yet; this is a class-level commitment.

proposal.utterance: Other things are only modes of attributes.

entities.label: OtherThings
entities.rationale: In Spinoza's system, 'other things' (i.e., non-Substance entities, finite modes) are independent continuants in so far as they are things at all, but their ontological status is as modes of attributes. Modeled as a class of independent continuants whose instances are also instances of Mode (specifically dependent continuants). Note tension: Spinoza's modes are technically dependent, but BFO requires independent continuants to have their own existence. We model OtherThings as a class, with the constraint that every instance also bears a ModeInstance, to capture the dependency.

entities.label: ModeOfAttribute
entities.rationale: A ModeOfAttribute is a specifically dependent continuant (a mode) that inheres in an attribute of Substance, rather than directly in Substance itself. This is the Spinozistic claim: other things are modes of God's attributes (Thought, Extension, etc.), not modes of Substance directly. Subclass of ModeInstance.

relations.rationale: ModeOfAttribute is a more specific kind of ModeInstance — it is specifically a mode that inheres in an attribute.
Other things are independent continuants in BFO's taxonomy, even though Spinoza treats them as ontologically dependent on Substance via its attributes.
A ModeOfAttribute inheres in an AttributeOfSubstance — this captures the Spinozistic claim that other things are modes OF the attributes (Thought, Extension) rather than of Substance per se.

open_questions: Spinoza's modes are ontologically dependent entities, but BFO treats specifically dependent continuants as inhering in independent continuants. Should OtherThings be modeled as a subclass of FiniteSingularThing (already in the ontology) rather than a new class?

The statement 'other things are only modes of attributes' — does this mean (a) other things ARE modes (i.e., are identical to ModeOfAttribute instances), or (b) other things are characterized/defined by having a ModeOfAttribute inhering in them? This affects whether OtherThings should be a subclass of a dependent or independent continuant.
Should 'attributes' here refer specifically to the existing individuals Extension and Thought, or to the class AttributeOfSubstance generally?
Should we assert that OtherThings and Substance are disjoint classes, formalizing Spinoza's division of reality?
proposal.rationale_summary: Spinoza's claim 'other things are only modes of attributes' asserts that every entity other than Substance (God/Nature) exists as a mode — a dependent modification — of one of Substance's infinite attributes (primarily Thought and Extension). In BFO terms, modes are specifically dependent continuants that inhere in a bearer. The claim introduces two key ontological commitments: (1) there is a class OtherThings distinct from Substance, and (2) these other things exist only as ModeOfAttribute instances — a subclass of the existing ModeInstance class — where the bearer of that mode is an AttributeOfSubstance (the class already in the ontology). A key BFO tension is that Spinoza's modes are ontologically dependent (they cannot exist without their bearer-attribute), yet BFO's independent continuants are self-subsistent. The proposed modeling uses ModeOfAttribute as a specifically dependent continuant inhering in AttributeOfSubstance to capture the dependency, while flagging the question of whether OtherThings should simply be identified with FiniteSingularThing (already in the ontology) to avoid redundancy.
