proposal.utterance: Modes cannot exist or be understood without the attributes of which they are modes.

entities.label: ModeAttributeDependence
entities.rationale: The claim that modes cannot exist or be understood without their attribute is best captured as a disposition (an internally grounded, structural dependency) that every Mode instance bears toward its constituting Attribute. It is a disposition because it reflects a necessary, intrinsic feature of Modes: they are disposed to require their Attribute for both existence and intelligibility.

entities.label: ModeExistenceDependenceOnAttribute
entities.rationale: The ontological dependency of a mode's existence on its attribute is a quality that each mode bears — it characterises the mode's existential status as derivative from and conditioned by the attribute.

entities.label: ModeIntelligibilityDependenceOnAttribute
entities.rationale: Spinoza's claim includes epistemic dependency: modes cannot be *understood* apart from their attribute. This intelligibility-dependence is a distinct quality of modes, separable from (though correlated with) their existential dependence.

relations.rationale: ModeAttributeDependence is a subclass of Disposition (BFO_0000016).
ModeExistenceDependenceOnAttribute is a subclass of Quality (BFO_0000019).
ModeIntelligibilityDependenceOnAttribute is a subclass of Quality (BFO_0000019).
Every Mode, as a class, bears a ModeAttributeDependence disposition — expressed as a subclass axiom indicating every mode instance inheres-dependently on an attribute.
ModeAttributeDependence inheres in Mode instances; this expresses the direction of the specifically dependent continuant toward its bearer.
The existence-dependence quality inheres in Mode instances.
The intelligibility-dependence quality inheres in Mode instances.
Modes are parts of (exist within / are ontologically dependent on) the Attributes of which they are modes, reflecting Spinoza's claim that modes cannot exist without their attribute.

open_questions: Should ModeAttributeDependence be modeled as a single class covering both existence- and intelligibility-dependence, or kept split into ModeExistenceDependenceOnAttribute and ModeIntelligibilityDependenceOnAttribute? The split respects the two distinct claims but adds complexity.

The BFO relation BFO_0000050 (part of) is used here to represent existential containment of modes within attributes. Is this the intended mereological sense, or should a dedicated 'ontological dependence' object property be introduced?
Should ModeInstance (already in the ontology) bear these qualities/dispositions rather than the Mode class itself, since ModeInstance is the class of particular mode instances?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts two closely related ontological claims about Modes (Spinoza Ethics II, Def.1): (1) modes cannot *exist* independently of the attributes they belong to, and (2) modes cannot be *understood* independently of those attributes. Both claims are about necessary, intrinsic dependencies that every mode bears. In BFO terms, existence-dependency is modeled as a Quality (ModeExistenceDependenceOnAttribute) and a Disposition (ModeAttributeDependence) inhering in every Mode, while intelligibility-dependence is also modeled as a Quality (ModeIntelligibilityDependenceOnAttribute). The existing classes Mode and AttributeOfSubstance are reused. A BFO_0000050 (part of) relation from Mode to AttributeOfSubstance captures the containment/existential grounding of modes within their attributes. The 'cannot be understood without' claim is harder to represent in BFO directly since BFO does not have epistemic relations; it is therefore recorded as a Quality on Mode instances, flagged for review.

proposal.utterance: God is a being that exists through itself without needing anything else.

entities.label: God_SubstanceIndividual
entities.rationale: God already exists as an individual typed as BFO_0000004. The utterance reaffirms God as a self-subsisting being, consistent with the existing individual.

entities.label: CausaSui
entities.rationale: The class CausaSui (cause of itself / existing through itself) already exists and directly captures the Spinozistic notion of a being that exists through its own nature without external dependence.

entities.label: GodCausaSuiDisposition
entities.rationale: A token instance of CausaSui inhering in the individual God, representing the specific disposition by which God exists through itself without needing anything else.

entities.label: SelfSustainingExistenceDisposition
entities.rationale: Already exists as an individual disposition of God capturing self-sustaining existence; reused here to avoid duplication.

relations.rationale: Types the new individual as an instance of the CausaSui disposition class.
The CausaSui disposition inheres in God as its bearer, expressing that it is God specifically who exists through itself.
Inverse: God is the bearer of the GodCausaSuiDisposition.
Reaffirms the already-existing disposition of self-sustaining existence as borne by God, consistent with the utterance.
The self-sustaining existence disposition inheres in God.

open_questions: Should GodCausaSuiDisposition and SelfSustainingExistenceDisposition be treated as distinct dispositions, or should one subsume the other (e.g., GodCausaSuiDisposition rdfs:subClassOf SelfSustainingExistenceDisposition)?

The utterance also implies independence from external causes (no external determination). Should we also assert that the ExistenceNecessitation individual inheres in God here, or is that already covered by NecessaryExistenceOfGod and GodNecessaryExistenceDisposition?
Is 'being' in this context precisely synonymous with 'Substance' (Spinoza's usage), or should a more generic 'Being' class be introduced as a parent of Substance?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance encodes the classical Spinozistic definition of God as causa sui: a being whose essence involves existence and which depends on nothing outside itself. The individual 'God' and the class 'CausaSui' (disposition) already exist in the working ontology. I mint a new individual token 'GodCausaSuiDisposition' typed as CausaSui and inhering in God to make the claim about this particular being explicit at the individual level. I also reuse the existing 'SelfSustainingExistenceDisposition' individual, asserting the inheres-in / bearer-of relations to God. No new classes are required. The open questions flag potential redundancy between the two disposition individuals and invite the user to decide on their relationship.

proposal.utterance: Natura naturata requires substances in order to be conceived properly.

entities.label: NaturaNaturata
entities.rationale: Natura naturata, in Spinoza's system, is the totality of finite modes (everything that follows from God's attributes). It is a distinct individual continuant in the ontology, parallel to NaturaNaturans already in the graph.

entities.label: NaturaNaturataConceivabilityConstraint
entities.rationale: The claim that Natura naturata requires substances to be properly conceived is best modeled as a disposition (constraint) inhering in NaturaNaturata: it is internally grounded in Natura naturata's nature that it can only be conceived through the substances (attributes) it depends on. This mirrors SubstanceProductionConstraint already in the graph.

relations.rationale: NaturaNaturata is an independent continuant of type Substance (the totality that follows from God/NaturaNaturans).
The conceivability constraint inheres in NaturaNaturata as its bearer.
Natura naturata is part of the whole of nature (WholeOfNature individual already in graph), since in Spinoza nature as a whole = NaturaNaturans + NaturaNaturata.
The constraint is a subtype of SubstanceProductionConstraint, expressing that Natura naturata's conceptual derivability depends on substances.

open_questions: Should NaturaNaturata be typed as working:Substance (BFO:Independent continuant) or more specifically as a collection of modes (BFO_0000020, Specifically dependent continuant)? In Spinoza modes inhere in substance, so Natura naturata as a totality of modes might better be typed as BFO_0000020 or a subclass thereof rather than BFO_0000004.

The utterance says Natura naturata 'requires substances in order to be conceived properly.' Should this dependence be captured as a generic dependence relation (the idea of Natura naturata generically depends on the idea of Substance) via a GDC relation, rather than as a disposition inhering in Natura naturata?

Is the 'substance' referred to here specifically God/the one Substance (NaturaNaturans), or substances in general (the Substance class)? This affects whether the relation should point to the individual NaturaNaturans or to the class Substance.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance introduces Natura naturata as an entity not yet in the graph (NaturaNaturans is present but not NaturaNaturata) and asserts a conceivability-dependence on substances. I mint NaturaNaturata as a new individual of type Substance (BFO_0000004), parallel to NaturaNaturans, and model the dependency as a disposition (NaturaNaturataConceivabilityConstraint, subtype of SubstanceProductionConstraint) inhering in NaturaNaturata. A part-of relation connects NaturaNaturata to WholeOfNature. The most significant open question is whether NaturaNaturata, being the totality of modes, should be BFO_0000004 or BFO_0000020, since modes in Spinoza are specifically dependent on substance—this needs user confirmation before commitment.

proposal.utterance: Motion and Intellect are universal modes that immediately depend on God.

entities.label: Motion
entities.rationale: Motion is a universal mode in Spinoza's system. Modes are specifically dependent continuants that inhere in Substance/God. Typed as individual of class ModeInstance (which is a subclass of Mode, itself under BFO_0000020).

entities.label: UniversalModeRole
entities.rationale: A role class distinguishing universal (immediate infinite) modes from finite or mediate modes. Roles are externally grounded in Spinozist metaphysics by their direct relation to God.

entities.label: MotionUniversalModeRole
entities.rationale: The specific instance of UniversalModeRole borne by the mode Motion.

entities.label: IntellectUniversalModeRole
entities.rationale: The specific instance of UniversalModeRole borne by TrueIntellect (the existing individual representing Intellect as a universal mode).

entities.label: ImmediateInfiniteModeDepedence
entities.rationale: A disposition class representing the internally grounded capacity of universal/immediate infinite modes to depend directly on God (Substance) without mediation.

entities.label: MotionImmediateDependenceDisposition
entities.rationale: Instance of the immediate dependence disposition inhering in Motion.

entities.label: IntellectImmediateDependenceDisposition
entities.rationale: Instance of the immediate dependence disposition inhering in TrueIntellect.

proposal.utterance: Relations are beings of reason, not real beings in Nature.

entities.label: RelationAsBeingOfReason

entities.label: RealBeing

entities.label: MindDependenceQuality

proposal.utterance: Death occurs when the body's proportion of motion and rest can no longer be maintained.

entities.label: Death
entities.rationale: Death is a process that occurs to a body — an unfolding event in time, not a persistent thing. Spinoza's account treats death as a transition event, making Process the most accurate BFO typing.

entities.label: BodyMotionRestProportion
entities.rationale: The proportion of motion and rest is a specific measurable relational quality inhering in a body. In Spinoza, this ratio constitutes the body's characteristic form. It is a Quality in BFO terms — a specifically dependent continuant inhering in the body.

entities.label: BodyMotionRestProportionMaintenanceDisposition
entities.rationale: The capacity of a body to maintain its characteristic proportion of motion and rest is an internally grounded disposition — a realizable entity that can be lost, at which point death occurs. This models Spinoza's claim that the body has a conatus to preserve this ratio.

entities.label: ProportionMaintenanceFailureProcess
entities.rationale: The process by which the body's proportion can no longer be maintained — the proximate process constituting or immediately preceding death. Distinct from Death itself, this is the failure event that brings about death.

relations.rationale: BodyMotionRestProportion is a subclass of Quality (BFO_0000019), as it is a specifically dependent property inhering in a material body.
The maintenance disposition is a subclass of Disposition — internally grounded in the body's structural constitution.
Death is a Process subclass.
ProportionMaintenanceFailureProcess is a Process subclass.

Death (as a process) has as part the failure process wherein the proportion can no longer be maintained — or alternatively Death is realized when this failure occurs. Using part-of to relate the failure process as a constituent of the death process.
The maintenance disposition (in its failure/negation) is realized in the ProportionMaintenanceFailureProcess — the process in which the disposition can no longer be exercised.

Is 'Death' being asserted here as applying to finite modes (FiniteSingularThing) only, or also potentially to other composite bodies? This would affect whether Death should be a subclass under FiniteSingularThingModeInstance processes.

proposal.rationale_summary: Spinoza's definition of death (Ethics IV, Prop. 39 Schol.) states that death occurs when a body can no longer maintain its characteristic proportion (ratio) of motion and rest among its parts. This introduces four new ontological commitments: (1) Death as a Process class — an unfolding event; (2) BodyMotionRestProportion as a Quality class — a specifically dependent relational property inhering in material bodies; (3) BodyMotionRestProportionMaintenanceDisposition as a Disposition class — the internally grounded capacity to preserve that ratio, whose loss occasions death; and (4) ProportionMaintenanceFailureProcess as the proximate sub-process constituting the onset of death. The existing working:Motion individual is relevant but represents extension-attribute motion rather than the internal motion/rest ratio of finite bodies, so a new Quality class is warranted. No existing individuals or classes in the working ontology directly capture these concepts, though they connect naturally to FiniteSingularThing, ModeInstance, and the Motion/Extension apparatus already present.

proposal.utterance: The soul, as a mode of thinking substance, can know and love that substance and extension.

entities.label: Soul
entities.rationale: In Spinoza's system the soul (mind) is a mode of thinking substance — a finite singular thing that is an instance of Thought-attribute modification. It is an independent continuant (persists through time) whose nature is given by its mode-type. Typing it as a subclass of Mode (itself BFO_0000020 / specifically dependent continuant) captures the Spinozistic dependency while BFO_0000004 tensions arise; see open_questions.

entities.label: KnowledgeCapacity
entities.rationale: The capacity of the soul to know substance and attributes is an internally grounded disposition inhering in the soul as a cognitive entity.

entities.label: LoveCapacity
entities.rationale: The capacity of the soul to love substance is an internally grounded disposition; distinct from mere cognition but co-present with it in Spinoza's account of intellectual love.

entities.label: ThinkingSubstanceRole
entities.rationale: The role of being 'thinking substance' that the one Substance bears under the attribute of Thought. This externalises the relational characterisation without duplicating the Thought quality already in the graph.

entities.label: SoulKnowsSubstanceProcess
entities.rationale: The process by which the soul exercises its knowledge capacity toward substance (under Thought and Extension attributes); an occurrent that realizes KnowledgeCapacity.

entities.label: SoulLovesSubstanceProcess
entities.rationale: The process by which the soul exercises its love capacity toward substance; realizes LoveCapacity.

LoveCapacity inheres in the soul as its bearer.

Should 'Thought' (existing individual typed BFO_0000019 quality) be promoted to a class or a separate attribute-individual to serve as the attribute under which the soul is a mode? Currently Thought is an individual quality, but the utterance treats it as a type of substance.

proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts three main commitments: (1) the soul is a mode of thinking substance — modeled as a class Soul that is a subclass of both Mode and FiniteSingularThingModeInstance, with a ThinkingSubstanceRole borne by God under the Thought attribute; (2) the soul has a capacity to know substance and its attributes (Extension, Thought) — modeled as a KnowledgeCapacity disposition inhering in Soul, realized in a SoulKnowsSubstanceProcess with God and Extension as participants; (3) the soul has a capacity to love substance — modeled as a LoveCapacity disposition realized in SoulLovesSubstanceProcess. Existing individuals God, Extension, and Thought are reused. A critical BFO disjointness tension arises because Mode is a specifically dependent continuant while FiniteSingularThingModeInstance descends from an independent continuant; this is flagged as an open question requiring user resolution before commitment.

proposal.utterance: Perceptions or consciousness of knowledge arise from either belief, true belief, or clear and distinct conception.

entities.label: KnowledgePerception
entities.rationale: A perception or consciousness of knowledge is a cognitive capacity or disposition of a knowing subject — it is internally grounded in the bearer and thus fits BFO Disposition. It is the generic kind of which Belief, TrueBeliefPerception, and ClearAndDistinctConception are sub-kinds.

entities.label: BeliefPerception
entities.rationale: Belief as a mode of epistemic access — the weakest of the three, a disposition of the cognizer toward a proposition without guarantee of truth. Subclass of KnowledgePerception.

entities.label: TrueBeliefPerception
entities.rationale: True belief as a mode of epistemic access — a disposition that tracks truth but lacks the necessity of clear and distinct conception. Subclass of KnowledgePerception.

entities.label: ClearAndDistinctConception
entities.rationale: Clear and distinct conception is the highest grade of epistemic access — a fully adequate, internally grounded disposition of the intellect. Subclass of KnowledgePerception. Closely related to the existing ClearAndDistinctIdea (BFO_0000031, a GDC), but this is the cognitive disposition/capacity that produces or apprehends such ideas, not the idea-content itself.

relations.rationale: Belief is one of the three enumerated sources/modes of knowledge-perception.
True belief is one of the three enumerated sources/modes of knowledge-perception.
Clear and distinct conception is one of the three enumerated sources/modes of knowledge-perception.
Clear and distinct conception is the highest form of intellectual certainty-disposition already in the ontology; subclassing captures that relationship.

open_questions: Is this utterance from Spinoza's Emendation of the Intellect (TIE) where he enumerates four modes of perception (perception by hearsay, by vague experience, by inference, by adequate idea)? If so, should 'BeliefPerception' map to hearsay/opinion and 'TrueBeliefPerception' to vague experience or inference? Clarification would allow finer-grained subclassing.

Should 'KnowledgePerception' be modeled as a Disposition (internally grounded capacity of the cognizer) or as a Quality (a measurable epistemic property of the cognizer)? The disposition reading emphasizes the cognizer's active capacity; the quality reading emphasizes a state they are in.

entities.label: BeliefPerception

entities.label: TrueBeliefPerception

entities.label: ClearAndDistinctConception

proposal.utterance: Knowledge is the proximate cause of all passions of the soul.

entities.label: PassionOfTheSoul
entities.rationale: A passion of the soul (passio animi) is an affective state that a mind is disposed toward or undergoes; it is internally grounded in the bearer (the soul/mind) and hence fits Disposition rather than Role. It is a class because passions are kinds of states, not a single individual.

entities.label: KnowledgeProximateCauseRole
entities.rationale: The proposition asserts that Knowledge bears the role of proximate cause with respect to passions of the soul. The role is externally grounded (defined by its causal relationship to passions), hence Role rather than Disposition. This is a class of roles that instances of knowledge can bear.

entities.label: KnowledgeCausesPassionProcess
entities.rationale: The causal relationship between knowledge and passions is realized in a process — the process by which knowledge (as proximate cause) brings about or actualizes passions of the soul. This is a subclass of Process, not an individual, because it covers all such causal episodes.

relations.rationale: The proximate-cause role of knowledge is realized in the process of knowledge causing passions of the soul.
Inverse: the causal process realizes the proximate-cause role borne by knowledge.
Instances of PassionOfTheSoul participate in (as patient/output) the KnowledgeCausesPassionProcess, since knowledge is their proximate cause.

Three new ontological commitments are introduced: (1) a class PassionOfTheSoul, typed as Disposition (BFO_0000016) because passions are internally grounded affective states of a bearer-soul; (2) a class KnowledgeProximateCauseRole, typed as Role (BFO_0000023) because 'being a proximate cause' is an externally grounded relational property knowledge bears with respect to passions; and (3) a class KnowledgeCausesPassionProcess, typed as Process (BFO_0000015), in which the role is realized and in which PassionOfTheSoul instances participate as effects. proposal.utterance: Opinion produces all passions contrary to good reason.

entities.label: Opinion
entities.rationale: Opinion in Spinoza (and classical/early modern usage) is a cognitive disposition or faculty — a settled tendency to form beliefs not grounded in adequate ideas. Disposition (BFO_0000016) is the best fit for an internally-grounded capacity to produce effects.

entities.label: Passion
entities.rationale: Passions (affectus passivi) are specifically dependent states that inhere in a mind/body — they are affective qualities or modes, not independent entities. BFO SDC (Mode, which is already in the ontology) would also work; Passion as a subclass of Mode captures this. Using BFO_0000020 as parent with the intent to subclass Mode.

entities.label: GoodReason
entities.rationale: Good reason (recta ratio) is a cognitive normative standard — in BFO terms best modeled as a disposition or method. It is an internally grounded capacity for correct inferential behavior. Disposition fits.

entities.label: ContraryToGoodReasonQuality
entities.rationale: The property of being contrary to good reason is a quality that inheres in passions — a normative/relational quality marking their status as irrational.

entities.label: PassionProductionProcess
entities.rationale: The production of passions by opinion is a process — an occurrent unfolding in time. This models the causal/generative claim in the utterance.

relations.rationale: Passions are modes (specifically dependent continuants) in the Spinozist framework — they are finite modifications of substance.
The passion production process realizes the disposition of Opinion — Opinion (as disposition) is realized in the PassionProductionProcess.
Not appropriate — removing this. The ContraryToGoodReasonQuality inheres in Passion instances.
Passions are specifically dependent continuants inhering in a bearer (mind or body).
Good reason (recta ratio) is a species of Method in the existing ontology — it is a disposition governing correct inferential procedure.

open_questions: Is 'Opinion' here Spinoza's first kind of knowledge (imaginatio/opinio), i.e. BFO Disposition inhering in a finite mind? Or should it be typed as a generically dependent continuant (a body of beliefs/information content)?

Is 'good reason' here recta ratio (Spinoza's second kind of knowledge, ratio) — should GoodReason be linked to existing ClearAndDistinctIdea or InnateCapacity classes?

proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts a causal/generative relationship: Opinion (as a cognitive faculty or disposition) produces passions, and the passions so produced are contrary to good reason. In BFO terms, Opinion is best typed as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) — an internally-grounded tendency in a bearer (the mind) that can be realized in processes. The production event is a Process (BFO_0000015), specifically PassionProductionProcess. Passions are specifically dependent continuants (modes) inhering in a bearer, making them subclasses of the existing Mode class. The property of being contrary to good reason is a Quality (BFO_0000019) inhering in those passions. GoodReason is modeled as a Disposition/Method — a capacity for correct reasoning. proposal.utterance: True belief produces good desires.

entities.label: TrueBelief
entities.rationale: A true belief is an internal cognitive disposition of an agent — it is grounded in the bearer's nature (epistemic state) and can be realized in cognitive or conative processes. Modeled as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) rather than a Quality because it has a directedness toward realization in behaviour/desire-production.

entities.label: GoodDesire
entities.rationale: A desire is a conative disposition of an agent — an internally grounded tendency toward action or an end. 'Good' is an evaluative qualification of that disposition. Modeled as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) because desires are internally grounded tendencies that can be realized in processes of action.

entities.label: TrueBeliefProducesGoodDesireProcess
entities.rationale: The causal-productive relation between true belief and good desire is a process — an unfolding in time in which a true belief disposition is realized and results in (triggers or shapes) a good desire disposition in the same or another bearer. This is modeled as a Process class to represent the productive/causal happening asserted by the utterance.

relations.rationale: The production process has a true belief as participant — the true belief is realized in (and triggers) this process.
The production process has a good desire as participant — the good desire is the output disposition that results from this process.
TrueBelief as a disposition is realized in the TrueBeliefProducesGoodDesireProcess — this is the standard BFO way to express that a disposition manifests via a process.

open_questions: Is this utterance intended as a universal causal law (all true beliefs always produce good desires), or as a general tendency/defeasible claim? This affects whether the production process is modeled as a necessary realization or a probabilistic one.

Who or what is the bearer of the TrueBelief and GoodDesire here — a human mind, an intellect (cf. existing working:TrueIntellect or working:Intellect individuals), or some more general agent? Knowing the bearer would allow us to assert RO_0000052 (inheres in) relations.

Is 'good desire' in the context of this ontology (which appears Spinozistic) equivalent to a desire aligned with the conatus or with clear-and-distinct ideas? This would allow us to link GoodDesire to existing classes like working:ClearAndDistinctIdea or working:ReflexiveKnowledge.

proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance 'True belief produces good desires' asserts a causal-productive relationship between two cognitive-conative states. In BFO terms, beliefs and desires are internally grounded states of a bearer and are best typed as Dispositions (BFO_0000016), since they are grounded in the bearer's nature and are directed toward realization in processes. The productive relation itself — the happening by which true belief gives rise to good desire — is typed as a Process (BFO_0000015). I mint three new classes: TrueBelief (Disposition), GoodDesire (Disposition), and TrueBeliefProducesGoodDesireProcess (Process). The process has both disposition classes as participants via RO_0000057, and TrueBelief is realized in the process via BFO_0000054. Several open questions remain, especially about the bearers of these dispositions and whether TrueBelief should be linked to existing classes such as ClearAndDistinctIdea or ReflexiveKnowledge, given the Spinozistic context of this ontology.

proposal.utterance: Clear knowledge produces true and genuine love.

entities.label: ClearKnowledge
entities.rationale: Clear knowledge in Spinoza's sense is an epistemic capacity or disposition inhering in a mind/intellect — it is internally grounded and can be realized in cognitive processes. It is distinct from but related to ClearAndDistinctIdea (which is the GDC content); here we capture the knowing disposition itself.

entities.label: TrueAndGenuineLove
entities.rationale: True and genuine love (amor verus) for Spinoza is an affect-disposition — a stable conative-affective orientation of the mind toward its object, internally grounded in adequate ideas. Typed as Disposition (BFO_0000016) as it is an internally grounded realizable that can manifest in affective processes.

entities.label: KnowledgeToLoveRealizationProcess
entities.rationale: The causal/generative relationship between clear knowledge and true love is a process in which clear knowledge is realized and produces (or co-realizes) the love disposition. Modeled as a Process subclass to capture the productive/causal transition.

relations.rationale: ClearKnowledge is a species of InnateCapacity (existing Disposition class in the ontology), the epistemic faculty for forming clear and distinct ideas.
TrueAndGenuineLove is a Disposition (internally grounded realizable entity) distinct from existing classes.

The process by which clear knowledge produces love is a subspecies of IdeaFormationProcess (existing Process class), as it involves the actualization of adequate cognitive content into an affective disposition.
The realization process has ClearKnowledge as a participant (it is the disposition being realized that drives the process).
TrueAndGenuineLove is produced/realized as an outcome participant of the KnowledgeToLoveRealizationProcess.
ClearKnowledge (as a Disposition/realizable) is realized in the KnowledgeToLoveRealizationProcess, per BFO_0000054 (realized in).

proposal.utterance: Desire comes from experience of particular cases.

entities.label: Desire
entities.rationale: Desire is an internally-grounded tendency or striving inhering in a bearer; it fits BFO Disposition as a realizable entity that is intrinsic to the subject. In Spinoza's framework (conatus/desire), it is a disposition of the finite thing toward self-preservation and action.

entities.label: ExperienceOfParticularCases
entities.rationale: Experience of particular cases is an occurrent process — a happening in time during which a subject encounters and registers particular finite things. It is not a continuant property but an unfolding episode.

entities.label: DesireFormationProcess
entities.rationale: The coming-to-have of a desire disposition through experience is itself a process — the process by which experience of particulars gives rise to (realizes or grounds) the Desire disposition. This captures the 'comes from' causal/genetic claim.

relations.rationale: ExperienceOfParticularCases is a subclass of Process (BFO_0000015).
DesireFormationProcess is a subclass of Process.
Desire is a subclass of Disposition.
The desire-formation process is part of (or unfolds within) the process of experiencing particular cases — it is the aspect of that experience through which desire is constituted.
The DesireFormationProcess realizes the Desire disposition: the disposition is first exhibited/grounded through this process of experiencing particulars.

open_questions: Is 'Desire' here Spinoza's conatus (the striving of each finite thing to persist in its being) or a more cognitive/appetitive notion from the later Ethics (Appetitus/Cupiditas, Part III)? This affects whether Desire should be a subclass of existing working:ModeInstance or working:Disposition and whether its bearer is working:FiniteSingularThing.
Should working:DesireFormationProcess be typed as a subclass of working:IdeaFormationProcess given the existing class, or is desire formation distinct from idea formation in this ontology?
Does 'particular cases' map to existing working:FiniteSingularThing individuals/class, so that ExperienceOfParticularCases should have participants typed as FiniteSingularThing?

proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts a genetic/causal claim: Desire (a disposition inhering in a finite subject) arises from the process of experiencing particular cases. proposal.utterance: Hate arises from error in opinion.

entities.label: Hate
entities.rationale: Hate is an affective state that inheres in a bearer (a mind or person) and is internally grounded — it disposes the bearer toward certain behaviors and responses. BFO Disposition is appropriate as it is an intrinsic, realizable specifically dependent continuant. It is not merely a quality (static measurable property) but an active tendency.

entities.label: ErrorInOpinion
entities.rationale: An error in opinion is a specific epistemic property inhering in a mind or cognitive agent — a defective quality of a belief or judgment. Modeled as a Quality (BFO_0000019), a specifically dependent continuant that characterizes the bearer's cognitive state at a time.

entities.label: HateArisingProcess
entities.rationale: The arising of hate from error is a causal/generative process unfolding in time. Modeling this transition as a Process (BFO_0000015) captures the dynamic relationship between the ErrorInOpinion quality and the Hate disposition.

relations.rationale: Hate is a subclass of Disposition (BFO_0000016), inhering in cognitive/affective bearers.
Error in opinion is a subclass of Quality (BFO_0000019), a defective epistemic property inhering in a mind.
The process of hate arising is a subclass of Process.
The HateArisingProcess has participant ErrorInOpinion — the error is what the process operates on or is triggered by.
The HateArisingProcess realizes the Hate disposition — the process is the realization of hate as it comes about from the error.

open_questions: Is 'hate' here understood in the Spinozistic sense (a passion arising from inadequate ideas / error in first-kind knowledge), or is this a more general claim about the etiology of hate?

Is the 'opinion' (Latin: opinio) the same as Spinoza's first kind of knowledge (imaginatio), in which case should ErrorInOpinion be linked to an ImaginativeKnowledge class?

Should 'Hate' be modeled as a Mode (working:Mode) rather than a bare Disposition, given that in Spinoza's system affects are modes of Substance? The working ontology already has a Mode class (parent BFO_0000020).
Is this claim from a specific text (e.g., the Ethics, the Tractatus)? If so, should provenance relations to working:TheEthics be asserted?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance 'Hate arises from error in opinion' asserts a causal-generative claim: there is a kind of affective state (Hate) that comes about through a process triggered by a defective epistemic quality (ErrorInOpinion). proposal.utterance: Passions arise from error of opinion.

entities.label: Passion
entities.rationale: A passion, in Spinozistic/Stoic usage, is an affective state that inheres in a minded entity — a specifically dependent continuant. The existing individual working:DenialOfPassion presupposes a Passion class. It is a mode/affect, appropriately typed as SDC.

entities.label: ErrorOfOpinion
entities.rationale: An error of opinion is a propositional/cognitive content that can be instantiated in a mind — an information-bearing generically dependent continuant. It is a false or mistaken idea/belief, hence a subtype of representational content (GDC). It is distinct from working:ClearAndDistinctIdea (its opposite) already in the ontology.

entities.label: PassionArisingFromErrorProcess
entities.rationale: The arising (causal production/realization) of a Passion from an ErrorOfOpinion is an occurrent — a process in which the error functions as a participant bringing about the passion. This captures the dynamic 'arise from' relationship asserted in the utterance.

entities.label: PassionArisingDisposition
entities.rationale: The ErrorOfOpinion has an internal grounding — a disposition — to produce or trigger Passions. This models the causal-dispositional aspect: given error, passion tends to arise.

relations.rationale: An ErrorOfOpinion has as part (bears) the PassionArisingDisposition — the disposition inheres in the error-bearing entity and is grounded in the erroneous content.
The PassionArisingDisposition is realized in the PassionArisingFromErrorProcess — the process by which passions come to be.
The PassionArisingFromErrorProcess has as participant an instance of Passion — the passion is brought into being or sustained through this process.
The PassionArisingFromErrorProcess also has the ErrorOfOpinion as participant — the error is the causal input to the process.
A Passion is a kind of Mode (in the Spinozistic sense, a finite modification of substance), which is already modeled as a subclass of BFO_0000020 in the working ontology.

open_questions: Is this utterance Spinozistic (Ethics III) or Stoic (passions as false judgments)? The ontological modeling differs slightly: in Spinoza passions are inadequate ideas causing affects; in Stoicism passions are themselves assents to false impressions. The current modeling treats ErrorOfOpinion as a GDC causing a Passion (SDC), which is compatible with both but could be refined.

Should ErrorOfOpinion be typed as a subclass of working:ClearAndDistinctIdea's complement, or as a distinct branch under Idea (GDC) alongside ClearAndDistinctIdea? We could mint a working:Idea superclass if not already present.
Should 'Passion' be modeled as a subclass of working:Mode (as proposed) or directly under BFO_0000020? The Mode class already exists and Passion fits naturally as a subkind.
Is 'error of opinion' equivalent to working:ErrorOfOpinion as a class of cognitive content, or should a specific individual (e.g., a particular erroneous belief) be modeled here?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance 'Passions arise from error of opinion' asserts a causal-generative relationship: a class of affective states (Passions) is produced by a class of cognitive-representational failures (ErrorOfOpinion). Under BFO, Passion is most naturally a specifically dependent continuant (a Mode, following the already-established working:Mode class), while ErrorOfOpinion is a generically dependent continuant — a type of information/propositional content that can be instantiated in a mind and copied or shared (like other ideas already in the ontology). The causal 'arising' is modeled as a process (PassionArisingFromErrorProcess) triggered by a disposition (PassionArisingDisposition) that inheres in the bearer of the ErrorOfOpinion. This preserves BFO's process/disposition structure while capturing the directional causal claim. The Passion class is placed as a subclass of the existing working:Mode to maintain consistency with prior modeling of finite modifications of substance.

proposal.utterance: True belief teaches what belongs to a thing to be, not what it truly is.

entities.label: TrueBelief
entities.rationale: True belief is a kind of cognitive content that can be instantiated in multiple bearers and communicated; it is an information-bearing pattern, hence a generically dependent continuant. It is distinct from a clear and distinct idea (which gives the true nature of a thing) — here the utterance contrasts true belief with genuine knowledge of essence.

entities.label: BelongingToAThing
entities.rationale: The utterance distinguishes 'what belongs to a thing to be' (its accidental or attributed properties, what predicates hold of it) from what it truly is (its essence). 'Belonging to a thing' as a predicated property is modeled as a Quality — a specifically dependent continuant inhering in the thing.

entities.label: TrueNatureOfAThing
entities.rationale: The utterance contrasts properties-belonging-to with what a thing 'truly is' — its essential nature or essence as quality. This maps onto a quality that constitutes the intrinsic essential character of the thing, distinct from extrinsically attributed properties.

entities.label: TeachingProcess
entities.rationale: The utterance asserts that true belief 'teaches' something — a transmitting or instructing activity is a process in BFO terms.

relations.rationale: TrueBelief is a kind of generically dependent continuant (information content), not a clear and distinct idea of essence.
Attributed properties that belong to a thing are qualities inhering in it.
The true essential nature is a quality constituting the intrinsic character of the thing.
Teaching/instructing is an occurrent process.
The teaching process has true belief as a participant (bearer/content being transmitted).
What is taught in a true-belief teaching process is what belongs to the thing (its attributed properties), not its true nature.

open_questions: Is this utterance from Spinoza's Emendation of the Intellect or the Ethics? The distinction between 'true belief' (vera opinio / historia) and genuine knowledge of essence is key in the TIE; knowing which text would help anchor the individual-level assertions.
Should TrueBelief be modeled as a subclass of ClearAndDistinctIdea (with a negating property) or as disjoint from it? The utterance seems to mark them as contrasting epistemic kinds.
Should 'what a thing truly is' (TrueNatureOfAThing) be linked to EternalInfiniteEssence or to the existing EssenceInvariance quality already in the ontology?

Is BelongingToAThing intended to capture accidental predication (Aristotelian accidents) vs. essential predication? Clarifying this would sharpen the disjointness axiom between BelongingToAThing and TrueNatureOfAThing.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts an epistemic distinction: true belief conveys what properties belong to a thing (its predicated, attributed qualities) but not what the thing truly is (its essence). This is a Spinozistic distinction (prominent in the Treatise on the Emendation of the Intellect) between historia — knowledge of attributes and accidents — and genuine rational or intuitive knowledge of the thing's essence. I model TrueBelief as a generically dependent continuant (information content pattern), BelongingToAThing as the class of quality-type predications that hold of a thing without revealing its essence, and TrueNatureOfAThing as the quality constituting the thing's essential character. A TeachingProcess class is minted to capture the communicative act asserted. The key ontological commitment is the contrast between attributed qualities and essential qualities, both subtypes of BFO Quality. No individuals are committed to — the utterance is a general philosophical claim. The existing EssenceInvariance and EternalInfiniteEssence classes in the ontology are related but not identical; open questions flag whether TrueNatureOfAThing should be aligned with them.

proposal.utterance: All things are necessitated in nature.

entities.label: NecessitationOfAllThings
entities.rationale: The necessity by which all things are determined in nature is a quality inhering in the whole of nature (or in God/Substance). It is a specific property of the natural order, not a disposition (which would imply it might or might not be realized), but a permanent structural feature.

entities.label: NecessitationInNatureDisposition
entities.rationale: The causal-necessitating power inherent in nature by which all things are produced necessarily; this is an internally grounded disposition of the Substance/WholeOfNature to necessitate all things that follow from it.

entities.label: NecessitationOfAllThingsProcess
entities.rationale: The ongoing process by which nature (God/Substance) necessitates all things; the disposition is realized in this process.

relations.rationale: The quality of necessitating all things inheres in the WholeOfNature (or equivalently God as Substance).
The disposition to necessitate all things inheres in the WholeOfNature as its bearer.
The disposition to necessitate all things is realized in the ongoing process of necessitation.
The process of necessitating all things realizes the corresponding disposition of nature.
The WholeOfNature participates in the necessitation process as its principal participant.

open_questions: Should 'all things' here refer specifically to finite modes/particulars (FiniteSingularThing instances) or also to the infinite modes? This affects whether we need a relation linking NecessitationOfAllThingsProcess to FiniteSingularThing as a class.

Is the necessitation here meant in the sense of logical/formal necessity (following from God's nature) or causal necessity (efficient causation)? Spinoza holds both, but the emphasis may affect whether ExistenceNecessitation (already in the ontology) subsumes this or whether NecessitationOfAllThings is a distinct quality.

Should NecessitationOfAllThings be typed as a subclass of ExistenceNecessitation (already present as a disposition) rather than as a separate individual quality? Please confirm whether you want a class or individual here.

Is the bearer of NecessitationOfAllThings God, WholeOfNature, or NaturaNaturans? In the current ontology these are distinct individuals—should we assert this quality of all three or pick one canonical bearer?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance 'All things are necessitated in nature' commits the ontology to the claim that the existence and properties of every thing follow necessarily from the nature of the whole (God/Substance/NaturaNaturans). This is modeled in three layers: (1) a Quality (NecessitationOfAllThings) inhering in WholeOfNature, capturing the structural property that everything in nature is necessitated; (2) a Disposition (NecessitationInNatureDisposition) also inhering in WholeOfNature, capturing the internally grounded power by which this necessitation is enacted; and (3) a Process (NecessitationOfAllThingsProcess) in which that disposition is realized and in which WholeOfNature participates. This parallels the existing pattern for GodNecessaryExistenceDisposition and related individuals. The ExistenceNecessitation class and NecessaryExistenceOfGod individual already in the ontology concern the necessity of God's own existence; the new entities concern the necessity of all derivative things, so they are distinct rather than reuses.

proposal.utterance: In nature, there is no good and no evil.

entities.label: MoralAbsenceInNature
entities.rationale: The claim that nature contains no good and no evil is best modeled as a quality-level assertion about nature as a whole: the absence of moral valence is a characteristic (a quality) of natural things. Typed as a subclass of Quality (BFO_0000019) because it describes a property that inheres in bearers.

entities.label: GoodQuality
entities.rationale: The concept of 'good' as a quality that could inhere in a thing — asserted here to be absent from natural entities. Needed to ground the negation claim.

entities.label: EvilQuality
entities.rationale: The concept of 'evil' as a quality that could inhere in a thing — asserted here to be absent from natural entities. Needed to ground the negation claim.

entities.rationale: The structural feature of nature (or WholeOfNature) that grounds the absence of intrinsic moral valence. Modeled as a Disposition because it is an internally grounded capacity/constraint of the bearer (WholeOfNature/NaturaNaturans) that explains why GoodQuality and EvilQuality do not inhere in natural things.

relations.rationale: WholeOfNature (existing individual) is the bearer of the NaturalValueNeutralityConstraint disposition, grounding the claim that nature as such has no moral valence.

proposal.utterance: Whatever helps attain human perfection is good.

entities.label: HumanPerfection
entities.rationale: Human perfection is a quality or end-state attributed to a human being — a measurable property of a continuant bearer. It is not a disposition (no triggering stimulus/manifestation structure) but rather a quality that a person can approximate or instantiate.

entities.label: Good
entities.rationale: Goodness in this Spinozistic axiom is a relational quality: something is good insofar as it contributes to human perfection. It inheres in the thing that is good and is evaluated relative to a human bearer's perfection.

entities.label: HumanPerfectionContributionDisposition
entities.rationale: The capacity of a thing to help attain human perfection is internally grounded in that thing — a disposition that, when realized, brings about or advances the state of human perfection. This captures 'helps attain' as a realizable structure.

entities.label: HumanPerfectionAttainmentProcess
entities.rationale: The process by which something helps a human attain perfection — the realization of HumanPerfectionContributionDisposition. This process is what the disposition is realized in.

relations.rationale: HumanPerfectionContributionDisposition is realized in HumanPerfectionAttainmentProcess — the disposition manifests when a thing actually contributes to the attainment of human perfection.
NOT asserted — goodness is not a subclass of human perfection but is grounded in relation to it. Left as open question.
Confirms BFO typing of the disposition class under Disposition.

open_questions: In Spinoza's Ethics, 'good' is defined explicitly as whatever helps attain human perfection (Preface to Part IV). Should we encode this as a definitional equivalence — i.e., Good is defined as bearing a HumanPerfectionContributionDisposition — possibly using an OWL equivalentClass axiom?

Should 'HumanPerfection' be typed as a Quality (BFO_0000019) inhering in a human individual, or as an ideal end-state that might be better modeled as a Generically Dependent Continuant (BFO_0000031, an information content entity representing the ideal)? Spinoza's use suggests it is a quality of the individual mind/person.

Is 'Good' here a quality that inheres in things that help attain perfection, or should it be modeled as a Role (BFO_0000023) — something is extrinsically 'good' relative to its contribution? The relational character of Spinoza's goodness (relative to human perfection) suggests a Role may be more appropriate than an intrinsic Quality.
Should we assert an individual or class for 'Human' / 'HumanBeing' to serve as the bearer of HumanPerfection, or reuse an existing class?

The subClassOf relation between Good and HumanPerfection was flagged — should Good be modeled as the quality of 'bearing a HumanPerfectionContributionDisposition', i.e., the two are linked by a value restriction rather than subsumption?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance expresses Spinoza's axiom from Ethics Part IV Preface: goodness is defined relationally as whatever helps a human being attain perfection. Ontologically, this requires: (1) HumanPerfection as a quality inhering in human bearers; (2) Good as a quality (or possibly role) of things that stand in the right relation to human perfection; (3) HumanPerfectionContributionDisposition as the internally-grounded capacity in a thing that — when realized — advances human perfection; and (4) HumanPerfectionAttainmentProcess as the process in which that disposition is realized. The relation erroneously drafted as 'Good rdfs:subClassOf HumanPerfection' should not be committed — it is flagged in open_questions for user resolution. The subClassOf BFO relations for the new classes are implicit in their bfo_type declarations. Key open questions concern whether Good is better typed as a Role (extrinsic, relational) rather than a Quality (intrinsic), and whether an OWL equivalentClass or necessary-and-sufficient condition axiom should capture the definitional character of this claim.

proposal.utterance: Wonder arising from ignorance or prejudice is an imperfection.

entities.label: WonderFromIgnorance
entities.rationale: Wonder arising from ignorance or prejudice is a disposition — an internally grounded tendency of a mind/intellect to be struck by astonishment when lacking adequate knowledge. It is not a quality (it is not a static measurable property) but a disposition that is realized in episodes of wondering. This is a new class.

entities.label: Imperfection
entities.rationale: Imperfection is a quality that inheres in a bearer — it characterizes something as falling short of perfection. It is a measurable/assessable property, hence a Quality. This is a new class.

entities.label: Ignorance
entities.rationale: Ignorance is the disposition of a mind/intellect to lack adequate ideas. It grounds wonder-from-ignorance. Modeled as a Disposition because it is an internally grounded incapacity that manifests in cognitive processes.

entities.label: Prejudice
entities.rationale: Prejudice is a disposition to judge prior to adequate rational investigation. It is internally grounded in the bearer (a finite intellect). It is a co-cause of wonder-from-ignorance.

relations.rationale: WonderFromIgnorance is a subclass of Disposition (BFO_0000016).
Imperfection is a subclass of Quality (BFO_0000019).
Ignorance is a subclass of Disposition (BFO_0000016).
Prejudice is a subclass of Disposition (BFO_0000016).

The assertion that wonder-from-ignorance IS an imperfection is modeled by making WonderFromIgnorance a subclass of Imperfection. However, WonderFromIgnorance is a Disposition and Imperfection is a Quality — this is a cross-category subClassOf, which BFO-strict reasoning may flag. This is flagged in open_questions.

open_questions: The utterance asserts that wonder-from-ignorance 'is' an imperfection. In BFO, WonderFromIgnorance is a Disposition (BFO_0000016) and Imperfection is a Quality (BFO_0000019). These are disjoint BFO categories, so a strict rdfs:subClassOf relation between them would violate BFO disjointness axioms. Should we instead model this as: every instance of WonderFromIgnorance is accompanied by (co-occurs with / is correlated with) an instance of Imperfection inhering in the same bearer? Or should we treat WonderFromIgnorance itself as a Quality (a static property) rather than a Disposition?

Is 'wonder' here Spinoza's concept from the Ethics (Appendix to Part I or Part III) where he criticizes wonder arising from ignorance? Confirming the textual source would help determine whether this should be linked to working:TheEthics.
Should Ignorance and Prejudice be modeled as dispositions of working:FiniteSingularThing or specifically of a finite intellect (similar to working:TrueIntellect but its deficient counterpart)?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts that wonder arising from ignorance or prejudice is an imperfection — a claim characteristic of Spinoza's critique of final-cause thinking in the Ethics. I introduce four new classes: WonderFromIgnorance (a Disposition, because it is an internally grounded tendency of a finite mind lacking adequate ideas), Imperfection (a Quality, as it characterizes a bearer as falling short), Ignorance (a Disposition grounding inadequate cognition), and Prejudice (a Disposition to judge without rational investigation). The critical ontological tension is that asserting WonderFromIgnorance is a subclass of Imperfection crosses BFO category boundaries (Disposition vs. Quality), which HermiT will likely flag as inconsistent. Alternative modeling strategies — such as a property-chain axiom or a co-occurrence relation — are raised in open_questions for the user to resolve before committing.

proposal.utterance: Love arises from perception and knowledge of a thing.

entities.label: Love
entities.rationale: Love in Spinozist context is an affect or disposition inhering in a mind/person, internally grounded in the nature of the bearer (an emotion arising from within upon perception). Disposition is the best BFO fit for an internally grounded capacity or affect.

entities.label: Perception
entities.rationale: Perception is a cognitive process unfolding in time through which a perceiver apprehends something. Best typed as a Process (occurrent).

entities.label: KnowledgeOfAThing
entities.rationale: Knowledge of a thing in Spinoza's framework is an internally grounded cognitive state or capacity inhering in a mind. Disposition is appropriate as knowledge is an intrinsic, internally grounded property of the knower. Note: could also be modeled as ClearAndDistinctIdea (GDC) but 'knowledge of a thing' is broader than a clear and distinct idea.

entities.label: LoveArisingProcess
entities.rationale: The arising of Love from perception and knowledge is itself a process — a causal or generative occurrence unfolding in time that results in Love being realized.

relations.rationale: The process by which love arises is analogous to an idea-formation process in Spinoza — it involves cognitive and perceptual activity leading to an affective state.
Love (as a disposition/affect) is realized in the LoveArisingProcess — the process of perceiving and knowing a thing triggers/realizes the disposition of love.
The LoveArisingProcess has Perception as a participant — perception is a constituent process/participant in the arising of love.
The LoveArisingProcess has KnowledgeOfAThing as a participant — knowledge of the thing is also a constituent in the arising of love.
Perception in Spinoza is a form of idea formation — the apprehension of a thing through the intellect or senses involves forming an idea of that thing.

open_questions: Is 'Love' here intended as a Spinozist affect (an emotion arising from increased power of acting, as in Ethics III), or a more general concept of love? This affects whether Love should be a Disposition or perhaps a Quality (a felt state) or even a specifically dependent continuant of another kind.

Should 'Perception' be distinguished from 'Knowledge' (cognitio) as in Spinoza's three kinds of knowledge (imagination/opinion, reason, intuition)? If so, these may need to be modeled as separate subclasses with distinct epistemic grades.
Is 'KnowledgeOfAThing' intended to be the same as or a superclass of the existing 'ClearAndDistinctIdea' class, or is it a broader, possibly lower-grade cognitive state (e.g., imaginative knowledge)?
Should Love inhere in a specific bearer (e.g., a finite mind or the TrueIntellect individual), or is it being asserted as a general class-level claim about love in any cognizer?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance 'Love arises from perception and knowledge of a thing' asserts a causal/generative relationship among three new ontological items: Love (an affect or disposition), Perception (a cognitive process), and Knowledge of a thing (a cognitive disposition or state). In Spinozist metaphysics, love is an affect — a modification of the mind involving increased power — which is internally grounded and arises through the cognitive activity of perceiving and knowing something. I therefore model Love as a Disposition (BFO_0000016), Perception and LoveArisingProcess as Processes (BFO_0000015), and KnowledgeOfAThing as a Disposition. The LoveArisingProcess is the occurrent in which Love is realized, with Perception and KnowledgeOfAThing as participants. Perception is sub-typed under IdeaFormationProcess to connect it to the existing ontology. Several open questions remain about epistemic grade distinctions and the exact BFO typing of Love.

entities.rationale: The greatness/magnificence of an object as perceived is a quality inhering in the object (or the idea of it). Modeled as a Quality (BFO_0000019) because it is a measurable/gradable property attributed to the object.

entities.rationale: The degree or intensity of love is a quality of the love-disposition (or of the affect itself), expressible as a gradient. This captures the claim that love 'increases'.

entities.rationale: The process by which love increases in proportion to perceived magnitude of its object. This is an occurrent, capturing the dynamic claim in the utterance.

relations.rationale: LoveIntensity is a quality that characterizes instances of the Love disposition; it is naturally associated with Love as a sub-quality profile.
The LoveAugmentationProcess realizes the Love disposition — the process of love increasing is the realization of the underlying disposition in response to perceived magnitude.
The LoveAugmentationProcess has PerceivedMagnitude as a participant (the quality of the object that drives the augmentation process).

entities.rationale: Confidence is a kind of Joy (an affect/idea type in Spinoza), defined as a subtype. Since Joy itself would be a generically dependent continuant (a pattern of affective content), Confidence inherits that typing. However, Joy is not yet in the ontology, so we must mint it or note the dependency.

entities.label: Joy
entities.rationale: Joy is a basic Spinozistic affect — a pattern of increasing power/perfection. As an affect-type (a representational/information content pattern that can be multiply instantiated as modes), it fits GDC. We also mint Affect as its parent.

entities.label: Affect
entities.rationale: In Spinoza, affects are defined patterns of the mind's power of thinking — representational/intentional content types. Modeled as GDC (information/pattern) rather than SDC because the same affect-type can be copied/instantiated across many minds. This serves as the top affect class.

entities.label: Sadness
entities.rationale: Sadness is the contrasting basic affect referenced in the definition of Confidence (joy 'not mixed with sadness'). Needs to be in the ontology to express the disjointness/absence relation.

entities.label: FutureGoodConception
entities.rationale: The conception of a future good as necessary is the intentional content (idea) that gives rise to Confidence. As an idea-type it is a GDC, and it is a subtype of ClearAndDistinctIdea (or more broadly Idea) already in the ontology.

entities.label: NecessityQuality
entities.rationale: The definition specifies the future good is conceived as necessary — necessity here is a quality attributed to the conceived object within the idea. Modeled as a Quality class.

entities.label: ConfidenceArisingProcess
entities.rationale: The 'arising' of Confidence from conceiving a future good as necessary is a process — the causal/generative event by which the Confidence affect is produced in a mind.

relations.rationale: Joy is a species of Affect in Spinoza's taxonomy.

Confidence is defined as a kind of Joy — direct subclass relation.

entities.label: Despair

Modeling it as a Quality subclass under Sadness follows the pattern used for other Spinozist affects.

entities.label: Sadness
entities.rationale: Sadness is a fundamental Spinozist affect-quality (passage to a lesser perfection). It must be introduced as a class if not already present, as Despair is defined as a species of it.

entities.label: FutureThingConceived
entities.rationale: The cognitive content 'conceiving a future thing as necessarily evil' is an idea or mental representation — a generically dependent continuant (information content) that can be instantiated in a mind. This is the intentional object grounding Despair.

entities.label: NecessarilyEvilQuality
entities.rationale: The quality of being conceived as necessarily evil is a quality attributed (via cognition) to a future thing — it is the modal-evaluative quality that distinguishes the object of Despair from objects of other sadness-subspecies such as Fear.

entities.label: DespairArisingProcess
entities.rationale: The arising of Despair from conceiving a future thing as necessarily evil is a process — a temporal unfolding in which the cognitive representation triggers or realizes the affect-quality of Despair.

relations.rationale: Despair is a kind of sadness — direct genus-species relation.

open_questions: Should 'Sadness' be typed purely as a BFO Quality, or should it also carry a Disposition component (as Spinoza's affects involve both a phenomenal quality and a conative-dispositional aspect)?

Should 'FutureThingConceived' be a subclass of 'ClearAndDistinctIdea' (which carries positive epistemic valence in Spinoza) or just a plain BFO_0000031 generically dependent continuant, since the conceiving here may be adequate or inadequate?

Spinoza contrasts Despair with Fear (same structure but the future thing is conceived as possibly, not necessarily, evil) — should 'Fear' be introduced now as a sibling class under Sadness for structural completeness?

Should 'NecessarilyEvilQuality' be typed as a Quality inhering in the conceived object, or rather as part of the propositional content of the FutureThingConceived idea (i.e., a part of the GDC rather than a separate Quality)?

Is 'DespairArisingProcess' the right modeling choice, or should the causal link between conceiving and despair be captured purely via a BFO Disposition that is realized in the affect, without a separate arising-process class?
proposal.rationale_summary: Spinoza's definition (Ethics III, Def. of the Affects 15) identifies Despair as a species of Sadness whose differentia is the modal character of its intentional object: the future thing is conceived as necessarily (not merely possibly) evil. The cognitive content that grounds Despair ('a future thing conceived as necessarily evil') is modeled as a generically dependent continuant class (FutureThingConceived), following the existing use of ClearAndDistinctIdea and related idea-classes; however, an open question flags whether this should subclass ClearAndDistinctIdea or remain a plain GDC. The modal-evaluative character of the object is captured by NecessarilyEvilQuality. The causal/arising relation is represented by DespairArisingProcess (a Process), which realizes the Despair quality and has as participant the FutureThingConceived. No existing individuals or classes in the current ontology map directly to Sadness or Despair, so new classes are minted.

proposal.utterance: Hope, Fear, Confidence, Despair, and Jealousy arise from incorrect opinion.

entities.label: Hope
entities.rationale: Hope in Spinoza's psychology is an affective disposition (an affect) inhering in a finite thing, contingently directed toward a future good; best typed as Disposition (internally grounded tendency).

entities.label: Fear
entities.rationale: Fear is the complementary affect to Hope, an affective disposition toward a future ill; typed as Disposition.

entities.label: Confidence
entities.rationale: Confidence (securitas) in Spinoza is Hope without admixture of doubt—an affective disposition; typed as Disposition.

entities.label: Despair
entities.rationale: Despair is Fear without doubt—an affective disposition directed toward certain future ill; typed as Disposition.

entities.label: Jealousy
entities.rationale: Jealousy (invidia/zelotypia) is an affective disposition arising from fluctuating hope and fear regarding the love or attention of another; typed as Disposition.

entities.label: IncorrectOpinion
entities.rationale: An incorrect opinion is a cognitive content—a propositional or representational pattern that can be held by multiple minds—best typed as a generically dependent continuant (information/cognitive content). It is distinct from the affect it gives rise to.

entities.label: AffectArisingFromIncorrectOpinion
entities.rationale: A superclass grouping Hope, Fear, Confidence, Despair, and Jealousy as affective dispositions that Spinoza characterises as arising from incorrect (inadequate) opinion; allows the shared origin to be modelled structurally.

relations.rationale: Hope is one of the affects Spinoza places in the category arising from incorrect opinion.
Fear is one of the affects Spinoza places in this category.
Confidence (securitas) derives from Hope and hence from incorrect opinion.
Despair derives from Fear and hence from incorrect opinion.
Jealousy arises from the fluctuation of Hope and Fear, thus rooted in incorrect opinion.

Should Hope, Fear, etc. be typed as Quality (BFO_0000019) rather than Disposition (BFO_0000016), since they may be more like occurrent affective states than internal tendencies? Or should we have both a dispositional and a quality layer?

2. 'Incorrect opinion' is rendered here as a generically dependent continuant (cognitive content). Should it instead be a quality of the intellect (BFO_0000019) inhering in the mind/intellect bearer, or kept as GDC? This turns on whether we treat opinion as a content-type or as a mental state-token.

3. The relation BFO_0000054 (realized in) requires a process individual on its target. Should we mint a process class 'IncorrectOpinionGroundingProcess' to serve as the realization context for these affect-dispositions, or model the causal link differently (e.g., via a custom 'arises from' annotation property)?

4. Should 'Confidence' and 'Despair' be modelled as subclasses of Hope and Fear respectively (as Spinoza does in Ethics III), or is flat subclassing under AffectArisingFromIncorrectOpinion sufficient at this stage?
5. Is this utterance drawing on the Short Treatise (Part II, Ch. 9–10) or the Ethics (Part III, Definitions of the Affects)? The source text may affect how we type and relate these entities.

Each affect is modelled as a class of Disposition (BFO_0000016) because each is an internally-grounded, contingent tendency of a finite mind directed toward uncertain or misrepresented future states. A grouping class AffectArisingFromIncorrectOpinion is introduced as their common parent to carry the ontological commitment about shared origin. 'Incorrect opinion' is modelled as a class of generically dependent continuant (BFO_0000031)—a representational content-type that can be instantiated in multiple minds—rather than as a quality, on the grounds that it is fundamentally a propositional pattern. Several open questions are flagged because the Quality-vs-Disposition choice for affects, the GDC-vs-Quality choice for opinion, and the realization relation modelling all involve interpretive decisions that depend on which Spinoza text is being formalized and what level of granularity is desired.

proposal.utterance: All things have necessary causes and must happen as they do happen.

entities.label: CausalNecessityPrinciple
entities.rationale: The claim 'all things have necessary causes and must happen as they do' is a specific propositional content — a philosophical thesis that can be instantiated in multiple texts. It is best typed as a generically dependent continuant (information content entity / philosophical thesis).

entities.label: CausalDetermination
entities.rationale: The disposition inhering in things whereby each thing is disposed to occur in exactly one way given its causes. This models the internal grounding of causal necessity — that each thing has a causal structure that necessitates its occurrence.

entities.label: CausallyNecessitatedOccurrence
entities.rationale: A class of processes that are the realization of CausalDetermination dispositions — i.e., events/happenings that occur as they must given their necessary causes.

entities.label: NecessaryCause
entities.rationale: The role played by an entity that stands as a necessary (i.e., sufficient and unavoidable) cause of another thing. Externally grounded — something bears this role relative to its effect.

relations.rationale: CausalDetermination dispositions are realized in CausallyNecessitatedOccurrence processes — the necessity of cause is expressed as the occurrence happening as it must.
The thesis 'all things have necessary causes and must happen as they do' is a generically dependent continuant — a propositional content that can be tokened in texts (e.g., TheEthics).
This principle is a part of (content expressed within) TheEthics, which is already in the ontology as a generically dependent continuant.
CausalDetermination is a more specific kind of the constraint on production already modeled — all things being causally determined is a constraint on how substance produces its modes.

open_questions: Should CausalDetermination be treated as a universal disposition inhering in all things (modes and substance alike), or only in finite modes? Spinoza's causal necessity applies universally but the locus of the disposition differs (God/Substance vs. finite things).

Is the utterance specifically asserting Spinoza's doctrine of causal necessity (Ethics IP29, IP33) — that there are no contingent things — or a more generic causal principle? This affects whether CausalNecessityPrinciple should be linked to TheEthics or treated as a standalone axiom.

Should 'NecessaryCause' be modeled as a Role (externally grounded) or as a Disposition (internally grounded)? In Spinoza, God is causa sui so self-causation may require a Disposition, whereas efficient causation of finite things is a Role.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts the Spinozistic doctrine of universal causal necessity: every thing has a necessary cause and could not have happened otherwise. I model this with four entities: (1) CausalNecessityPrinciple, an individual generically dependent continuant representing the propositional content of this thesis, linked as a part of TheEthics; (2) CausalDetermination, a class of dispositions inhering in things that grounds their being causally necessitated — typed as Disposition (BFO_0000016) and placed as a subclass of the existing SubstanceProductionConstraint; (3) CausallyNecessitatedOccurrence, a class of processes that are the realizations of those dispositions; and (4) NecessaryCause, a Role class for things that stand as necessary causes. These reuse existing infrastructure (SubstanceProductionConstraint, TheEthics) and introduce only what the utterance strictly commits to. The realization relation connects dispositions to the processes they ground, consistent with BFO's disposition-realization model.

proposal.utterance: Love of Esteem and Shame are injurious and objectionable.

entities.label: LoveOfEsteem
entities.rationale: Love of Esteem (gloria/vainglory in Spinoza) is a disposition inhering in a mind/person — a tendency to seek the esteem of others. Typed as Disposition (BFO_0000016) since it is internally grounded in its bearer and can be realized in behavior.

entities.label: Shame

entities.label: ObjectionableAffectQuality

proposal.utterance: Love, desire, and everything proper to love are essential to our being and persistence.

entities.label: Love
entities.rationale: Love in Spinoza's framework is an active affective disposition (affect toward an external cause of joy) inhering in a finite thing; it is internally grounded, making Disposition the best BFO fit.

entities.label: Desire
entities.rationale: Desire (cupiditas) in Spinoza is the very essence of a person as conatus — a striving disposition internally grounded in the bearer. Disposition is the correct BFO type.

entities.label: Conatus
entities.rationale: Conatus is the striving of each thing to persist in its own being — the foundational internally-grounded disposition underlying love and desire in Spinoza. Essential to being and persistence.

entities.label: AffectEssentiality
entities.rationale: The claim that love, desire and related affects are *essential* to being and persistence can be captured as a quality — the property of being affect-essential — borne by finite things.

entities.label: Affect
entities.rationale: Affect (affectus) is Spinoza's general category for modifications of the conatus — increases or decreases of the power of acting. It is an internally-grounded disposition of the bearer. Love and Desire are subclasses.

AffectEssentiality is a specific form of EssentialExistenceQuality — the quality of being essentially constituted by affective dispositions.

This is grounded in the doctrine of conatus (E3p6-9): each thing strives to persist in its own being, and this striving, when conscious, is desire; love is an affect arising from that striving augmented by an external cause of joy. In BFO terms, these are best modeled as Dispositions (BFO_0000016) because they are internally grounded in the bearer and can be realized in processes of persistence and action. A general Affect class is introduced as the superclass of Love and Desire, with Conatus as the foundational striving disposition that grounds desire specifically. The essentiality of these affects to being is captured by a new AffectEssentiality quality (subclass of the existing EssentialExistenceQuality), which FiniteSingularThing is related to. An open question flags that the universal bearer relation should ideally be expressed as an OWL restriction rather than a subclassOf link.
