proposal.utterance: Evil passions are not essential; we can exist properly only by freeing ourselves from them.

entities.label: EvilPassion
entities.rationale: Evil passions in Spinozistic context are passions (passive affects) that arise from inadequate ideas and external causes; they are internally-grounded tendencies of finite things to be acted upon in harmful ways — best typed as Disposition (BFO_0000016). They are not essential qualities (Quality) because the proposition explicitly asserts they are non-essential.

entities.label: NonEssentialityQuality
entities.rationale: The proposition asserts that evil passions are not essential — i.e., they are accidental, non-essential qualities of a being. This non-essentiality is a quality of the disposition: it does not belong to the essence of the bearer.

entities.label: LiberationProcess
entities.rationale: The freeing of oneself from evil passions is a process — an unfolding in time by which an entity transitions from passivity to activity. This aligns with Spinoza's ethics of liberation.

entities.label: ProperExistenceQuality
entities.rationale: Existing 'properly' (in one's true or adequate mode of existence) is a quality of the finite thing — the quality of existing in accordance with one's essential nature. This is distinct from mere existence; it captures adequacy/virtue in Spinoza's sense.

entities.label: LiberationDisposition
entities.rationale: The capacity or tendency of a finite thing to free itself from evil passions through active reason — an internally grounded disposition realized in the liberation process.

relations.rationale: Evil passions are a subclass of Disposition, being internally-grounded tendencies toward passive affection.
Non-essentiality is a Quality inhering in bearers of EvilPassion, marking those dispositions as accidental.
Freeing oneself from evil passions is a temporal process.
Proper existence is a quality of finite singular things that have undergone liberation.
Liberation capacity is a disposition of finite things.
The liberation disposition is realized in the liberation process (BFO realized-in relation).
Evil passions are modes (specifically passive modes) of finite things in Spinoza's system, consistent with Mode as SDC subclass already in the ontology.
Proper existence aligns with EssenceInvariance — existing in accordance with one's essential nature — already represented in the ontology.

open_questions: Should 'evil passions' be modeled as a subclass of Mode (already in ontology as SDC) rather than directly under Disposition? In Spinoza, passions are modes, but they also function dispositionally — should we use both inheritance paths or pick one?
Is 'proper existence' here equivalent to or a subtype of EssenceInvariance already in the ontology, or does it add something new (e.g., active virtue)?
Should LiberationProcess be linked to FiniteSingularThing as participant (RO_0000057), or is that too specific without a named individual?
Is the 'freeing from passions' process here Spinoza-specific (Ethics Part V), or intended as a more general philosophical claim? This affects whether we should flag TheEthics as the source.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance makes three ontological commitments: (1) evil passions exist but are not essential to a being — they are accidental, non-essential dispositions (BFO_0000016) and modes (Mode already in ontology); (2) there is a quality of proper or adequate existence (ProperExistenceQuality, BFO_0000019) that finite beings can instantiate; (3) freeing oneself from evil passions is a real process (LiberationProcess, BFO_0000015) that realizes a disposition (LiberationDisposition) inherent in finite things. Evil passions are typed as Disposition rather than Quality because they are tendencies/capacities to be affected passively — they manifest conditionally. Non-essentiality is separately typed as a Quality because it characterizes the accidental nature of those passions relative to the bearer's essence. ProperExistenceQuality is plausibly a subtype of EssenceInvariance already in the ontology. No new individuals are warranted; all commitments are general (class-level). The relation between EvilPassion and Mode reuses the existing Mode class.

proposal.utterance: Love of a corruptible object necessarily produces hate, sadness, and related passions.

entities.label: LoveOf
entities.rationale: Love toward an object is an internally grounded disposition of a mind/agent toward that object; it can be realized in affective processes.

entities.label: LoveOfCorruptibleObject

entities.label: Hate
entities.rationale: Hate is an affective disposition (passion) inhering in a subject; parallel structure to Love.

entities.label: Sadness
entities.rationale: Sadness is an affective disposition (passion) resulting from loss or anticipated loss of a loved object.

entities.label: Passion
entities.rationale: Passion (passio) is a general class for externally-caused affective dispositions in Spinozistic framework; Hate and Sadness are subclasses.

entities.label: NecessaryPassionProductionDisposition
entities.rationale: The disposition of LoveOfCorruptibleObject to necessarily produce Hate, Sadness, and related passions; captures the modal force ('necessarily produces') as a disposition realized in passion-formation processes.

entities.label: PassionFormationProcess
entities.rationale: The process by which love of a corruptible object is realized in the production of hate, sadness, and related passions.

relations.rationale: Hate is a species of passion (externally caused affective disposition).
Sadness is a species of passion.

The disposition is realized in a passion-formation process (BFO: realized in).
The passion-formation process has hate (as a disposition instance) as a participant/output.
The passion-formation process has sadness as a participant/output.

proposal.utterance: Truth manifests both itself and falsity; falsity is never manifested through itself.

entities.label: Truth
entities.rationale: Truth in Spinoza's epistemology is a quality or property of ideas — specifically of adequate ideas — that inheres in the intellect bearing them. Typed as Quality (BFO_0000019) under the specifically dependent continuant branch.

entities.label: Falsity
entities.rationale: Falsity is a quality of inadequate ideas, the privation or deficiency aspect of an idea. Typed as Quality (BFO_0000019) as the correlative deficient property opposed to Truth.

entities.label: TruthManifestsItselfDisposition
entities.rationale: Spinoza's claim that truth is its own standard (norma sui) is best captured as a disposition: truth, when instantiated, is intrinsically disposed to make both itself and falsity manifest. This is internally grounded in the nature of a true idea, fitting BFO Disposition.

entities.label: SelfManifestation
entities.rationale: The manifesting of truth (of itself and of falsity) is an occurrent process — a happening in which the truth of an idea becomes evident to the intellect. Typed as Process (BFO_0000015).

entities.label: FalsityNonSelfManifestationConstraint
entities.rationale: The claim that falsity is never manifested through itself is a structural constraint on falsity: it lacks the intrinsic disposition to reveal itself. Modeled as a Disposition (an internally grounded realizable) whose realization is blocked — or rather as the absence/lack disposition. This captures the epistemic asymmetry Spinoza asserts.

relations.rationale: TruthManifestsItselfDisposition is a subclass of BFO Disposition.
Truth is a subclass of BFO Quality.
Falsity is a subclass of BFO Quality.
The disposition to manifest itself and falsity is realized in a SelfManifestation process — 'realized in' (BFO_0000054).
The SelfManifestation process has Truth as a participant — it is the process in which truth makes itself evident.
The SelfManifestation process also has Falsity as a participant — truth in manifesting itself simultaneously manifests falsity as its contrast/privation.
FalsityNonSelfManifestationConstraint is a subclass of BFO Disposition capturing the absence of self-revealing capacity in falsity.

open_questions: Should Truth and Falsity be modeled as qualities of Ideas (inhering in instances of ClearAndDistinctIdea or its complement InadequateIdea) rather than as top-level quality classes? This would require minting an InadequateIdea class to serve as the bearer of Falsity.
Should 'norma sui' (truth as its own standard) be explicitly linked to an existing individual such as TrueIntellect, given that for Spinoza truth inheres in the intellect of God/Nature?

Is FalsityNonSelfManifestationConstraint best modeled as a negative disposition (a lacking) or rather as an annotation/axiom stating that no instance of Falsity bears TruthManifestsItselfDisposition? The latter may be more OWL-appropriate.
Should SelfManifestation be linked to TrueIntellect as the bearer/participant in whose intellect the manifestation occurs?
proposal.rationale_summary: Spinoza's dictum 'Veritas norma sui et falsi est' (Ethics II P43S) asserts an epistemic asymmetry: a true idea, by its intrinsic nature, reveals both itself as true and its opposite as false, while falsity has no corresponding self-revealing power. In BFO terms: Truth and Falsity are Qualities (BFO_0000019) that inhere in ideas. The self-manifesting character of truth is internally grounded and therefore fits a Disposition (BFO_0000016) — TruthManifestsItselfDisposition — which is realized in a process of SelfManifestation (BFO_0000015) that has both Truth and Falsity as participants. The asymmetry on falsity's side is captured by FalsityNonSelfManifestationConstraint, a disposition class that models the structural incapacity of falsity to reveal itself. Several open questions arise about where exactly these qualities inhere (in ideas, in an intellect) and whether InadequateIdea should be minted as the bearer of Falsity.

proposal.utterance: The Will is only a mode of thinking, a Being of Reason, not a Real Being.

entities.label: Will
entities.rationale: Spinoza explicitly states Will is a mode of thinking — a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in a bearer (Thought/Substance). It is typed as a subclass of Mode (already in ontology), which is itself a subclass of BFO_0000020.

entities.label: ModeOfThinking
entities.rationale: The utterance categorizes Will as a mode of thinking specifically. A class ModeOfThinking (subclass of Mode) captures this genus before the differentia 'Will' is applied. Reuses Mode from existing ontology.

entities.label: BeingOfReason
entities.rationale: A 'Being of Reason' (ens rationis) in Spinoza is a conceptual/intellectual construct — a pattern of thought that can be abstracted and communicated, with no independent real existence. This fits BFO generically dependent continuant (information artifact / abstract pattern). It is explicitly contrasted with 'Real Being'.

entities.label: RealBeing
entities.rationale: A 'Real Being' (ens reale) is something that exists independently in nature. BFO independent continuant is the best fit, as it persists and exists without needing to inhere in another entity. Will is denied this status in the utterance.

entities.label: WillNotRealBeingQuality
entities.rationale: The ontological status of Will as lacking real being is a quality (a specifically dependent property) that can be attributed to instances of Will — it is a denial of independent real existence, expressible as a quality inhering in Will instances.

relations.rationale: Will is a species of ModeOfThinking per Spinoza's assertion.
ModeOfThinking is a subclass of Mode (already in ontology), restricted to modes inhering in the attribute of Thought.

The quality of not being a Real Being inheres in Will instances — it is a specifically dependent property of Will.

open_questions: Should 'BeingOfReason' (ens rationis) be modeled as a subclass of BFO_0000031 (generically dependent continuant) as proposed, or would you prefer it as a subclass of BFO_0000020 (specifically dependent continuant), given that for Spinoza beings of reason are mind-dependent conceptual tools rather than information artifacts in the usual sense?
The utterance implies Will lacks causal or productive power — should a DispositionAbsence or a negative quality be added to capture that Will has no efficacious disposition (unlike God's attributes)?
Should we also represent the Intellect (already in ontology as an individual 'TrueIntellect') as another example of a ModeOfThinking, parallel to Will, to build out the category?
Spinoza's 'Thought' is currently an individual typed as BFO_0000019 (Quality). Should it instead be an Attribute (a DivineAttribute individual) to properly serve as the bearer of modes of thinking?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts three ontological claims: (1) Will is a mode of thinking — typed as a subclass of the existing Mode class, under a new intermediate class ModeOfThinking that restricts modes to those inhering in the attribute of Thought; (2) Will is a Being of Reason (ens rationis) — a class BeingOfReason is minted as a generically dependent continuant, capturing the Spinozistic notion of conceptual constructs with no independent existence in natura; (3) Will is NOT a Real Being (ens reale) — a class RealBeing is minted as an independent continuant to represent what Will is denied to be, and a quality WillNotRealBeingQuality is introduced to explicitly represent this ontological demotion inhering in Will. The key BFO modeling challenge is the Being of Reason / Real Being distinction: BFO_0000031 (generically dependent continuant) is chosen for BeingOfReason because beings of reason are mind-dependent patterns or constructs, while BFO_0000004 (independent continuant) is chosen for RealBeing because real beings exist in and through themselves. An open question is raised about whether Thought should be retyped from Quality to DivineAttribute to properly ground the inheres-in relation for modes of thinking.

entities.label: ExNihiloNihilFit
entities.rationale: The principle 'nothing comes from nothing' (ex nihilo nihil fit) is a propositional content — an information artifact or philosophical thesis whose identity is pattern-based and can be instantiated in multiple bearers (texts, minds). BFO_0000031 (generically dependent continuant) is the appropriate type. It is a specific, named principle, so it is an individual.

entities.label: CausalGroundednessConstraint
entities.rationale: The ontological content of ex nihilo nihil fit is that every entity or process has a cause or ground — i.e., nothing is uncaused. This is best captured as a disposition class: the disposition of any thing to be causally grounded. It is internally grounded in the nature of existents and would be realized in any causal process. This is a general kind, so it is a class.

relations.rationale: ExNihiloNihilFit is an instance of PhilosophicalWork (a generically dependent continuant class already in the ontology), since it is a named philosophical principle/thesis.
CausalGroundednessConstraint is a subclass of Disposition (BFO_0000016), expressing the internally grounded necessity for any entity or process to have a causal source.

CausalGroundednessConstraint is a more specific constraint than SubstanceProductionConstraint already in the ontology; in Spinoza's context, nothing produced from nothing is intimately related to how substance production is constrained.

proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance 'Nothing comes from nothing' (ex nihilo nihil fit) is a classical metaphysical axiom. It has two aspects to represent: (1) the propositional content — modeled as an individual of type PhilosophicalWork (a generically dependent continuant), named ExNihiloNihilFit; and (2) the ontological constraint it expresses — that every entity or process must have a causal ground, modeled as a new disposition class CausalGroundednessConstraint, which is a subclass of both BFO Disposition (BFO_0000016) and the existing SubstanceProductionConstraint, since in the Spinozist context this principle grounds why substance cannot arise from nothing and reinforces the causal necessity already partially captured by SubstanceProductionConstraint. proposal.utterance: An idea can be feigned only after the mind first knows the thing itself of which abstractions are made.

entities.label: FeigningProcess
entities.rationale: Feigning (fictio) is an occurrent process by which the mind constructs or entertains a fictional idea. It is a happening that unfolds in time.

entities.label: AbstractionProcess
entities.rationale: Abstraction is a cognitive process by which the mind strips away particulars from a thing known to form a more general or partial representation. It is a process occurrent.

entities.label: PriorKnowledgeOfThing
entities.rationale: Prior knowledge of the thing itself is an internally grounded capacity/disposition of the mind that must be present before feigning or abstraction can occur. It grounds the possibility of those subsequent processes.

entities.label: FeigningPreconditionConstraint
entities.rationale: The constraint that feigning is only possible after prior knowledge of the thing exists is itself a disposition-like structural rule inhering in the mind. Models Spinoza's epistemic precondition on feigning.

entities.label: FeignedIdea
entities.rationale: A feigned idea is an information-like content (a constructed mental representation) that can in principle be copied or tokened; it is the product of a FeigningProcess. As an idea-content it is a generically dependent continuant.

relations.rationale: AbstractionProcess is a subclass of Process.
FeigningProcess is a subclass of Process.
FeigningPreconditionConstraint is a subclass of Disposition.
PriorKnowledgeOfThing is a subclass of Disposition.
A FeigningProcess realizes the FeigningPreconditionConstraint disposition — the constraint is actualized when feigning occurs.
According to the utterance, abstractions are made as part of feigning; AbstractionProcess is part of FeigningProcess.

The utterance involves 'the mind' — should an individual or class for Mind be introduced here, serving as the bearer of PriorKnowledgeOfThing and FeigningPreconditionConstraint?

Should AbstractionProcess be a proper part-of FeigningProcess (temporal part), or merely a prerequisite process that temporally precedes FeigningProcess? The utterance says abstractions are 'made' during feigning, but this could also be read as a precondition.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts an epistemic ordering: feigning an idea requires the mind to first know the thing from which abstractions are drawn. Ontologically this introduces (1) FeigningProcess — the occurrent act of constructing a feigned idea; (2) AbstractionProcess — a sub-process or constituent process of feigning in which particulars are stripped away; (3) PriorKnowledgeOfThing — a disposition of the mind that must be present before feigning can occur; (4) FeigningPreconditionConstraint — a dispositional rule capturing that feigning is conditioned on prior knowledge; and (5) FeignedIdea — the generically dependent continuant that is the output of a FeigningProcess. The existing individual IncompatibilityOfImpossibleSuppositionWithFeigning is related but captures a different commitment (the incompatibility of impossible suppositions with feigning), so new classes are warranted. No individuals are minted because the utterance states a general principle, not a particular event.

proposal.utterance: Some Ideas are impossible to instantiate in nature, such as hybrid creatures combining two natures.

entities.label: ImpossibleIdea
entities.rationale: An impossible idea is an informational/conceptual content — a pattern that can be encoded, transmitted, or instantiated (or attempted to be instantiated) — fitting BFO's generically dependent continuant. The claim is that such ideas cannot be realized in nature, not that they lack ontological status as ideas.

entities.label: NatureInstantiability
entities.rationale: The capacity or disposition of an idea to be instantiated (realized) in nature. Impossible ideas lack this disposition, possible ideas bear it. Typed as Disposition (BFO_0000016) because it is an internally grounded realizable property of the idea.

entities.label: HybridNatureIdea
entities.rationale: A subclass of ImpossibleIdea representing ideas that combine two incompatible natures (e.g., a chimeric creature). Used as the canonical example Spinoza cites for impossible ideas.

entities.label: NatureIncompatibility
entities.rationale: A quality inhering in a HybridNatureIdea indicating that the natures combined within the idea are mutually incompatible, explaining why instantiation in nature is impossible.

relations.rationale: Hybrid-nature ideas are the exemplary subclass of impossible ideas mentioned in the utterance.
Impossible ideas are still generically dependent continuants — they are conceptual contents that can be entertained, even if they cannot be instantiated in nature.
NatureInstantiability is a disposition (BFO_0000016) borne by ideas with respect to their capacity for natural instantiation.
NatureIncompatibility is a quality (BFO_0000019) inhering in hybrid-nature ideas.

proposal.utterance: Love arises from opinion, clear knowledge, and report.

entities.label: Love
entities.rationale: Love in the Spinozistic/early-modern context is a disposition or affect inhering in a finite thing; it is a kind of mental state with a causal structure, best modeled as a Disposition subclass.

entities.label: Opinion
entities.rationale: Opinion is a type of cognitive content — an informational or representational entity that can be held by multiple minds; best typed as a generically dependent continuant (information content entity).

entities.label: ClearKnowledge
entities.rationale: Clear knowledge is an epistemic content type (analogous to adequate idea or clear and distinct idea in rationalist tradition); typed as a generically dependent continuant representing a kind of information/cognitive content.

entities.label: Report
entities.rationale: Report (hearsay/testimony) is a transmitted informational content entity; typed as a generically dependent continuant.

entities.label: LoveArisingProcess
entities.rationale: The arising of love from epistemic sources is an occurrent — a process by which the disposition of love is realized or constituted from epistemic inputs (opinion, clear knowledge, report).

relations.rationale: Opinion participates in the process by which love arises, as one of its epistemic inputs.
Clear knowledge participates in the love-arising process as a second epistemic source.
Report (testimony) participates in the love-arising process as a third epistemic source.
The love-arising process realizes the disposition of Love in its bearer.

open_questions: What text is this claim drawn from? It does not appear in Spinoza's Ethics in this exact form; it more closely resembles Spinoza's Treatise on the Emendation of the Intellect or the Short Treatise, where three kinds of knowledge (opinion/hearsay, true belief, intuitive knowledge) are discussed. Should 'Opinion' and 'ClearKnowledge' be linked to existing knowledge-kind classes (e.g., working:NecessaryIdea)?

Is 'Love' here an affect (as in Ethics Part III) inhering in a finite singular thing, or is it used in a different sense (e.g., intellectual love of God)? This affects whether it should be a Disposition (internally grounded) or a Role.
Should 'Report' be treated as a subtype of Opinion (both belonging to the first kind of knowledge), or kept distinct as stated in the utterance?
Should we mint a working:EpistemicSource class as a common parent for Opinion, ClearKnowledge, and Report?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts that the affect of Love is causally/genetically dependent on three epistemic sources: opinion, clear knowledge, and report. In BFO terms, Love is modeled as a Disposition class (an internally grounded realizable that inheres in a finite bearer); Opinion, ClearKnowledge, and Report are modeled as generically dependent continuant classes (information/cognitive content types). A process class, LoveArisingProcess, represents the occurrent in which love comes to be realized, with the three epistemic sources as participants. This structure preserves the causal-genetic claim without collapsing the ontological distinction between informational content and mental dispositions. The claim likely derives from Spinoza's Short Treatise or Treatise on the Emendation of the Intellect rather than the Ethics, and should be confirmed against source text.

entities.label: Belief
entities.rationale: Belief is an internally grounded, causally potent state that produces intellectual conviction when realized; this fits BFO Disposition (internally grounded realizable entity) rather than a Quality or Role.

entities.label: StrongProof
entities.rationale: A proof constituted by reasons is an information artifact — a generically dependent continuant (pattern of reasons) that can be instantiated or conveyed; it is the evidential/rational content grounding Belief.

entities.label: IntellectualConviction
entities.rationale: Intellectual conviction is a stable epistemic quality that inheres in a mind/intellect — a measurable property of the bearer's cognitive state, distinct from the disposition that produces it.

entities.label: BeliefFormationProcess
entities.rationale: The production (actualization) of intellectual conviction from a strong proof is an occurrent process — the process in which the Belief disposition is realized.

relations.rationale: Belief is a subclass of BFO Disposition.
StrongProof is a subclass of BFO Generically Dependent Continuant (information/reasons content).
IntellectualConviction is a subclass of BFO Quality.
BeliefFormationProcess is a subclass of BFO Process.
The Belief disposition is realized in a BeliefFormationProcess (BFO: realized in).
BeliefFormationProcess realizes the Belief disposition (BFO: realizes).
Belief, as a disposition producing intellectual conviction, is a subclass of the already-existing IntellectualCertaintyDisposition in the working ontology.

open_questions: In Spinoza's framework (which this ontology appears to track), 'belief' (fides) is a mode of knowledge: should Belief be typed as a subclass of Mode (working:Mode) rather than directly under BFO Disposition, to align with how Modes are already modeled in this ontology?

Should StrongProof be modeled as a subclass of working:NecessaryIdea (already in the ontology) or kept as a distinct GDC class? The definition 'based on reasons' suggests it may overlap with necessary/clear ideas.

Is 'Belief' here intended as a general class or as a specific individual proposition within a philosophical work (e.g., from the Emendation of the Intellect or the Ethics)? This affects individual vs. class treatment.
Should IntellectualConviction be related to the existing working:Thought individual or working:IntellectualCertaintyDisposition class by a subclass or parthood relation?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance 'Belief is a strong proof based on reasons that produces intellectual conviction' introduces three new ontological commitments: (1) Belief as a disposition (internally grounded, causally potent state) in a cognizer; (2) StrongProof as a generically dependent continuant — the reasons-based informational content that grounds Belief; and (3) IntellectualConviction as the Quality produced (inhering in the intellect) when Belief is actualized. A BeliefFormationProcess is also minted as the BFO Process in which Belief is realized, yielding the required conviction. Belief is typed as a subclass of the existing working:IntellectualCertaintyDisposition to reuse existing ontology infrastructure. The open questions flag whether this aligns better with the working:Mode hierarchy (given apparent Spinozistic context) and whether StrongProof should be unified with working:NecessaryIdea.

entities.label: Opinion
entities.rationale: Opinion is a kind of cognitive content or representational state — a pattern that can be instantiated in different bearers — best typed as a generically dependent continuant (information content entity). It is a class, not an individual, because the utterance speaks of opinion in general.

entities.label: Doubtfulness
entities.rationale: Doubtfulness is an epistemic quality that inheres in an opinion — a specific, measurable (in principle) property of that cognitive content. Typed as Quality (BFO_0000019).

entities.label: SubjectToError
entities.rationale: Being subject to error is an internally grounded tendency of opinions — they have the disposition to lead to or contain error. Typed as Disposition (BFO_0000016) rather than Quality because it expresses a potentiality/tendency rather than a currently manifest property.

relations.rationale: Doubtfulness inheres in instances of Opinion; expressing this via a domain axiom on the quality class scoped to Opinion.
The disposition SubjectToError is borne by instances of Opinion, consistent with BFO's inheres-in / bearer-of structure.

Opinion itself is a class of generically dependent continuants (representational/cognitive content). Doubtfulness is typed as a Quality because the statement asserts it as always-present; SubjectToError is typed as a Disposition because it expresses a potentiality/tendency toward error rather than a currently manifest state. No existing individuals or classes in the working ontology capture these commitments, so three new classes are proposed. Relations are expressed as domain constraints pending confirmation of the preferred BFO-idiomatic encoding (RO_0000052 inheres-in at the instance level vs. class-level OWL restrictions).

proposal.utterance: Wonder occurs without formal inference when we tacitly presume the thing accords with custom.

entities.label: Wonder
entities.rationale: Wonder in Spinoza (and Descartes) is a disposition or affect of the mind: a tendency to attend to a thing without causal reasoning. It is internally grounded in the bearer (a mind or finite thing), making Disposition the best BFO fit. It is not a process itself but a realizable state that manifests in episodes of wondering.

entities.label: CustomPresumption
entities.rationale: The tacit presumption that a thing accords with custom is an internally grounded disposition of a cognitive agent: a background readiness to expect conformity with past patterns. It is a disposition that, when absent, triggers wonder.

entities.label: FormalInference
entities.rationale: Formal inference is a process: an occurrent cognitive event in which a conclusion is drawn by explicit reasoning steps. The utterance asserts that wonder occurs without this process.

entities.label: WonderOccurrence
entities.rationale: An episode in which Wonder (as disposition) is realized: the actual occurrent of wondering. The utterance says 'wonder occurs', marking a process class distinct from the disposition.

entities.label: AccordanceWithCustomQuality
entities.rationale: The property of a thing being in accordance with custom is a quality that inheres in the thing (or in the cognitive representation of it). It is the tacitly presumed quality that, when present, suppresses wonder and whose absence (or non-presumption) enables wonder.

relations.rationale: A WonderOccurrence process realizes the Wonder disposition (BFO: realizes).
The Wonder disposition is realized in a WonderOccurrence process (BFO: realized in).
Wonder is a subclass of Disposition.
CustomPresumption is a subclass of Disposition.
FormalInference is a subclass of Process.
WonderOccurrence is a subclass of Process.
AccordanceWithCustomQuality is a subclass of Quality.

Should 'custom' (consuetudo) itself be represented as a generically dependent continuant (a social norm or pattern) with its own IRI, or is AccordanceWithCustomQuality sufficient?

Is Wonder here an affect (affectus) — which in Spinoza's system involves a transition in the body's power of acting — or is it a purely cognitive episode? If the former, it should bear a relation to the body's power, and we may need a BodyPowerTransition or AffectClass.

The utterance implies a negative condition (absence of FormalInference). Should we represent this as a disjointness axiom (WonderOccurrence disjointWith some process that includes FormalInference as a part), or is a note/annotation sufficient?

AccordanceWithCustomQuality captures the property presumed to inhere in the perceived thing. The key structural claim — that WonderOccurrence lacks FormalInference as a part — is noted in open questions as a potential disjointness or negative constraint, which requires user confirmation before axiomatization. entities.rationale: Universal Desire is asserted not to be something really existing in Nature but rather an abstracted concept — a pattern abstracted from particular desires. This fits BFO's Generically Dependent Continuant: it is an informational/conceptual pattern whose existence depends on being abstracted (represented) rather than having independent material or immaterial existence. It is an individual because Spinoza is referring to this specific universal concept.

As conative states inhering in finite particular things, they are specifically dependent continuants (following Spinoza's treatment of desire as an affect or conatus). Modeled as a class since multiple particular desires are implied.

proposal.rationale_summary: Spinoza's claim that 'Universal Desire is not something really in Nature, but is only abstracted from particular desires' makes two distinct ontological assertions: (1) Universal Desire lacks real existence in Nature — it is not a genuine entity among Nature's constituents — and (2) it is derived by an abstraction process from particular desires that do really exist in Nature. Following the pattern already established for Will (WillIsNotRealBeingQuality, WillLacksRealBeingQuality, WillFictumStatusInstance), I model Universal Desire as a GDC individual (an abstract representational pattern in the intellect) bearing two qualities: one capturing its abstractedness from particulars, another capturing its lack of real existence in Nature. Particular desires, by contrast, are real specifically dependent continuants (modes) inhering in finite singular things. The abstraction process is the occurrent by which the intellect moves from particulars to the universal concept. New classes LacksRealNatureExistenceQuality and AbstractionFromParticularsQuality are proposed to carry these predicates, consistent with the BFO Quality type and parallel to existing individuals in the ontology.

entities.label: Man
entities.rationale: Man (humankind, the kind 'human being') is a class of finite singular things — independent continuants that are parts of Nature (WholeOfNature). Modeled as a subclass of FiniteSingularThing since humans are finite, mode-like expressions of Substance in Spinoza's system.

entities.rationale: The claim that Man depends on Nature expresses an internally grounded disposition: a structural, metaphysical incapacity to exist independently of the whole of Nature/Substance. This is a disposition class inhering in instances of Man.

entities.label: GovernanceByNature
entities.rationale: Being governed by Nature is a disposition inhering in Man: the lawful, causal determination of man's states and actions by Nature's necessary order. Models Spinoza's claim that man is subject to Nature's laws.

GovernanceByNature inheres in instances of Man.

Man bears the disposition GovernanceByNature; encodes 'Man is governed by Nature'.

entities.rationale: The soul in Spinoza's framework is an independent continuant (a thinking thing / mode of thought that has its own identity); modeled as a class for the kind, paralleling how Intellect is a class.

entities.label: Body
entities.rationale: The body is a material entity with mass and spatial extent; in Spinoza it is a mode of Extension, but as a class of things it fits BFO material entity.

entities.label: SoulBodyAffectionProcess
entities.rationale: The affecting of the soul by the body is a happening (process) in BFO terms.

entities.label: ObjectOfPerceptionRole
entities.rationale: Being an 'object of perception' is an externally grounded role the body bears in relation to the soul; it is the role under which the body causally affects the soul, per the utterance.

entities.label: BodyAsMaterialBearerRole
entities.rationale: The role of being merely a body (material extended thing) is distinguished from the perceptual-object role; the utterance asserts the soul is NOT affected under this role, making this a necessary contrastive entity.

entities.label: SoulAffectedByBodyQuality
entities.rationale: The being-affected (affection) of the soul is a quality that inheres in the soul as a result of the affection process; models Spinoza's notion of the soul's being modified by perceptual content.

entities.label: PerceptionProcess
entities.rationale: Perception is the process through which the body (as object) affects the soul; a distinct process class capturing the epistemic/causal mechanism.

relations.rationale: Soul-body affection is a process.
The specific affection process is realized through perception; perception is the subkind of affection process asserted here.

Body-as-material-bearer role is a role.

open_questions: Is 'Soul' here Spinoza's idea mentis (the mind/idea of the body as mode of Thought), or a distinct substance? This affects whether Soul should be a subclass of Mode or of Intellect rather than a bare independent continuant.
Should Body here be typed as a subclass of FiniteSingularThing (already in the ontology) rather than a fresh class, given that Spinoza's bodies are finite modes of Extension?

The utterance implies a negative claim (soul is NOT affected insofar as the body is merely a body). Should we assert a disjointness axiom or an explicit negation between BodyAsMaterialBearerRole and the affection relation, or is the contrastive role sufficient?

Is 'perception' here Spinoza's imaginatio (first kind of knowledge) specifically, or generic causal-perceptual affection? This would determine whether PerceptionProcess should be further refined into an ImaginatioProcess subclass.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance makes an ontological claim about the causal/perceptual relation between soul and body: the soul is affected by the body specifically under the role of being an object of perception, not merely as a material extended thing. In BFO terms this requires: (1) Soul and Body as independent continuant classes; (2) a role class ObjectOfPerceptionRole that the body bears, which is the ground of the causal/affective relation; (3) a contrastive role BodyAsMaterialBearerRole under which no such affection occurs; (4) a PerceptionProcess (subclass of Process) in which both soul and body participate, and through which the affection quality inheres in the soul; (5) a SoulAffectedByBodyQuality as the resulting quality inhering in the soul. The key ontological distinction drawn is between two roles the body can bear—perceptual object vs. mere material entity—and the claim that only the former grounds the soul's affection. Open questions concern whether Soul should be more specifically typed as a mode of Thought (Mode subclass) per Spinoza's technical vocabulary already in the ontology.

entities.label: Passion
entities.rationale: In Spinoza's framework, passions (affects of a passive kind) are states that inhere in the soul/mind as a bearer — they are specifically dependent on that bearer, fitting SDC. They are not qualities (measurable properties) but rather affective states that arise and change, so Disposition (BFO_0000016) or a general SDC parent is appropriate. Using BFO_0000020 (SDC) directly as parent since they could be dispositions or qualities; see open_questions.

It parallels BFO independent continuant. Related to but distinct from the existing TrueIntellect individual and Intellect class.

entities.rationale: Spinoza distinguishes kinds of knowledge (imagination/opinion, reason, intuitive knowledge). The 'kind of knowledge' a soul has is a qualitative property of that soul — a quality inhering in it — that determines the character of the passions produced.

entities.label: PassionProduction
entities.rationale: The production of passions according to knowledge type is a process — a happening in time in which a passion comes to be in the soul. This captures the 'are produced' aspect of the assertion.

entities.label: PassionDeterminingDisposition
entities.rationale: The causal-determinative capacity by which a soul's kind of knowledge gives rise to (disposes toward) particular passions. This is internally grounded in the soul qua knower and is realized in PassionProduction processes.

Should 'Passion' be typed as BFO_0000016 (Disposition) rather than BFO_0000020 (SDC generic)? Spinoza's passions are ongoing states, so SDC with Disposition sub-type may be best.

This introduces at minimum four new ontological classes: Soul (an independent continuant, the finite knowing subject), KnowledgeKind (a quality inhering in the soul), Passion (a specifically dependent continuant / mode of the soul), and PassionProduction (the process by which passions are generated). A PassionDeterminingDisposition class bridges the quality of knowledge and the production process, capturing the dispositional-causal claim. Passions are linked to the existing Mode class (BFO_0000020 parent) since in Spinoza passions are finite modes. The relation between KnowledgeKind and PassionDeterminingDisposition is flagged as an open question because conflating a quality with a disposition may be ontologically imprecise. No existing individuals are reused directly, though Soul relates to the existing Intellect class and TrueIntellect individual conceptually.

proposal.utterance: If the soul knows God with clear knowledge, it will be impossible for passions to produce disturbance in it.

entities.label: Soul
entities.rationale: The soul in Spinoza's philosophy (Short Treatise / Ethics) is a mind-like independent continuant — a finite singular thing with cognitive capacities. Modeled as a class since 'soul' is a natural kind here.

entities.label: ClearKnowledgeOfGod
entities.rationale: Clear knowledge of God is a representational / informational content — a species of the clear and distinct idea — that can be possessed by (concretized in) a soul. Best typed as a generically dependent continuant (informational content). Related to the existing NecessaryIdea and ClearAndDistinctIdea lineage.

entities.label: PassionDisturbance
entities.rationale: A disturbance produced in a soul by passions is an occurrent — a happening/process of being disturbed. It is the process of passion acting on the soul. Passions themselves (affects driven by external causes) are already partially captured by DenialOfPassion and Mode lineage; the disturbance they produce is a process.

entities.label: PassionDisturbanceImmunity
entities.rationale: The soul's immunity to disturbance by passions when it possesses clear knowledge of God is an internally grounded disposition — it is a stable capacity/tendency of the soul to resist passion-disturbance, grounded in its cognitive constitution. Disposition is more appropriate than Role because it is constitutively grounded.

entities.label: ClearKnowledgeConditionedImmunity
entities.rationale: The specific propositional claim that possession of clear knowledge of God is a sufficient condition for passion-disturbance immunity is itself an informational content — a thesis belonging to the philosophical work (TheEthics / Short Treatise). Modeled as an individual of the ClearKnowledgeOfGod GDC class, encoding the specific conditional proposition.

relations.rationale: Souls are finite singular things (independent continuants with finitude quality) in Spinoza's system.
Clear knowledge of God is a subspecies of necessary idea — it is the adequate idea of God's eternal essence.
Immunity to passion-disturbance through clear knowledge is a species of intellectual certainty disposition — the soul's constitutive cognitive stability.
PassionDisturbance is a subclass of Process (occurrent happening).
The conditional proposition is an instance of the ClearKnowledgeOfGod GDC class.
This thesis is part of the content of TheEthics (or the Short Treatise) as a philosophical work.

The immunity disposition, when realized, is expressed precisely in the non-occurrence / suppression of PassionDisturbance processes — the disposition is realized (negatively) relative to that process type.

open_questions: Is this utterance drawn from Spinoza's Short Treatise, the Ethics (Part V), or both? The Short Treatise has explicit soul-knowledge-of-God-and-passion claims that differ slightly from Ethics Part V on the intellectual love of God.

Should 'Soul' be identified with 'TrueIntellect' (already in the ontology) or treated as a distinct class? In Spinoza the human mind/soul is a mode of Thought, which may mean Soul should be a subclass of ModeInstance rather than of FiniteSingularThing directly.

Should PassionDisturbanceImmunity be modeled as a disposition that is realized in the absence-of-disturbance, or as a realizable that is realized in a positive process of intellectual stability? proposal.utterance: The power a thing itself gives us is always greater than power from a second thing.

entities.label: SelfDerivedPower
entities.rationale: The power a thing has from itself (its own nature) is a disposition internally grounded in that bearer — fitting BFO Disposition rather than Role (which is externally grounded).

entities.label: ExternallyDerivedPower
entities.rationale: The power a thing has from a second (external) thing is also a disposition, but one whose grounding source is external. Modeled as a sibling class to SelfDerivedPower under Disposition.

entities.label: PowerComparativeQuality
entities.rationale: The comparative magnitude of power (greater vs. lesser) is a quality inhering in the bearer — the relational dimension of power-strength that the proposition is asserting a ranking over.

entities.label: SelfDerivedPowerSuperiorityConstraint
entities.rationale: This individual reifies the specific metaphysical claim that self-derived power always exceeds externally-derived power — it is a standing structural disposition (a constraint on how powers compare) attributed to any self-subsistent thing.

relations.rationale: SelfDerivedPower is a subclass of BFO Disposition — internally grounded capacity of a thing from its own nature.
ExternallyDerivedPower is a subclass of BFO Disposition — a capacity whose source is an external bearer.
The comparative degree of power is a quality inhering in a continuant.
The superiority constraint is an instance of SelfDerivedPower — it is the specific disposition encoding Spinoza's claim that self-grounded power exceeds externally-sourced power.

open_questions: Is this claim intended as Spinoza's general metaphysical principle (Ethics I, Prop. 34 context, or Short Treatise I?) — should the claim be linked to TheEthics or another PhilosophicalWork individual?

Should 'power' here be understood as conatus (the striving to persist in being), or as causal power (efficacy), or both? This affects whether we should relate SelfDerivedPower to CausaSui or SubstanceProductionConstraint already in the ontology.
Should SelfDerivedPowerSuperiorityConstraint be linked to God or Substance as its primary bearer, or left as a class-level constraint on all self-subsistent things?

The utterance uses a comparative ('always greater') — should we model a formal ordering relation between SelfDerivedPower and ExternallyDerivedPower using an object property, or is the PowerComparativeQuality sufficient?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts a general metaphysical principle: that the power a thing derives from itself (its own nature) is always greater than any power it could receive from an external cause. In BFO terms, 'power' is most naturally typed as Disposition (BFO_0000016) — internally grounded capacities. I distinguish two subclasses: SelfDerivedPower (grounded in the bearer's own nature, closely related to existing CausaSui and SubstanceProductionConstraint) and ExternallyDerivedPower (grounded in a second external bearer). The comparative claim ('greater than') is captured as a PowerComparativeQuality (BFO_0000019) that admits of degrees. The specific superiority principle is reified as an individual SelfDerivedPowerSuperiorityConstraint. I flag open questions about the Spinozistic source (Short Treatise vs. Ethics), the intended sense of power (conatus vs. causal efficacy), and the bearer to whom the constraint attaches, since these affect how this principle connects to God, Substance, and CausaSui already in the ontology.

proposal.utterance: All passion must proceed from an external agent, not an internal one.

entities.label: Passion
entities.rationale: A passion in Spinoza's sense is a mode of affect whose cause is external; it inheres in a bearer but is triggered by something outside. Specifically dependent continuant (BFO_0000020) is the most appropriate top-level type, parallel to the existing Mode class.

entities.label: ExternalAgent
entities.rationale: An external agent is a thing that exists and acts from outside the subject bearing the passion; it is an independent continuant distinct from the bearer.

entities.label: ExternalCausationConstraint
entities.rationale: The claim that passion must proceed from an external cause is an internally-grounded normative/structural constraint on passions — it is a disposition-like property specifying that whenever a passion is manifested its causal ground must be external. Disposition (BFO_0000016) captures this internal grounding.

entities.label: PassionCausationProcess
entities.rationale: The proceeding of a passion from an external agent is a causal process — an occurrent unfolding in time. This class represents that type of causal event.

relations.rationale: Passion is a specific kind of Mode in Spinoza's system — a modification of Substance — so Passion is a subclass of the existing Mode class.
Every instance of Passion bears the ExternalCausationConstraint disposition, encoding the definitional requirement that passion proceeds from an external cause.
PassionCausationProcess is a species of DeterminingRelation process — the external agent determines the passion in the subject.
The ExternalCausationConstraint disposition is realized in a PassionCausationProcess — when the disposition manifests, a passion-causing process occurs involving an external agent.

open_questions: Should 'ExternalAgent' be modeled as a role (BFO_0000023) borne by some independent continuant, rather than a class of independent continuants, since 'external' is relational (external to a given subject)?

Is 'passion' here the Spinozistic affect-passion (a mode of the conatus diminished by external causes) or a more general notion of passivity? This affects whether Passion should be a subclass of Mode or a subclass of a forthcoming Affect class.

Should there be an explicit disjointness axiom asserting that PassionCausationProcess cannot have only internal participants (i.e., no self-caused passion), encoding the 'not from an internal agent' clause?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts the Spinozistic (and more broadly Scholastic) principle that passion (passio) is definitionally externally caused — a thing cannot be a passion if its sufficient cause is internal to it. Ontologically this introduces: (1) a class Passion as a species of Mode, (2) a class ExternalAgent for the thing doing the causing, (3) a disposition ExternalCausationConstraint that inheres in every Passion and encodes the external-causation requirement, and (4) a process class PassionCausationProcess for the causal event itself. The constraint is expressed by making Passion a subclass of the bearer of ExternalCausationConstraint, which is realized in PassionCausationProcess. ExternalAgent is tentatively a class of independent continuants, but the open questions flag whether 'external' is better captured as a role, since externality is always relative to a particular subject.

proposal.utterance: Things that are different are distinguished either really or modally.

entities.label: RealDistinction
entities.rationale: A real distinction is a quality or ontological status that holds between two things when they differ in substance or attribute — a specific kind of difference-relation that can inhere in things being compared. Modeled as a Quality subclass because it characterizes the mode of difference between entities.

entities.label: ModalDistinction
entities.rationale: A modal distinction is a quality of difference between a substance/attribute and its mode, or between two modes of the same thing. It is weaker than a real distinction and characterizes how things differ through their modes rather than their essences.

entities.label: Distinction
entities.rationale: Distinction is the superclass quality covering all forms of ontological difference between things. RealDistinction and ModalDistinction are its two species according to the doctrine being modeled.

relations.rationale: Real distinction is a species of Distinction.
Modal distinction is a species of Distinction.

open_questions: In Spinoza's framework (Ethics Part I, especially Def. III and the scholium to E1P4), distinctions between things are either real (between substances with different attributes) or modal (between a mode and its substance, or between modes). Should RealDistinction be further constrained to inhere only in Substance instances, and ModalDistinction only in Mode instances?
Should we also model a 'ConceptualDistinction' (distinctio rationis) as a third subclass, since some interpreters of Spinoza recognize it even if Spinoza collapses it into real or modal distinction?
Is this utterance derived from Descartes (Principles I.60–62) or Spinoza's appropriation of it? The source text will affect which individuals bear these qualities.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts a logical/ontological taxonomy: anything that differs from something else bears a quality of distinction, and that quality is either a RealDistinction or a ModalDistinction. I model Distinction as a new Quality class (BFO_0000019) with two subclasses: RealDistinction and ModalDistinction. These are classes rather than individuals because the claim is generic — it states a rule about kinds of difference, not about one specific pair of things. No existing working classes directly capture this taxonomy, though Mode and Substance (already in the ontology) will serve as the natural bearers of ModalDistinction and RealDistinction respectively. The relations added are simple subClassOf links establishing the taxonomy. Open questions flag whether to constrain the bearer restrictions and whether a third type (conceptual/rational distinction) should be included.

proposal.utterance: Things that have different attributes have nothing in themselves the one from the other.

entities.label: AttributeDifferenceConstraint
entities.rationale: Spinoza's claim (Ethics 1P2) that things with different attributes share nothing in themselves expresses a structural constraint or disposition grounded in the nature of substances: if two things have distinct attributes, they have no common nature. This is best typed as a Disposition (internally grounded incapacity/constraint on bearing shared content).

entities.label: CommonNatureAbsence
entities.rationale: The result of having distinct attributes is the absence of any shared nature between the two substances — a quality of the pair relation: they share no intrinsic content. Modeled as a Quality inhering in (or jointly characterizing) substances with distinct attributes.

relations.rationale: AttributeDifferenceConstraint is a subclass of BFO Disposition, grounded internally in having a particular attribute.
CommonNatureAbsence is a subclass of BFO Quality, representing the quality of lacking any shared nature with a substance bearing a different attribute.

An attribute-difference constraint is a species of the more general SubstanceProductionConstraint already in the ontology, since distinct attributes preclude substances from sharing or producing one another through a common nature.

open_questions: Should 'CommonNatureAbsence' be represented as a relational quality between two substances (a tuple quality), or simply as a quality inhering in each individual substance that bears a specific attribute? BFO does not natively support relational qualities inhering in pairs, so we may need a bridging pattern.

This statement corresponds to Ethics 1P2. Should we mint an individual for that specific proposition (as a generically dependent continuant / NecessaryIdea) and link these classes to it, analogous to how TheEthics is already represented?

Does 'nothing in themselves the one from the other' imply strict mereological disjointness of substances with distinct attributes, or only qualitative/essential distinctness? This affects whether we should assert a disjointness axiom between Substance individuals bearing different AttributeOfSubstance instances.
proposal.rationale_summary: Spinoza's Ethics 1P2 asserts that two substances with different attributes share no common nature. This introduces two ontological commitments: (1) a constraint or disposition grounded in having a particular attribute that blocks sharing of nature with any substance bearing a different attribute (AttributeDifferenceConstraint, typed as BFO Disposition and made a subclass of the existing SubstanceProductionConstraint), and (2) a quality of CommonNatureAbsence that characterizes the relationship between such substances. No individuals are minted because the statement is a universal claim about a kind (substances with different attributes), not about named particulars. The existing classes Substance and AttributeOfSubstance are presupposed but not re-minted. Several open questions remain about relational quality representation and whether to link these to a proposition individual for 1P2.

proposal.utterance: What has nothing in itself from another thing cannot be the cause of that other thing's existence.

entities.label: CausalExclusionPrinciple
entities.rationale: This is a specific philosophical principle (a propositional content / information artifact) asserting that what contains nothing from another thing cannot cause that thing's existence. As a named, citable propositional claim it is best typed as a generically dependent continuant — an information content entity that can be instantiated across carriers.

entities.label: CausalSufficiencyRequirement
entities.rationale: The principle implies that for X to cause Y's existence, X must bear some intrinsic ground — a disposition — that is sufficient for Y. 'CausalSufficiencyRequirement' captures the dispositional ground a cause must have. This is a new class of disposition.

entities.label: CausalIncapacity
entities.rationale: The negative counterpart: what lacks any intrinsic content from X bears a CausalIncapacity with respect to producing X's existence. Modeled as a disposition (an internally grounded incapacity) inhering in a would-be cause.

entities.label: ExistenceProductionProcess
entities.rationale: The process of one thing bringing about (causing) the existence of another. The principle constrains which entities can participate as agents in this process type.

relations.rationale: The principle is an instance of generically dependent continuant (information content entity).
CausalIncapacity is a subclass of Disposition, representing the internally grounded incapacity to cause existence when no intrinsic content from the effect is present in the cause.
CausalSufficiencyRequirement is a subclass of Disposition, representing the required internal ground for genuine causal efficacy over existence.
ExistenceProductionProcess is a subclass of Process.

A CausalIncapacity, if it could be realized, would be realized in an ExistenceProductionProcess — but the principle asserts it cannot be. This relation records the process type the disposition is about, even under negation.

If the latter, should CausalExclusionPrinciple be linked to TheEthics or to working:SubstanceProductionConstraint?
Should 'CausalIncapacity' be modeled as a subclass of the existing working:SubstanceProductionConstraint (a Disposition already in the ontology), or kept distinct?

The phrase 'has nothing in itself from another thing' is the key condition — should we model 'IntrinsicContentAbsence' as a Quality inhering in the would-be cause, to ground the CausalIncapacity disposition formally?

This is a propositional/informational claim (an information content entity, BFO generically dependent continuant) distinct from previously recorded individuals. It commits us to: (1) an individual CausalExclusionPrinciple typed as GDC; (2) a class CausalSufficiencyRequirement (Disposition) for what a genuine cause must bear; (3) a class CausalIncapacity (Disposition) borne by things that lack intrinsic content from a potential effect; and (4) a class ExistenceProductionProcess (Process) as the process type being constrained. relations.rationale: SelfLimitationIncapacity is typed as a subclass of Disposition (BFO_0000016), representing the intrinsic incapacity of a causa sui to limit itself.

Spinoza's claim entails that whatever bears the CausaSui disposition also necessarily bears the SelfLimitationIncapacity disposition — i.e., every instance of CausaSui co-inheres with SelfLimitationIncapacity in the same bearer. Modeling this as a subclass relation captures that every CausaSui is also a SelfLimitationIncapacity (both inhere in the same bearer, and the CausaSui disposition entails the SelfLimitationIncapacity disposition).

I model this as a new disposition class SelfLimitationIncapacity (subclass of BFO_0000016 Disposition) representing the intrinsic incapacity for self-limitation, and I link it to the existing CausaSui class via a subClassOf relation, capturing that every instance of CausaSui co-inheres with SelfLimitationIncapacity in the same bearer. No new individuals are minted; the constraint is expressed at the class level. The subClassOf from CausaSui to SelfLimitationIncapacity is semantically strong and may warrant an open question about whether an OWL existential restriction or property chain is more appropriate — flagged accordingly.

(1) DistinctionGrounding (GDC/BFO_0000031): the principle or content of what does the distinguishing — a generically dependent continuant because it is an informational/propositional ground that can be multiply expressed. entities.rationale: The infinitude of each substance in its kind is a quality inhering in that substance. Spinoza holds that each substance, conceived through its attribute, is infinite in its kind. entities.rationale: Supreme perfection in its kind is a quality inhering in a substance. For Spinoza, perfection tracks existence/reality, and each substance has the maximum perfection possible within its attribute-kind.

entities.label: InfiniteInKindConstraint
entities.rationale: Being infinite in its kind is not merely a static quality but also reflects an internally grounded necessity: a substance cannot be limited by anything of the same nature, which is a Disposition (SelfLimitationIncapacity already captures part of this, but this Disposition captures the positive side — the compulsion to be infinite within its kind). Modeled as a distinct Disposition.

SubstanceInfinity is a quality that qualifies a Substance via its attribute, so it is a subkind of AttributeOfSubstance qualities.
SubstanceSupremePerfection qualifies a Substance in terms of its attribute-kind, so it falls under AttributeOfSubstance.

Being infinite in its kind is grounded in the incapacity for self-limitation; InfiniteInKindConstraint is a more specific Disposition that specializes SelfLimitationIncapacity by positively characterizing the unbounded infinity of a substance within its kind.

entities.label: Idea

proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts a necessary union between an idea and its ideatum (object). A process class is added to model the realisation of that disposition. All new classes are related to the appropriate BFO parents, and the relation between the idea and its object is expressed via participation in the union process.

entities.label: Accident
entities.rationale: In scholastic and early-modern metaphysics, an Accident is an entity that exists in (inheres in) a substance; it cannot exist independently. BFO's specifically dependent continuant (SDC) captures this: SDCs inhere in exactly one bearer and cannot exist without it. This maps cleanly to the Spinozistic/scholastic notion of Accident.

entities.rationale: The claim that Substances and Accidents exist 'in reality or outside the intellect' introduces a quality of extra-mental, formal existence. This is distinct from mere conceptual or fictive being. It is a quality that bearers (Substances or Accidents) can possess.

entities.rationale: The proposition that only Substances and Accidents exist outside the intellect is itself an ontological thesis—a propositional content that can be encoded as a generically dependent continuant (information artifact / propositional content). It can be instantiated in different texts.

relations.rationale: Accidents, as things that inhere in substances and cannot exist independently, are subsumed under BFO specifically dependent continuant.
Spinoza's Modes are the paradigm case of Accidents (modifications of Substance that inhere in Substance); Mode is already typed as BFO_0000020, so it is appropriately a subclass of Accident.

The thesis itself is propositional content, a generically dependent continuant.

Should 'Accident' here be equated with 'Mode' in the Spinozistic sense, or is this utterance tracking a pre-Spinozistic scholastic framework that the ontology should distinguish?

Should 'existing outside the intellect' be modeled as a Quality on individual Substances/Accidents, or as a scope restriction (a closed-world axiom) asserting that the union of Substance and Accident exhausts extra-mental being? The latter would require a disjoint-union axiom or similar OWL construct.
Is 'Accident' intended to be disjoint from 'Substance'? If so, should we add an owl:disjointWith axiom between working:Substance and working:Accident?

Does 'intellect' here refer to any finite intellect, or specifically to God's intellect (infinite intellect)? This affects whether OntologicalExhaustiveness should be linked to TrueIntellect or to a general notion of mind.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts a classic metaphysical exhaustiveness claim: the only kinds of things that have extra-mental (formal) existence are Substances and Accidents. Three new items are proposed. First, an 'Accident' class (subclass of BFO specifically dependent continuant) to capture the scholastic category of entities that inhere in substances—this is the BFO-natural home since SDCs cannot exist independently of their bearers. Second, an 'ExtraIntellectExistence' quality class (subclass of existing FormalExistence) to represent the property of having being outside the mind. Third, 'OntologicalExhaustiveness' as a generically dependent continuant representing the propositional content of the thesis itself. Key relations added: Mode subclasses Accident (Spinoza's Modes are the paradigm Accidents); ExtraIntellectExistence subclasses FormalExistence. Several open questions remain, most importantly whether 'Accident' in this utterance is synonymous with Spinoza's 'Mode' or invokes an older scholastic framework, and whether a disjointness axiom between Substance and Accident should be asserted.

proposal.utterance: Men are generated rather than created, and their bodies existed before in different form.

entities.label: HumanGeneration
entities.rationale: The process by which men/humans come into being through generation (natural causation), as distinct from creation ex nihilo. This is an occurrent, a kind of process.

entities.label: HumanCreation
entities.rationale: The process of creation (ex nihilo or direct divine production) of humans, which Spinoza denies obtains for men. Needed as a contrast class to HumanGeneration.

entities.label: Human
entities.rationale: A human being, a material entity, participant in generation processes. Needed as the subject of the assertion.

entities.label: HumanBody
entities.rationale: The material body of a human being. The assertion claims human bodies pre-existed generation in a different form.

entities.label: PriorMaterialForm
entities.rationale: The quality of having existed in a prior, different material form before undergoing transformation into a human body. Captures the 'different form' aspect of the utterance.

entities.label: MaterialTransformation
entities.rationale: The process by which a material entity changes from one form to another, underlying the claim that bodies existed before in different form.

relations.rationale: HumanGeneration is a kind of process.
HumanCreation is a kind of process.
Humans are material entities.
Human bodies are material entities.
A human body is part of a human.
The process of human generation has humans as participants.
MaterialTransformation is a kind of process.
The material transformation process has the human body as participant (as output).

Human generation is a specific kind of material transformation — bodies existing in prior form are transformed into human bodies.

Should HumanGeneration be modeled as a subclass of FiniteSingularThingModeInstance-producing process, given that humans are finite things (modes) in Spinoza's system?
Should we assert a disjointness axiom between HumanGeneration and HumanCreation (i.e., men are generated, not created), or is that a separate proposition to be added explicitly?
Is 'body' here strictly BFO material entity, or should it be typed under a Mode class (under Extension attribute) consistent with the existing ontology?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts two claims: (1) humans come into being via generation (a natural causal process), not creation ex nihilo; and (2) the matter composing human bodies pre-existed in a different form, implying material continuity through transformation. In BFO terms, generation and creation are both processes (BFO_0000015); humans and their bodies are material entities (BFO_0000040); the prior form is a quality (BFO_0000019) of the pre-existing matter; and the change of form is a material transformation process. I have kept the typing conservative, flagging in open_questions whether these entities should be more tightly integrated with the existing Spinozistic mode/attribute hierarchy already in the ontology (e.g., bodies as modes of Extension). No existing individuals or classes were directly reused, as no existing individual represents humans or bodies as material entities, though several open questions probe whether tighter integration with Mode and FiniteSingularThing is warranted.

proposal.utterance: If one part of matter were annihilated, the whole of Extension would vanish at the same time.

entities.label: ExtensionInseparabilityQuality
entities.rationale: This asserts a quality of Extension: that its parts are not independently annihilable — the whole vanishes if any part does. This is a quality inhering in the individual Extension.

entities.label: MatterPartAnnihilationProcess
entities.rationale: A class of processes in which a part of matter is annihilated. The proposition is a conditional about this type of process.

entities.label: ExtensionAnnihilationProcess
entities.rationale: A class of processes in which the whole of Extension vanishes — the consequent of the conditional asserted.

entities.label: ExtensionNecessaryWholenessDisposition
entities.rationale: Extension bears a disposition whose realization is: whenever any part of matter is annihilated, the whole of Extension is annihilated simultaneously. This captures the metaphysical claim that Extension is necessarily whole — partial annihilation is impossible without total annihilation.

relations.rationale: The inseparability quality inheres in the individual Extension.
The disposition for necessary wholeness inheres in Extension as its bearer.
The disposition is realized in an ExtensionAnnihilationProcess whenever a MatterPartAnnihilationProcess occurs — capturing the conditional dependency.
Typing assertion: ExtensionInseparabilityQuality is a Quality.

open_questions: Should 'matter' here be represented as a class of material entities (BFO_0000040 subclass) or is it equivalent to Extension itself in Spinoza's system (Extension being the attribute of which matter is a mode)?

Should MatterPartAnnihilationProcess be linked to ExtensionAnnihilationProcess via a necessary co-occurrence relation, or would you prefer a formal logical axiom (e.g., OWL axiom) expressing the conditional?

Is 'annihilation' best modeled as a process (BFO_0000015) or as a change-of-quality (loss of FormalExistence quality)? The latter might better integrate with the existing FormalExistence and FormalExistenceNecessitation classes.
proposal.rationale_summary: Spinoza's claim (Ethics I, Prop. XV, Schol.) is that matter, as a mode of Extension, cannot be partially annihilated without the whole attribute of Extension being destroyed — because Extension is indivisible and infinite. This is modeled as: (1) a quality of inseparability inhering in the individual Extension; (2) a disposition of necessary wholeness inhering in Extension, realized in an ExtensionAnnihilationProcess; (3) two process classes — MatterPartAnnihilationProcess and ExtensionAnnihilationProcess — standing in a necessary co-occurrence relation. The existing individual Extension (BFO_0000019) and the existing FormalExistence / FormalExistenceNecessitation classes are leveraged to anchor this. Open questions remain about whether matter should be modeled as a subclass of FiniteSingularThing or as a mode of Extension, and whether the conditional is better captured as an OWL axiom.

entities.label: BodyAtRest
entities.rationale: A body is a material entity (BFO_0000040) that has mass and spatial extent. 'BodyAtRest' is a subclass representing material entities that are currently in a state of rest.

entities.label: StateOfRest
entities.rationale: Being at rest is a measurable/observable quality inhering in a material body at a given time — a specifically dependent continuant of the Quality type.

entities.label: MutualContactRelation
entities.rationale: The relation of two bodies being 'against one another' (in mutual contact) is a quality of their configuration, inhering in the pair of material entities.

entities.label: ResistanceDisposition
entities.rationale: Resistance to change of state is an internally grounded disposition inhering in a body — it can be realized when a force acts on the body. This maps to inertial resistance.

entities.label: PersistenceInStateDisposition
entities.rationale: The disposition of a body (or system of bodies) to continue in its current state unless acted upon by an external force — the ontological correlate of the inertia principle stated in the utterance.

entities.label: Force
entities.rationale: Force in the Spinozistic/physical sense is a disposition or power that, when realized, produces change in the state of a body. Modeled as a disposition whose realization is a process of change-of-state.

entities.label: OvercomingResistanceProcess
entities.rationale: The event of a force overcoming the resistance of a body (or pair of bodies), causing a change in state. This is the realization of the Force disposition that defeats the PersistenceInStateDisposition.

This introduces several new ontological commitments: (1) BodyAtRest as a kind of material entity (BFO_0000040); (2) StateOfRest as a quality (BFO_0000019) inhering in such bodies; (3) MutualContactRelation as a quality of the bodies' configuration; (4) ResistanceDisposition and PersistenceInStateDisposition as dispositions (BFO_0000016) inhering in bodies at rest; (5) Force as a disposition whose realization produces change; and (6) OvercomingResistanceProcess as the process (BFO_0000015) in which a force is realized and resistance is defeated. proposal.utterance: Many attributes that theologians attribute to God are creatures, and vice versa.

entities.label: TheologianAttributionError
entities.rationale: The claim that theologians misattribute creature-properties to God (and vice versa) is best represented as an informational/propositional content class — a type of doctrinal assertion or conceptual content that can be instantiated in various texts or traditions. It is a pattern of attribution that can be replicated across bearers.

entities.label: CreaturePropertyAttributedToGodQuality
entities.rationale: Represents the quality of a theological attribute that actually belongs to a creature but is erroneously predicated of God — a quality type inhering in such attributed properties.

entities.label: GodPropertyAttributedToCreatureQuality
entities.rationale: Represents the quality of a theological attribute that actually belongs to God but is erroneously predicated of a creature — the converse misattribution.

entities.label: TheologicalMisattributionProcess
entities.rationale: The act of theologically attributing a property to the wrong kind of entity (God vs. creature) is a process — a temporal occurrence of predication or doctrinal assertion.

entities.label: Creature
entities.rationale: Spinoza's use of 'creature' (Latin: creatura) refers to finite, produced things — independent continuants that are not God/Substance. This class distinguishes them from God as the unique Substance.

relations.rationale: Creatures in Spinoza's system are finite singular things — modes or finite independent continuants produced by God/Substance.

This quality subclasses DivineAttribute to mark cases where what is actually a creature-quality is being (mis)attributed as a divine attribute — capturing the error class within the divine attribute hierarchy.
The misattribution process realizes (brings to expression) the erroneous quality of treating a creature-property as divine.

proposal.rationale_summary: Spinoza's proposition that 'existence pertains to the essence of Substance' (Ethics I, Prop. 7) asserts a constitutive, non-contingent identity between essence and existence for Substance. In BFO terms this is most naturally a Quality inhering in Substance, because it is a static, intrinsic property (not merely a tendency or capacity). The ontology already has EssentialExistenceQuality as a quality class and SubstanceEssentialExistenceQuality as a subclass, plus the individual God as the unique Substance. I therefore propose a new individual ExistencePertainsToEssenceQuality typed as EssentialExistenceQuality (and thereby as BFO Quality) that inheres in God. This complements the existing disposition individual EssenceContainsExistenceDisposition without duplicating it: the quality states 'existence is part of what Substance is'; the disposition states 'Substance has the power/tendency to exist necessarily'. An open question is whether this assertion should be elevated to a class-level restriction on the Substance class rather than only asserted of the individual God.
