proposal.utterance: Heat is a motion of minute particles of bodies.

entities.label: Heat
entities.rationale: Heat as Spinoza (and later Boyle/Locke tradition) conceives it is a quality of bodies, here defined in terms of its microstructural basis. As a kind of quality, it is a subclass of BFO Quality.

entities.label: MinuteParticle
entities.rationale: Minute particles (corpuscles) of bodies are small material entities; they have mass and spatial extent. They are a subclass of Material entity.

entities.label: MinuteParticleMotion
entities.rationale: The motion of minute particles is an occurrent process unfolding in time. It is the process whose occurrence grounds (realizes) the quality of heat in the body. Spinoza's claim is that heat just is this motion.

entities.label: HeatGroundingRelation
entities.rationale: The claim that heat IS the motion of minute particles can be modeled as a disposition of the body: a body bearing the Heat quality has a disposition that is realized in MinuteParticleMotion. This captures the identity/grounding claim.

relations.rationale: Heat is a kind of Quality (BFO_0000019).
Minute particles are material entities.
Motion of minute particles is a process.
The motion process has the minute particles as participants (RO_0000057 has participant).
The heat-grounding disposition is a subclass of Disposition.
The disposition is realized in the MinuteParticleMotion process, encoding the claim that heat is constituted by such motion.
Heat as a quality is grounded in (associated with) the disposition that is realized in minute-particle motion, encoding the identity claim.

open_questions: Is this utterance from Spinoza's own text (e.g. a letter or the Ethics), or from a source Spinoza is commenting on (e.g. Boyle's corpuscular account)? This affects whether 'Heat' should be an individual quality-instance or a class, and whether it expresses Spinoza's positive view or a view he is critiquing.

Should 'Heat' be modeled as a quality that is numerically identical to the motion process (strict identity), or as a quality that is grounded in / realized by the motion (weaker constitutive relation)?
Should 'MinuteParticle' be linked to the existing working:FiniteSingularThing or working:Mode? Corpuscles in Spinoza's framework are finite modes of Extension.
Is 'Motion' here the same as the existing individual working:Motion or working:MotionAndRest? If so, MinuteParticleMotion could be typed as a subclass or instance under those existing entries.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts a definitional or constitutive claim: heat is (nothing but) the motion of minute particles of bodies. In BFO terms, Heat is best modeled as a Quality class (BFO_0000019) inhering in bodies, while the motion of minute particles is a Process class (BFO_0000015) in which those particles participate. The ontological link between heat and the motion is captured via a Disposition (HeatGroundedInMinuteParticleMotion) that is realized in MinuteParticleMotion, following BFO's realized-in pattern. An alternative strict-identity reading would collapse Heat directly onto MinuteParticleMotion, but BFO maintains a categorical distinction between qualities (continuants) and processes (occurrents), so the disposition-realized-in pattern is the most faithful BFO rendering of the grounding/constitution claim. Several open questions remain, especially about whether this is Spinoza's own view or a report of Boyle's, and whether MinuteParticle should be identified with working:Mode under working:Extension.

proposal.utterance: Corpuscles have determinate figures that must correspond to the pores of bodies they dissolve.

entities.label: Corpuscle
entities.rationale: A corpuscle is a small material body with determinate spatial extent and mass; it is an independent continuant material entity in BFO terms.

entities.label: DeterminateFigure
entities.rationale: The determinate figure (shape) of a corpuscle is a quality inhering in the corpuscle; shape is a paradigmatic BFO quality.

entities.label: Pore
entities.rationale: A pore is an immaterial cavity or channel within a body — a site in BFO terms; it is a three-dimensional spatial region bounded by matter.

entities.label: Body
entities.rationale: The body being dissolved is a material entity that bears pores (sites). Distinct from Corpuscle.

entities.label: PoreShape
entities.rationale: The shape or figure of a pore is a quality inhering in the site (or in the body bearing that site); needed to express the correspondence/fit constraint between corpuscle figure and pore.

entities.label: FigurePoreCorrespondence
entities.rationale: The dispositional property of a corpuscle to fit and pass through a pore of a corresponding shape — an internally-grounded capacity of the corpuscle depending on its own figure. This is a disposition because it grounds the possibility of dissolution.

entities.label: DissolutionProcess
entities.rationale: The dissolution of a body by corpuscles is a process (an occurrent) in which corpuscles participate by passing through the pores of the body.

relations.rationale: DeterminateFigure is a subclass of Quality.
PoreShape is a subclass of Quality.
DeterminateFigure inheres in Corpuscle (a quality inheres in its bearer).
PoreShape (as quality of the pore/body) inheres in Body.
A pore is part of (located within) the body it belongs to.
The disposition to fit pores inheres in the corpuscle.
The figure-pore correspondence disposition is realized in the dissolution process.
The dissolution process has the corpuscle as a participant.
The dissolution process has the body being dissolved as a participant.

open_questions: Is this utterance from a specific text (e.g., Boyle, Descartes, Spinoza's correspondence)? Knowing the source would help decide whether Corpuscle should be linked to existing individuals like Niter or PurifiedNiter already in the ontology.

Should 'FigurePoreCorrespondence' be modeled more specifically as a relational quality between DeterminateFigure and PoreShape (a relative quality), rather than a pure disposition? BFO distinguishes relational from non-relational qualities.

Is 'Pore' better modeled as a BFO_0000029 (Site, an immaterial entity) or should it be treated as a quality/structural feature of Body? The site interpretation is standard for cavities in BFO literature.
Does 'correspond' mean geometric congruence (exact fit) or merely sufficient fit? This may affect whether FigurePoreCorrespondence is a disposition or a quality.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts a corpuscularian mechanism: corpuscles (small material bodies, BFO_0000040) possess determinate figures (shapes, qualities inhering in them, BFO_0000019) that must match the shapes of pores (sites within bodies, BFO_0000029) for dissolution to occur. I introduce: Corpuscle and Body as material entity classes; DeterminateFigure and PoreShape as quality classes inhering in their respective bearers; Pore as a site class part-of Body; FigurePoreCorrespondence as a disposition inhering in the corpuscle that grounds its capacity to pass through matching pores; and DissolutionProcess as the process in which this disposition is realized. The assertion is new ontological content not present in the existing working ontology (which is Spinoza-focused), though the corpuscularian context may relate to the Niter example already present.

proposal.utterance: Some natural phenomena cannot be explained by atomical philosophy principles.

entities.label: NaturalPhenomenon
entities.rationale: Natural phenomena are occurrents — happenings or processes in the world that unfold in time and can be observed. Modeling them as a subclass of BFO Process is the most natural BFO fit.

entities.label: AtomicalPhilosophyPrinciple
entities.rationale: The principles of atomical philosophy are propositional/informational content — patterns of information that can be instantiated in multiple bearers (texts, minds). Generically dependent continuant is the appropriate BFO type for such theoretical content.

entities.label: ExplanatoryInadequacy
entities.rationale: The claim that certain phenomena cannot be explained by atomical principles is best captured as a disposition (or rather its absence/negation) — an incapacity inhering in atomical philosophy principles with respect to certain natural phenomena. Modeled as a disposition class representing explanatory inadequacy.

relations.rationale: ExplanatoryInadequacy is a subclass of Disposition (BFO_0000016), representing the incapacity of atomical principles to explain certain natural phenomena.

open_questions: Is 'atomical philosophy' here referring specifically to Cartesian mechanism/corpuscularianism (as Spinoza critiques), or to ancient Democritean atomism, or both? This affects how AtomicalPhilosophyPrinciple should be further typed or connected to existing ontology content.
Should 'natural phenomena' here be restricted to a particular domain (e.g., phenomena under the attribute of Extension), or is this a fully general claim?

Should 'ExplanatoryInadequacy' inhere in the AtomicalPhilosophyPrinciple (as a disposition of that content), or in the phenomena themselves (as a quality of being unexplained-by-atomism)?

proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts that some natural phenomena lie beyond the explanatory scope of atomical philosophy principles. Three new classes are proposed: NaturalPhenomenon (subclass of BFO Process, since natural phenomena are occurrents that unfold in time), AtomicalPhilosophyPrinciple (subclass of Generically Dependent Continuant, since philosophical principles are informational content), and ExplanatoryInadequacy (subclass of Disposition, capturing the incapacity or limitation of certain explanatory frameworks with respect to certain phenomena). The core ontological claim — that some instances of NaturalPhenomenon cannot be explained by AtomicalPhilosophyPrinciple — is a negative relational claim (an absence of explanatory coverage) best modeled as ExplanatoryInadequacy inhering in AtomicalPhilosophyPrinciple when directed at certain NaturalPhenomenon instances. Several open questions remain about scope, provenance, and precise BFO modeling of the explanatory relation before full commitment should be made.

entities.label: NaturalPhenomenon
entities.rationale: Natural phenomena are occurrents — happenings or processes in the world that unfold in time and can be observed. Modeling them as a subclass of BFO Process is the most natural BFO fit.

entities.label: AtomicalPhilosophyPrinciple
entities.rationale: The principles of atomical philosophy are propositional/informational content — patterns of information that can be instantiated in multiple bearers (texts, minds). Generically dependent continuant is the appropriate BFO type for such theoretical content.

entities.label: ExplanatoryInadequacy
entities.rationale: The claim that certain phenomena cannot be explained by atomical principles is best captured as a disposition (or rather its absence/negation) — an incapacity inhering in atomical philosophy principles with respect to certain natural phenomena. Modeled as a disposition class representing explanatory inadequacy.

relations.rationale: ExplanatoryInadequacy is a subclass of Disposition (BFO_0000016), representing the incapacity of atomical principles to explain certain natural phenomena.

open_questions: Is 'atomical philosophy' here referring specifically to Cartesian mechanism/corpuscularianism (as Spinoza critiques), or to ancient Democritean atomism, or both? This affects how AtomicalPhilosophyPrinciple should be further typed or connected to existing ontology content.

Should 'ExplanatoryInadequacy' inhere in the AtomicalPhilosophyPrinciple (as a disposition of that content), or in the phenomena themselves (as a quality of being unexplained-by-atomism)?

proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts that some natural phenomena lie beyond the explanatory scope of atomical philosophy principles. Relations use BFO's inheres-in (RO_0000052), bearer-of (RO_0000053), realized-in (BFO_0000054), and has-participant (RO_0000057) predicates. entities.label: Body

NOTE: open question raised below about whether Body should be a subclass of FiniteSingularThing or a sibling class under Material entity.

proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance 'Bodies are infinitely divisible' introduces two new ontological commitments: (1) a class Body — the kind of material extended thing in Spinoza's system, typed as a Material entity (BFO_0000040) and plausibly a subclass of the existing FiniteSingularThing; and (2) a class InfiniteDivisibility — the capacity or disposition of bodies to be divided without limit, typed as a BFO Disposition (BFO_0000016) because it is an internally grounded structural potentiality rather than a mere quality. The core claim is expressed as a subClassOf restriction: every Body bears some InfiniteDivisibility disposition (RO_0000053). Open questions concern whether the parent of Body should be FiniteSingularThing or purely BFO_0000040, whether the disposition is epistemic or ontological, and how Body relates to the existing Extension individual.

The existing individual 'Thought' is a quality individual and is left untouched; open questions flag whether the process class should be connected to it or to ThinkingAttribute. The subClassOf pattern is preferred over asserting individual-level identity because the utterance is a general philosophical claim about kinds of operations.

entities.label: Idea
entities.rationale: For Spinoza, ideas are modes of thought — specifically dependent continuants that inhere in a thinking substance. They are not independent things but modifications of the attribute of Thought.

entities.rationale: In Spinozistic context 'Body' is a kind of extended substance — a class of material entities (they have mass and spatial extent). It is a subclass of Substance since Spinoza's bodies are modes of the one substance under the attribute of Extension, but the utterance frames body as 'a substance capable of existing without mind', so it is typed as a subclass of Substance here.

entities.label: ExtendedSubstanceQuality
entities.rationale: The predicate 'extended' in 'extended substance' is a quality (specifically the instantiation of the Attribute Extension) that inheres in Body. It is a subclass of Attribute since Extension is one of God's infinite attributes; here it marks the quality of being spatially extended.

entities.label: MindIndependentExistenceCapacity
entities.rationale: The claim that body is 'capable of existing without mind' is an intrinsically-grounded capacity — a disposition of bodies to exist independently of any mental substance. Dispositions are internally grounded in their bearers, which fits BFO Disposition.

relations.rationale: Body is asserted to be a substance, so Body is a subclass of the existing Substance class.
Being extended is an instantiation of the Attribute of Extension; it is a subclass of Attribute.

Every Body, as an extended substance, bears the quality of extension — captured by making Body a subclass (via a restrictions axiom) of bearers of ExtendedSubstanceQuality. Modeled here as a subclass link pending a full restriction.
MindIndependentExistenceCapacity is a Disposition.

The utterance asserts bodies are capable of existing without mind — every body bears this disposition, so Body is a subclass of bearers of MindIndependentExistenceCapacity (approximated as subclass pending OWL restriction).

open_questions: In Spinoza's mature system (Ethics Part II) body is technically a mode of God under the attribute of Extension, not itself an independent substance — should Body be typed as a subclass of Mode rather than Substance, or do you intend the Cartesian reading where body is an independent extended substance?

Should ExtendedSubstanceQuality simply be the existing individual 'Extension' (already in the ontology) cast as a quality class, or is a new class preferred to distinguish the attribute-type from the quality-instance?

Should 'without mind' be glossed as independence from the existing individual 'ThinkingAttribute' / 'Thought', and should a formal disjointness axiom be added between Body and any mental substance class?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance makes three ontological commitments: (1) there is a kind of entity called Body; (2) it is an extended substance — it bears the attribute of Extension; (3) it has the capacity to exist without mind, i.e., independently of any thinking/mental substance. Body is minted as a new class, subclass of the existing Substance class (BFO independent continuant), reflecting the assertion that body is a substance. Its being 'extended' is captured by a new quality class ExtendedSubstanceQuality (subclass of Attribute) that inheres in bodies. The independence-from-mind claim is an internally grounded capacity, so it is modeled as a new Disposition class MindIndependentExistenceCapacity. The existing individual 'Extension' is related but is an individual quality-instance in the ontology; the new class is a type-level counterpart. Open questions flag the tension between the Cartesian reading (body as independent substance) and the Spinozistic reading (body as mode) and whether a disjointness axiom is warranted.

entities.label: PreservationByGodDisposition
entities.rationale: The claim that whatever exists is preserved by God's power names an internally-grounded capacity (power) of God that is realized in the continued existence of all things. A Disposition is the right BFO type for a power that is internally grounded in its bearer (God) and tends toward a specific realization (preservation/continued existence).

entities.label: PreservationByGodDispositionInstance
entities.rationale: This is the specific instance of God's preserving power inhering in God as an individual bearer.

entities.label: PreservationOfExistentsProcess
entities.rationale: The preservation of all existing things is an ongoing process — a happening in time realized by God's power. Spinoza's claim is that this process is universal and continuous.

entities.label: GodSolePowerPreservationQuality
entities.rationale: The exclusivity (alone/sole) of God's preserving power is a quality inhering in God — it characterizes the uniqueness of God as the sole sufficient cause of the continued existence of all things, paralleling GodNecessaryExistenceQuality and UniquenessInNatureQuality already in the ontology.

relations.rationale: The disposition to preserve all things inheres in God as its unique bearer.
God is the bearer of this preserving disposition (inverse of inheres-in).
The disposition is realized in the process of preservation of all existing things.
The process of preservation realizes God's preserving disposition.
The quality of being the sole preserver inheres in God.
God bears the quality of being the sole power that preserves all existents.
God participates in (as the sole causal agent of) the preservation process.

Should PreservationByGodDisposition be typed as a subclass of an existing class such as CausalReasonForExistence, since God's preserving power is a species of causal power?
Is this claim intended as equivalent to God being causa sui of all continued existence, meaning EssenceContainsExistenceDisposition should be reused or extended here?
proposal.rationale_summary: Spinoza's proposition that whatever exists is preserved by God's power alone introduces three new ontological commitments: (1) a disposition class (PreservationByGodDisposition) inhering in God that grounds the ongoing preservation of all things, modeled as a BFO Disposition because it is internally grounded in God and points toward a realization; (2) an individual instance of that disposition inhering in God (PreservationByGodDispositionInstance); (3) the process of preservation itself (PreservationOfExistentsProcess), a BFO Process realized by the disposition; and (4) a quality (GodSolePowerPreservationQuality) marking the exclusivity — 'alone' — of God's role as preserver. Relations connect the disposition to God via inheres-in/bearer-of, the disposition to the process via realized-in/realizes, and God to the process via participates-in. Existing individuals GodCausesAllThings and GodImmanentCauseRole are related in spirit but capture distinct propositions (causation vs. preservation, immanence vs. exclusive power), so new entities are minted. Open questions flag whether the universal quantifier ('whatever exists') should be expressed by linking all known individuals to the preservation process, and whether this disposition is a sub-type of CausalReasonForExistence.

entities.label: Assenting
entities.rationale: Assenting is a kind of mental happening or act — it unfolds in time and is thus a Process (BFO_0000015). Spinoza discusses assent (including to confused ideas) as an act of the mind, not a static property.

entities.label: Action
entities.rationale: Action in Spinoza's sense is something the mind does actively — a process. It is a superclass capturing the Spinozistic notion of active causation realized in time.

entities.label: AssentingToConfusedThings
entities.rationale: Assenting to confused (inadequate) things is a subtype of Assenting — it is the specific process of affirming confused ideas. The utterance singles this out as still counting as an action.

relations.rationale: The utterance asserts that assenting is a kind of action; modeled as Assenting being a subclass of Action.
Assenting to confused things is a specific subtype of assenting in general.
By transitivity (and explicitly stated in the utterance), assenting to confused things is also a kind of action.

Should 'Action' here be the broad sense (any mental act) or the strict Spinozistic sense (adequate/active causation)? If the latter, a separate 'Passion' class may also be needed.
Should 'ConfusedIdea' be modeled as a class (BFO_0000031, generically dependent continuant) to serve as the object of AssentingToConfusedThings, and linked via a participant relation?
Is this utterance from a specific proposition in the Ethics (e.g., Part II) that should be cited as provenance on these classes?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance makes a general claim that assenting — even to confused or inadequate content — is a kind of action. In BFO terms, both assenting and action are processes (BFO_0000015) because they are occurrents that unfold in time. I mint three classes: Action (a general process class for Spinozistic active mental/causal events), Assenting (a process subclass capturing the mental act of affirming), and AssentingToConfusedThings (a further subclass for affirmation of confused ideas). The core ontological commitment is the subClassOf relation Assenting ⊑ Action, and by extension AssentingToConfusedThings ⊑ Action. The main open question is whether Spinoza's technical sense of 'action' (requiring adequate causation) is intended, which could create tension since confused ideas are typically linked to inadequate causation and passivity.

entities.label: Error
entities.rationale: In Spinoza's Ethics, 'error' is not a positive entity but a privation — an absence or lack of the best use of freedom. Modeled as a disposition-class (specifically a privative disposition), it captures the tendency or state of falling short of adequate cognition or freedom. It inheres in minds/modes of thought.

entities.label: Privation
entities.rationale: Privation is a quality of absence or deficiency inhering in a bearer. Spinoza defines error as a privation, so Privation is the genus under which Error is characterized. A quality-class fits because privation is a measurable, attributable lack in a continuant.

entities.label: ErrorAsPrivationQuality
entities.rationale: The specific quality instance-type that constitutes error as a privation of the best freedom, inhering in human minds (modes of thought). Subclass of Privation, capturing the Spinozistic doctrine.

entities.label: BestFreedom
entities.rationale: The 'best freedom' in Spinoza refers to the capacity to act from adequate ideas, free from external compulsion — an internally-grounded disposition of a human mind. Disposition fits because it is a genuine capacity that may or may not be realized.

entities.label: HumanMind
entities.rationale: The human mind (mens humana) is the bearer of both the capacity for best freedom and the privation that constitutes error. As a mode of thought individuated as an idea of the human body, it functions as an independent continuant within the Spinozistic system.

relations.rationale: Error is typed as a disposition whose character is constituted by the quality of privation; linking the disposition class to the quality class captures the Spinozistic claim that error is privative.
ErrorAsPrivationQuality is a species of Privation.
The privation that constitutes error inheres in the human mind as its bearer, per Spinoza's doctrine that error belongs to human cognition.
The disposition of best freedom inheres in the human mind; error is its privation, so both share the same bearer class.
The human mind is a mode (of Thought/the thinking attribute) in Spinoza's system, so HumanMind is a subclass of the existing Mode class.

open_questions: Should 'Error' be modeled primarily as a Quality (the privation-quality itself) rather than a Disposition, given that Spinoza treats it as a deficiency inhering in the mind rather than a capacity?

Is 'BestFreedom' (optima libertas) here freedom of the will (free from external causes) or specifically the freedom that comes from adequate ideas? This affects whether BestFreedom should subclass an existing SelfConceivability or ConceptualIndependence class.
Should HumanMind be an individual (like God, WholeOfNature) or remain a class, given that Spinoza treats individual human minds as modes but speaks generically of 'man' here?

All three inhere in HumanMind, which is a subclass of the existing Mode class (minds being modes of the Thinking Attribute). Error is doubly typed: as a disposition-class capturing the tendency to fall into privation, and as co-characterized by ErrorAsPrivationQuality (a quality-subclass of Privation). The existing ImperfectionQuality individual is related in spirit but represents a distinct claim; a possible rdfs:subClassOf or equivalence could be explored in open questions. entities.label: DistinctionOfReason
entities.rationale: A distinction of reason (distinctio rationis) is a conceptual, not real, difference between two aspects of a thing. It is a quality of the relationship between the items distinguished — they share the same formal reality. Modeled as a Quality class.

Spinoza seems to treat intellect and will as modes of Thought rather than as attributes of God in the strict sense — clarification of the Spinoza passage would affect the typing.

This is distinct from the existing EssentialExistenceQuality (which concerns existence itself) and captures property-essentiality as a quality of the relation between a thing and one of its properties.

entities.label: NonEssentialPropertyQuality
entities.rationale: A quality that a bearer has when a given property can be removed while the bearer continues to exist (i.e., persists without that property). This is the complement of EssentialPropertyQuality.

entities.label: PropertyRemovalProcess
entities.rationale: The process (actual or counterfactual) of removing a property from a bearer. The criterion for non-essentiality is grounded in whether the bearer persists through such a process.

entities.label: PersistenceAfterPropertyRemovalDisposition
entities.rationale: A disposition of a bearer to continue existing after a specific property is removed. When this disposition is realized, it evidences that the removed property is non-essential. This is internally grounded in the bearer's nature.

relations.rationale: Non-essentiality of a property is a species of the broader class EssenceDoesNotInvolveExistence (the essence of the thing does not involve having that property), already in the ontology.
Essential property quality is a subtype of EssentialExistenceQuality: a property is essential when it is bound up with the thing's continued formal existence.
The disposition to persist after property removal is realized in a PropertyRemovalProcess (the process of removing the property).
The criterion is an information/conceptual content pattern — a generically dependent continuant.

entities.label: SpatialInvarianceQuality
entities.rationale: The claim that one space or extension cannot be larger at one time than at another expresses a quality of spatial extension: its magnitude does not vary over time. This is a Quality (BFO_0000019) inhering in extended entities, capturing temporal invariance of spatial magnitude.

Modeled as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) because it is an intrinsic, internally grounded feature.

relations.rationale: SpatialInvarianceQuality is a subclass of Quality.
TemporalInvarianceOfExtension is a subclass of Disposition.

The disposition of temporal invariance of extension is grounded in and co-expressed with the quality of spatial invariance; modeling the disposition as a specialization makes the two complementary aspects cohere.

Should SpatialInvarianceQuality be typed as a subclass of the existing 'AttributeOfSubstance' or 'DivineAttribute' classes rather than bare BFO_0000019?

proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts that a single space or extension cannot differ in size across time—i.e., extension is temporally invariant in its magnitude. Ontologically this commits to: (1) a Quality (SpatialInvarianceQuality) that inheres in extended entities and records that their spatial magnitude does not change over time, and (2) a Disposition (TemporalInvarianceOfExtension) that is internally grounded in the bearer and disposes it never to increase or decrease in size. The existing individual 'Extension' is the natural bearer, and these classes could be linked to existing classes like 'AttributeOfSubstance' or 'InfiniteInItsKind', but those linkages are left as open questions pending user confirmation of the Spinozistic context (whether this is about infinite Extension as Attribute or finite extended modes).

entities.rationale: The occurrent act of conceiving a limit or boundary of some extension; the process that realizes ExtensionBoundaryConceivability.

entities.rationale: The occurrent act of conceiving spaces beyond any conceived boundary; necessarily co-occurs with ExtensionBoundaryConceptionProcess per Spinoza's claim.

entities.label: ExtensionUnboundednessQuality

entities.label: ContinuousDetermination

entities.rationale: The specific ongoing determination process described in the proposition.

I have reused existing BFO process and disposition types, minted new classes and representative individuals for each component, and linked them via standard BFO participation and realization relations. The open questions flag the most important ontological ambiguities, especially the bearer of the external force and the relationship to existing Motion/MotionAndRest individuals already in the graph.

Key open questions concern whether FluidBody should be a subclass of Mode (consistent with Spinoza's view that bodies are modes of Extension), whether the part-whole relation should be expressed via OWL property restrictions rather than subClassOf, and the correct BFO typing of force as quality versus disposition. entities.label: Body
entities.rationale: A body (corpus) in Spinoza's physics is a material entity with mass and spatial extent; it is already partially represented by PartOfExtendedSubstance individual but here we need a class for bodies in general as bearers of rest.

entities.label: Rest
entities.rationale: Rest (quies) in Spinoza is a state inhering in a body, a specifically dependent continuant; it is the counterpart of Motion already in the ontology as individual MotionAndRest. Rest as a class (a quality/disposition) best fits SDC since it inheres in a body.

entities.label: BodyResistanceDisposition
entities.rationale: The capacity of a body to resist other bodies is a disposition inhering in the body; it is internally grounded in the body's rest-state.

entities.label: BodyResistanceProcess
entities.rationale: The actual resisting of one body by another is an occurrent process in which bodies participate.

Resistance capacity is a disposition.
The disposition to resist is realized in a process of resistance.
Bodies are material entities.

BFO does not natively express 'grounded in' between two SDC classes except via subclassing.

proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts a Spinozistic physical principle: bodies resist other bodies solely by virtue of their rest (quies), not by any positive active power. entities.label: Chimaera
entities.rationale: A chimaera in Spinoza's sense is a fictitious or impossible object—something that cannot exist in nature. It lacks the capacity for formal existence. It is best typed as a generically dependent continuant (an informational/conceptual pattern, a fiction or idea-content) rather than an independent continuant, since it cannot have formal existence. It exists only as a conceived content, not as a real being.

entities.label: ExistenceByOwnNature
entities.rationale: Existence by own nature is the disposition of a being whose essence involves its own existence—the capacity to exist through itself. Spinoza contrasts chimaeras with beings that have this disposition. It is a subclass of CausaSui (already in the ontology as a disposition), since causa sui is precisely the disposition to exist by one's own nature.

entities.label: LackOfExistenceByOwnNature
entities.rationale: The incapacity to exist by one's own nature is a quality that characterises chimaeras: their nature does not include existence. This is the ground for denying them the status of 'being'. It is modelled as a quality (a specifically dependent continuant), as it characterises the modal/essential status of chimaeras. It is a subclass of ContingentExistenceQuality (already in ontology).

entities.label: Being
entities.rationale: In Spinoza's usage, 'being' (ens) denotes something that has formal existence—something that can exist by virtue of its nature or by the power of God. It is most naturally typed as an independent continuant, since beings have formal existence in nature. Chimaeras are explicitly excluded from this class.

relations.rationale: Existence by own nature is a species of causa sui: a being whose essence involves its own existence has the disposition to be causa sui.
Beings (entia) in the formal sense have independent existence in nature, hence are independent continuants.
Chimaeras are impossible fictions—generically dependent conceptual contents that cannot have formal existence; they are not independent continuants.
Lacking existence by own nature is a species of contingent existence quality: such things cannot necessitate their own existence.

proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance defines imaging (imaginatio) in Spinoza's sense as awareness arising from traces left in the brain by the motion of animal spirits, which are themselves caused by external objects. Ontologically, this invokes: (1) Imaging as a disposition or cognitive capacity (BFO Disposition) realized in a process of spirit motion; (2) TraceInBrain as a quality inhering in the brain as material entity; (3) SpiritualMotion as the process whose participants include the brain and the external objects arousing it; (4) ImagingAwareness as the resultant quality of the cognitive mode. Two new classes are minted: ModeOfThinking (subclass of Mode/SDC) and IdeaOfThing (a specific subclass of ModeOfThinking representing representational/intentional modes). The key ontological assertion is that BeingOfExistence inheres in ThingsOutsideGod and is not self-grounding (contrasting with CausaSui and SubstanceEssentialExistenceQuality which are already modelled). Several open questions remain about whether BeingOfExistence is better a Quality than a Disposition, and about the perspectival distinction 'considered in itself' vs. 'as in God's intellect'.

proposal.utterance: Time is not an affection of things, but only a mode of thinking or being of reason.

entities.label: Time
entities.rationale: Spinoza's claim is that Time is not a real affection (quality or property) of things but a being of reason — a conceptual or mental construct. BFO_0000031 (Generically dependent continuant) best captures 'being of reason' as an information-bearing or representational entity that depends on minds/thinkers for its existence and can be copied/instantiated. It is not a temporal region in BFO's sense here because Spinoza explicitly denies it is a real feature of things.

entities.label: ModeOfThinking
entities.rationale: A 'mode of thinking' (modus cogitandi) in Spinoza is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in a thinking being and is realized in cognitive processes. entities.label: BeingOfReason
entities.rationale: Ens rationis (being of reason) is a Spinozist technical term for a concept or mental construct that has no formal existence outside the intellect. BFO_0000031 is the best fit: it is an information-content entity / abstract pattern that depends generically on minds for its existence, and unlike real affections it does not inhere in particular things.

proposal.rationale_summary: Spinoza's claim (Letter 12 / Ethics II) is that Time is not a real affection (quality) of things — it does not inhere in substances or their modes as an objective property — but is instead a 'mode of thinking' or 'being of reason' (ens rationis): a mental auxiliary used to explain duration in finite, comparable segments. The ontological work is thus: (1) we mint 'Time' as an individual of type BeingOfReason and ModeOfThinking; (2) BeingOfReason is a new class under BFO_0000031 (generically dependent continuant), capturing that it is a representational construct dependent on intellect; (3) ModeOfThinking is a new class under the existing Mode class, restricted to the Thought attribute; (4) a negative status quality TimeIsNotAffectionOfThingsQuality is introduced, paralleling WillIsNotRealBeingQuality, to make the denial explicit. The relation of Time to ThinkingAttribute is captured via BFO_0000050 (part of). This deliberately departs from BFO's own BFO_0000008 (Temporal region), which is a realist category Spinoza would reject for Time — an open question flags this tension.

proposal.utterance: Time is not an affection of things, but only a mode of thinking or being of reason.

entities.label: Time
entities.rationale: Spinoza's claim is that Time is not a real affection (quality or property) of things but a being of reason — a conceptual or mental construct. BFO_0000031 (Generically dependent continuant) best captures 'being of reason' as an information-bearing or representational entity that depends on minds/thinkers for its existence and can be copied/instantiated. It is not a temporal region in BFO's sense here because Spinoza explicitly denies it is a real feature of things.

entities.label: ModeOfThinking
entities.rationale: A 'mode of thinking' (modus cogitandi) in Spinoza is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in a thinking being and is realized in cognitive processes. Disposition (BFO_0000016) captures the internally grounded character of such a mode. It is a subclass of Mode (already in ontology) restricted to the attribute of Thought.

entities.label: BeingOfReason
entities.rationale: Ens rationis (being of reason) is a Spinozist technical term for a concept or mental construct that has no formal existence outside the intellect. BFO_0000031 is the best fit: it is an information-content entity / abstract pattern that depends generically on minds for its existence, and unlike real affections it does not inhere in particular things.

entities.label: TimeIsNotAffectionOfThingsQuality
entities.rationale: The denial that Time is an affection (real quality) of things is itself a quality-claim about Time's ontological status — specifically a negative ontological status quality analogous to existing individuals like WillIsNotRealBeingQuality.

relations.rationale: Spinoza asserts Time is a being of reason (ens rationis), not a real affection of things.
Spinoza explicitly classifies Time as a mode of thinking (modus cogitandi).
ModeOfThinking is a subclass of Mode (already in ontology), restricted to the attribute of Thought.
BeingOfReason is a subclass of generically dependent continuant, as it is a representational/conceptual construct dependent on minds.
This negative ontological-status quality inheres in Time as its bearer.
Time as a mode of thinking is part of (falls under) the attribute of Thought in Spinoza's system.

open_questions: Spinoza contrasts Time with Eternity and Duration elsewhere. Should we also assert a disjointness axiom between Time (as BeingOfReason) and Duration, or treat Duration as a separate individual/class at this point?

BFO already has BFO_0000008 (Temporal region) as a real ontological category. Should we explicitly assert that working:Time is disjoint from BFO_0000008 to flag the Spinozist departure from realist temporal ontology?

Should ModeOfThinking be typed as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) or as a Role (BFO_0000023)? In Spinoza, modes of thinking seem more internally grounded (disposition-like), but the user may prefer a different mapping.
proposal.rationale_summary: Spinoza's claim (Letter 12 / Ethics II) is that Time is not a real affection (quality) of things — it does not inhere in substances or their modes as an objective property — but is instead a 'mode of thinking' or 'being of reason' (ens rationis): a mental auxiliary used to explain duration in finite, comparable segments. The ontological work is thus: (1) we mint 'Time' as an individual of type BeingOfReason and ModeOfThinking; (2) BeingOfReason is a new class under BFO_0000031 (generically dependent continuant), capturing that it is a representational construct dependent on intellect; (3) ModeOfThinking is a new class under the existing Mode class, restricted to the Thought attribute; (4) a negative status quality TimeIsNotAffectionOfThingsQuality is introduced, paralleling WillIsNotRealBeingQuality, to make the denial explicit. The relation of Time to ThinkingAttribute is captured via BFO_0000050 (part of). This deliberately departs from BFO's own BFO_0000008 (Temporal region), which is a realist category Spinoza would reject for Time — an open question flags this tension.

proposal.utterance: An idea is true when it shows a thing as it is in itself, and false when it shows it otherwise than it really is.

entities.label: Idea
entities.rationale: An idea in Spinoza's sense is a representational content — an information-bearing pattern that can be instantiated in a mind, best typed as a generically dependent continuant (like a proposition or informational content).

entities.label: TrueIdea
entities.rationale: A true idea is a subtype of Idea that accurately represents a thing as it is in itself — a subclass of Idea (GDC) with an additional truth-quality.

entities.label: FalseIdea
entities.rationale: A false idea is a subtype of Idea that represents a thing otherwise than it really is — a subclass of Idea (GDC) with a falsity-quality.

entities.label: TruthQuality
entities.rationale: The property of an idea's accurately showing a thing as it is in itself is a quality (a specifically dependent continuant inhering in the idea). Truth is a measurable/assessable property of representational content.

entities.label: FalsityQuality
entities.rationale: The property of an idea's showing a thing otherwise than it really is — falsity — is likewise a quality inhering in the idea.

entities.label: AdequateRepresentationQuality
entities.rationale: Spinoza's criterion for truth is that the idea shows a thing 'as it is in itself' — this correspondence or adequacy is a sub-quality of TruthQuality specifying the intrinsic representational fidelity.

relations.rationale: A true idea is a kind of idea.
A false idea is a kind of idea.
TruthQuality is a BFO Quality.
FalsityQuality is a BFO Quality.
Adequate representation (showing the thing as it is in itself) is the specific character of TruthQuality per Spinoza's definition.

Every true idea, by definition, bears an AdequateRepresentationQuality. Modeled as subclass constraint (every true idea has this quality inhering in it); a more precise axiom would use an existential restriction: TrueIdea subClassOf (bearerOf some AdequateRepresentationQuality). Flagged in open_questions.
Every false idea bears a FalsityQuality. Same caveat as above — see open_questions.

Should these instead be OWL existential restrictions (TrueIdea subClassOf bearerOf some AdequateRepresentationQuality) using RO_0000053? Please confirm preferred axiom form.

proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance gives Spinoza's definition of truth and falsity for ideas (Ethics I or II). An 'Idea' is best typed as a generically dependent continuant (BFO_0000031) because it is representational/informational content that can be borne by minds. Truth and falsity are qualities (BFO_0000019) that inhere in ideas — specifically, TruthQuality captures the adequacy of representation ('as it is in itself') and FalsityQuality captures misrepresentation. TrueIdea and FalseIdea are subclasses of Idea distinguished by which quality they bear. AdequateRepresentationQuality is introduced as the specific positive criterion Spinoza invokes. proposal.utterance: There is no absolute evil.

entities.label: AbsoluteEvil
entities.rationale: Absolute evil, in Spinoza's framework, would be a quality (or purported quality) of a being. Typing it as a Quality class allows the assertion of its non-instantiation (i.e., nothing bears this quality). It parallels existing quality classes like ImperfectionQuality already in the ontology.

entities.label: AbsoluteEvilNonExistenceQuality
entities.rationale: The claim 'there is no absolute evil' is ontologically the assertion that the quality AbsoluteEvil has no instances — equivalently, that being absolutely evil is not a real quality anything can bear. This class reifies that meta-level claim as a quality of the system (Spinoza's metaphysics), parallel to ImperfectionQuality and NecessityOfExistence in the ontology.

relations.rationale: AbsoluteEvil is typed as a subclass of Quality (BFO_0000019), representing a putative quality that would inhere in a bearer.

The non-existence of absolute evil is related to Spinoza's denial of absolute imperfection; subclassing under ImperfectionQuality (already in the ontology) captures this conceptual relationship — absolute evil would be the maximal imperfection, which Spinoza denies exists.

open_questions: Should AbsoluteEvil be declared an empty class (owl:Nothing equivalent or unsatisfiable) to formally encode that nothing can instantiate it, rather than merely leaving it without instances?
Is this claim meant in Spinoza's sense that evil is merely privation/relative (i.e., evil is not a positive quality at all, but only the absence of something relative to a finite thing's nature)?
Should we also represent 'relative evil' or 'evil as privation' as a contrasting concept to complete the assertion?
Is 'absolute evil' here a quality of a thing, or a disposition/role — e.g., should it be modeled as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) rather than a Quality?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance 'There is no absolute evil' is a negative existential claim in Spinoza's Ethics: no entity instantiates the quality of being absolutely evil. To represent this, I mint a class AbsoluteEvil as a subclass of BFO Quality, and AbsoluteEvilNonExistenceQuality (subclass of the existing ImperfectionQuality) to capture the meta-claim that absolute evil is not a real quality of any being. The core ontological commitment is that AbsoluteEvil is an empty class — nothing in the ontology is a bearer of it. I flag open questions about whether to formally enforce emptiness via OWL (owl:equivalentClass owl:Nothing) and whether evil is better modeled as privation (a disposition or absence) rather than a positive quality. No individuals are added since the statement is a universal denial rather than an assertion about a specific named entity.

proposal.utterance: The thing itself and its striving to preserve its being are not really distinct, only distinguished by reason.

entities.label: Conatus
entities.rationale: Spinoza's conatus—the striving of a thing to preserve its being—is a disposition inhering in the thing, internally grounded in the thing's nature. It is an individual instance (specific to the entity bearing it) rather than a class, since the utterance speaks of the striving of a thing and its identity with that thing.

entities.label: RationalDistinction
entities.rationale: A distinction of reason (distinctio rationis) is a conceptual/logical distinction that exists only in how we conceive things, not in reality. It is best modeled as a generically dependent continuant—an informational/representational pattern that can be instantiated in minds—rather than a quality or disposition of the thing itself.

entities.label: RealDistinction
entities.rationale: A real distinction between two things is an objective difference in their being or qualities. Modeling it as a Quality class (or its absence) allows us to assert that Conatus and the thing lack this quality between them. Note: working:SoulBodyRealDistinction already exists as a quality individual; this class generalises that.

entities.label: CogatusRationalDistinction
entities.rationale: This is the specific rational (reason-based) distinction between the thing and its conatus, as asserted in the utterance—a conceptual distinction only, not a real one.

The conatus inheres in the thing (here represented by AnotherBeing as a stand-in for 'the thing itself'). Open to reassigning bearer once a more specific individual is identified.
The specific distinction between a thing and its conatus is an instance of RationalDistinction.
RationalDistinction is a class of generically dependent continuant (conceptual pattern).
RealDistinction is a quality class; its absence can be asserted of the conatus–thing pair.

open_questions: Should 'the thing itself' be modeled as a generic Substance individual, or should we use an existing individual like AnotherBeing or God as the bearer of Conatus? The utterance is general (any thing), so a class-level axiom may be more appropriate than an individual.
Should Conatus be a class rather than an individual, since Spinoza applies it universally to all things? If so, Conatus would be a subclass of BFO_0000016 (Disposition) bearing a universal scope.

How should we formally encode 'not really distinct, only distinguished by reason'? Option (b) is ontologically strong and may cause reasoning issues.

I model Conatus as a new Disposition individual (BFO_0000016) because it is internally grounded in the nature of the bearer. The distinction itself is bifurcated into two new classes: RationalDistinction (a generically dependent continuant, i.e., a conceptual pattern existing only in minds) and RealDistinction (a quality whose absence between the thing and its conatus is what the utterance asserts). A specific individual CogatusRationalDistinction captures the token rational distinction asserted here. The main open question is whether Conatus should be a class (applicable universally) rather than an individual, and how to formally encode identity-under-rational-distinction within OWL without triggering unsatisfiability.

entities.rationale: A quality that would represent duration as pertaining to an essence. Spinoza denies this quality applies to essences; we model the class so it can be asserted as empty or disjoint from EssentialExistenceQuality.

entities.label: Duration
entities.rationale: Duration as a measurable quality of existence in time. BFO treats temporal extension of a continuant as a quality-like feature; here we represent Spinozistic Duration as a Quality class so we can assert it is disjoint from EssentialExistenceQuality (essences have no duration).

entities.label: EssenceDurationExclusion
entities.rationale: The disposition of essences (qua essences) to be entirely non-durational — the internally grounded incapacity for duration to pertain to them. Modeled as a Disposition (internally grounded realizable) on the Substance/essence bearer.

relations.rationale: Duration is a Quality (BFO_0000019) as a measurable temporal property.

DurationPertainsToEssenceQuality would be a subtype of Duration, specifically the attribution of duration to an essence; Spinoza asserts nothing of this type exists (class is asserted empty / disjoint from EssentialExistenceQuality).

EssenceDurationExclusion is a Disposition — an internally grounded incapacity — on essences.
The exclusion of duration from essences is realized in processes of formal existence necessitation, where essences necessitate existence without temporal unfolding.

proposal.rationale_summary: Spinoza's claim 'No duration can pertain to the essences of things' (Ethics I, Def. 8 / II, Def. 5 context) asserts that duration — the indefinite continuation of existence in time — is categorically excluded from essences. In BFO terms, duration is a Quality (BFO_0000019) that inheres in existing things as they persist through time; essences, by contrast, are necessary and eternal, not temporally bounded. We therefore mint a Duration class (subclass of Quality), a DurationPertainsToEssenceQuality subclass representing the putative (but denied) attribution of duration to essences, and declare it disjoint from EssentialExistenceQuality. We also mint EssenceDurationExclusion as a Disposition (internally grounded incapacity for duration) that can be borne by substances/essences. The existing FormalExistenceNecessitationProcess is linked as the process in which this exclusion is realized, connecting the timeless necessitation of existence to the absence of duration.

proposal.utterance: There exist only substances and their modes in nature.

relations.rationale: Spinoza's claim that only substances and modes exist implies modes are ontologically grounded in substance; however this relation is already partially captured. The key new ontological claim is the exhaustiveness axiom below — no new entities are needed, but the subclass/disjointness structure should be noted.

open_questions: Spinoza's claim that 'only substances and their modes exist in nature' is an exhaustiveness claim — it asserts that Substance and Mode jointly cover all of nature, and nothing else exists. Should we represent this as a disjoint-union / covering axiom on a class like 'NaturalExistent' (which is partitioned into Substance and Mode)? Or should we assert it as an annotation/comment on the ontology itself?
Should we mint a class 'NaturalExistent' (subclass of BFO_0000004 or BFO_0000002) with disjoint subclasses Substance and Mode to formally capture the exhaustiveness claim?

Attributes are already in the ontology (working:Attribute, working:DivineAttribute). Spinoza sometimes treats attributes as a third category distinct from substance and mode. Does this statement implicitly exclude or subsume attributes, or are they considered aspects of substance rather than independent existents?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance 'there exist only substances and their modes in nature' is a partition/exhaustiveness claim about ontological categories. The classes working:Substance and working:Mode already exist in the ontology, so no new class or individual needs to be minted for the substantive terms. The philosophically significant new content is the claim that these two classes are jointly exhaustive of natural existence — nothing in nature falls outside Substance or Mode. This cannot be fully expressed by BFO subClassOf relations alone; it requires either a covering axiom (a class 'NaturalExistent' with disjoint subclasses Substance and Mode) or an OWL equivalent-class/union axiom. I have proposed the subClassOf relation from Mode to Substance only tentatively and flagged it as potentially incorrect (Spinoza's modes inhere in substance but are not a subclass of it in the identity sense). The main formal work needed is a covering/exhaustiveness axiom, which I flag in open_questions for user decision before committing.

proposal.utterance: Real distinctions hold between two substances that can each be conceived without the other.

entities.label: RealDistinction
entities.rationale: A real distinction is a relational quality holding between two substances, grounded in the nature of each substance. It is a specifically dependent continuant (Quality) that inheres in the pair-wise relationship of substances. We already have RelationalQuality in the ontology; RealDistinction is a subclass of it.

entities.label: MutualConceptualIndependence
entities.rationale: The condition that each of two substances can be conceived without the other is a mutual disposition grounded in each substance's nature — each bears a ConceptualIndependence disposition relative to the other. MutualConceptualIndependence captures the bilateral character of this conceivability condition.

relations.rationale: A real distinction is a species of RelationalQuality already defined in the ontology.
Mutual conceptual independence is a more specific form of conceptual independence applying symmetrically between two substances.

The definition supplied by the utterance asserts that a real distinction holds precisely when (and because) each substance bears mutual conceptual independence with respect to the other; thus RealDistinction is grounded in MutualConceptualIndependence, modeled as a subclass relationship capturing the definitional entailment.

open_questions: Spinoza's real distinction is between substances conceived through different attributes (e.g., Ethics 1D4). Should we link RealDistinction explicitly to DivineAttribute or Attribute, i.e., assert that two substances bear a RealDistinction if and only if they are conceived through different attributes?

Should RealDistinction be modeled as inhering in a pair of Substance individuals (a relational quality with two bearers), or is a simpler subclass-of-RelationalQuality sufficient for current purposes?

Spinoza ultimately concludes there is only one substance (God/Nature), which would make RealDistinction vacuously empty in extension. Should we assert that fact as a constraint here, or leave the class open?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance articulates Spinoza's definition of a real distinction (Ethics 1D4): two substances are really distinct when each can be conceived through itself without the other, i.e., when each bears ConceptualIndependence with respect to the other. I introduce two new classes: RealDistinction as a subclass of the existing RelationalQuality (it is a quality holding between substances), and MutualConceptualIndependence as a subclass of the existing ConceptualIndependence (it is the bilateral disposition grounding the real distinction). RealDistinction is then declared a subclass of MutualConceptualIndependence to encode the definitional claim that a real distinction just is the quality that obtains when mutual conceptual independence holds. No new individuals are required; the ontological content is purely class-level.

Mode-substance modal distinction is a species of modal distinction.
Inter-mode modal distinction is a species of modal distinction.

Instances of ModeSubstanceModalDistinction inhere in (are borne by) instances of Mode — the distinction is a quality of the mode vis-à-vis its substance. The utterance says a modal distinction exists 'between a mode and its substance' and 'between two modes of the same substance.' Should these be disjoint subclasses of ModalDistinction, and should we add an OWL disjointness axiom?

Should ModeSubstanceModalDistinction inhere in the mode (RO_0000052) or in the substance, or in both (as a relational quality with two bearers)? BFO relational qualities typically inhere in one bearer while being externally directed toward another — which should be primary here?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance introduces the concept of 'modal distinction' as a type of ontological distinction in Spinoza's metaphysics, asserting two specific cases: (1) between a mode and its substance, and (2) between two modes of the same substance. I mint a new class ModalDistinction as a subclass of the existing RelationalQuality (itself a BFO Quality, BFO_0000019), since a modal distinction is a relational property grounded in the natures of the entities involved rather than an independently-grounded disposition. Two subclasses are introduced — ModeSubstanceModalDistinction and InterModeModalDistinction — to capture the two specific relational cases. The existing Mode and Substance classes are reused as the relevant relata. I flag key open questions about whether Disposition would be a better BFO parent, whether complementary distinction types (real, rational) should be co-introduced, and the BFO treatment of relational qualities with two bearers.

entities.label: DistinctionOfReason
entities.rationale: A 'distinction of reason' (distinctio rationis) is a conceptual/intellectual distinction — a pattern of thought or conceptual content that can be entertained by different minds. It is not a real feature of the world (not a quality inhering in a bearer) but a conceptual artifact, best typed as a generically dependent continuant (information-like content). It is a class because the utterance asserts a kind of distinction, not a named individual.

entities.label: SubstanceAttributeDistinctionOfReason
entities.rationale: The specific distinction of reason that holds between Substance and its Attributes is a particular conceptual content asserted by the utterance. It is an individual instance of DistinctionOfReason, typed as a generically dependent continuant.

relations.rationale: The specific substance-attribute distinction of reason is an instance of the DistinctionOfReason class.

The distinction of reason between substance and its attributes is part of the conceptual content expressed by AttributeOfSubstance — it characterises the relationship as merely rational/conceptual rather than real.

The utterance implies that Substance and its Attributes are NOT really distinct (i.e., they are identical in re). Should we assert an explicit quality or disposition on God (the individual Substance) capturing that its attributes are not really distinct from it, or is this sufficiently captured via SubstanceAttributeDistinctionOfReason?

proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts that Substance and its Attributes are not really distinct but differ only 'by reason' (distinctio rationis) — a conceptual distinction made by an intellect, not a difference in the world. I mint a new class DistinctionOfReason as a generically dependent continuant (BFO_0000031) because it is a type of conceptual/informational content that can be entertained by multiple minds, consistent with Spinoza's view that this distinction is produced by the intellect abstracting rather than tracking genuine ontological cleavage. I then create an individual SubstanceAttributeDistinctionOfReason as the specific instance of this class asserted by the proposition. I relate it via BFO_0000050 (part of) to the existing class AttributeOfSubstance, capturing that this distinction is part of the conceptual apparatus governing Attributes. An open question remains about whether DistinctionOfReason should be typed as a quality inhering in an intellect (SDC), which is defensible under a more cognitivist reading; I flag this for the user's decision.

entities.label: BeingOfReason

The utterance asserts they are modes of thinking. Since Mode is already in the ontology as a subclass of BFO_0000020 (specifically dependent continuant), and thinking is the relevant attribute, BeingOfReason is best typed as a subclass of Mode that inheres in a thinking substance. This maps well to a specifically dependent continuant of a cognitive/mental kind.

entities.label: ModeOfThinking
entities.rationale: The utterance introduces 'modes of thinking' as a kind. Since ThinkingAttribute is already an individual in the ontology, a ModeOfThinking class — a subclass of Mode — captures the category of modes that fall under the attribute of Thought/Thinking. This serves as the parent of BeingOfReason per the assertion.

relations.rationale: ModeOfThinking is a subclass of Mode, since all modes of thinking are modes.
The utterance asserts 'beings of reason are modes of thinking', which is directly encoded as BeingOfReason rdfs:subClassOf ModeOfThinking.

open_questions: Should ModeOfThinking be further constrained to inhere specifically in a thinking substance (i.e., a substance bearing the ThinkingAttribute individual)? This would require a restriction axiom.

proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance 'beings of reason are modes of thinking' introduces two new classes: ModeOfThinking (modes falling under the attribute of Thought/Thinking, a subclass of the existing Mode class) and BeingOfReason (a subclass of ModeOfThinking, since beings of reason are asserted to be modes of thinking). Both are typed as BFO_0000020 (specifically dependent continuant) via inheritance from Mode. The existing individual ThinkingAttribute is relevant context but no new relation to it is added here beyond the class hierarchy, since the ontological commitment of the utterance is captured by the subclass chain. Open questions concern further restrictions, formal-reality contrasts, and disjointness axioms that would sharpen the Spinozistic distinction between beings of reason and formally existing modes.

proposal.rationale_summary: Spinoza's claim is that God's intellect, will, and power are not really distinct from one another — any distinction among them exists only in human conceptual thought, not in God's nature. Ontologically, this involves: (1) three dispositions (GodIntellect, GodWill, GodPower) inhering in God, which are in reality identical; (2) a quality (GodIntellectWillPowerRealIdentityQuality) inhering in God capturing their real non-distinction; and (3) a generically dependent continuant (GodIntellectWillPowerConceptualDistinction) that represents the merely conceptual distinction drawn by human thought. Existing individuals like AbsoluteFreedomOfWill and WillIsNotRealBeingQuality are related background commitments but do not fully capture this specific claim about the identity of the three divine attributes-cum-faculties. The three dispositions are modeled under BFO_0000016 (Disposition) since they represent internally grounded capacities of God, following the established pattern for similar divine properties in this ontology.

entities.label: Created
entities.rationale: The 'created' in Spinoza denotes a kind of thing (not a particular), namely whatever is not self-subsistent; it is best typed as a subclass of Independent continuant since it designates existing entities whose existence is not self-necessitated.

entities.label: EssenceConceivableWithoutExistenceQuality

This is a quality of the essence of such things, parallel to EssenceDoesNotInvolveExistence already in the ontology but framed specifically as a positive conceivability quality (essence is conceivable without existence being part of it). It is a subclass of the existing EssentialExistenceQuality cluster.

relations.rationale: Created things are independent continuants (they exist in their own right, though their existence is not necessitated by their essence).
This quality belongs to the cluster of qualities concerning the relationship between essence and existence.

The quality of having an essence conceivable without existence is a specialisation of the broader EssenceDoesNotInvolveExistence disposition/quality already in the ontology, making explicit the 'clear conception' aspect.

Every instance of Created bears an EssenceConceivableWithoutExistenceQuality — modelled via the bearer-of relation at the class level (universal restriction: Created subClassOf bearer_of some EssenceConceivableWithoutExistenceQuality).

proposal.utterance: No thing can determine the will except by God's power alone.

entities.label: WillDeterminationConstraint
entities.rationale: The claim that nothing can determine the will except through God's power is a constraint on causal determination of the will — an internally grounded disposition-like property expressing the exclusive causal dependency of will-determination on God's power.

entities.label: GodsPower
entities.rationale: God's power is a specific realizable property inhering in God — a disposition that is the sole sufficient ground for determining the will. It is an individual because it is the unique power of the individual God.

entities.label: WillDeterminationProcess
entities.rationale: The act of determining the will is an occurrent process. This class represents any such process of will-determination.

entities.label: ExclusiveCausalDependenceOnGod
entities.rationale: This individual represents the specific constraint asserted by the proposition: that will-determination is exclusively causally dependent on God's power alone — an instance of WillDeterminationConstraint inhering in the causal structure of the whole of nature / God.

relations.rationale: God's power inheres in God as its sole bearer, consistent with BFO's treatment of dispositions as specifically dependent continuants inhering in their bearer.
The exclusive causal dependence of will-determination on God is a specifically dependent property that inheres in God as the unique causal ground.
God's power is realized in any WillDeterminationProcess — the disposition is exercised precisely when will-determination occurs.
God participates in every WillDeterminationProcess as the sole sufficient determining agent, consistent with the proposition that only God's power can determine the will.
WillDeterminationConstraint is a subclass of Disposition (BFO_0000016), representing an internally grounded causal exclusivity property.

open_questions: Is 'the will' here Spinoza's will (voluntas) as a mode of thought, or a more general faculty-of-will concept? If the former, should WillDeterminationProcess be linked to the existing ThinkingAttribute or SoulModeOfThoughtQuality individuals?
Should GodsPower be modeled as identical to or as a subtype of CausaSui, given that Spinoza treats God's power as identical to God's essence and causal self-sufficiency?

proposal.rationale_summary: The proposition asserts that the will (as a mode or faculty) has no sufficient determining cause except God's power alone. Ontologically this commits us to: (1) a class of will-determination processes (WillDeterminationProcess), (2) God's power as a specific disposition inhering in God (GodsPower), (3) a constraint class (WillDeterminationConstraint) capturing the exclusive causal dependence of will-determination on God, and (4) an individual instance (ExclusiveCausalDependenceOnGod) asserting this constraint in the context of the current ontology. God's power is typed as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) since it is an internally grounded, realizable property of God; it is realized in will-determination processes. The existing individual AbsoluteFreedomOfWill is potentially related but is left unmerged pending clarification about whether this proposition denies absolute free will or grounds it in God's exclusive power. The existing DecreeNecessitationProcess and GodCausesAllThingsProcess individuals are contextually relevant but are not directly asserted to be identical to WillDeterminationProcess without further user confirmation.

entities.label: SubstanceGenerationIncapacity

Claim (1) is modeled as a disposition-class SubstanceGenerationIncapacity inhering in Substance, placed under the existing SubstanceProductionConstraint. Claim (2) is modeled as SubstanceCreationByGodDisposition inhering in God — the unique capacity to create substance — realized in SubstanceCreationProcess. proposal.utterance: Effects of imagination from corporeal causes cannot be omens of future things.

entities.label: ImaginationEffect
entities.rationale: An effect of imagination is a specifically dependent continuant inhering in a minded bearer — a modification of cognitive or perceptual state. Spinoza treats effects of imagination as modes of thought/extension, hence SDC.

entities.label: CorporealCause
entities.rationale: A corporeal cause is a role borne by a material body in a causal process. Roles are externally grounded and contingent, fitting Spinoza's treatment of finite modes causing one another.

entities.label: OmenStatusQuality
entities.rationale: Being an omen of a future thing is a putative quality (a sign-relation quality) attributed to an entity. Spinoza denies this quality can inhere in effects of imagination from corporeal causes.

entities.label: ImaginationEffectLacksOmenStatusQuality
entities.rationale: Spinoza's claim is that effects of imagination from corporeal causes bear a quality of lacking omen-status — i.e., the incapacity to function as signs of future things. This is a negation-quality parallel to ImperfectionQuality already in the ontology.

entities.label: ImaginationEffectFromCorporealCauseProcess
entities.rationale: The production of imagination effects by corporeal causes is a process — a causal happening — whose outputs are ImaginationEffect instances. Needed to ground the causal provenance of the effects.

relations.rationale: Effects of imagination are modes (specifically dependent continuants that are modifications of substance), consistent with Spinoza's framework already modeled as working:Mode.
Lacking omen-status (the inability to function as a sign of the future) is a specific form of imperfection or incapacity, connecting to the existing ImperfectionQuality class.
Process subclass axiom for the causal production process.
